children.translated_text: The <s>Āryā-saptaśatī</s> (Seven Hundred <s>Āryā</s> Verses) composed by <s>Govardhanācārya</s>
|| <s>Śrīḥ</s> (Auspiciousness) ||
The Opening Section (<s>Granthārambha-vrajyā</s>)

children.text: pāṇi-grahe pulakitaṃ vapur aiśaṃ bhūti-bhūṣitaṃ jayati |
children.translated_text: Victorious is the lordly body of <s>Śiva</s>, thrilling with horripilation at the wedding (<s>pāṇigraha</s>), adorned with sacred ash—
In which, even though reduced to ashes, <s>Manobhū</s> (Love) appears to have sprouted again.

children.text: mā vama saṃvṛṇu viṣam idam iti sātaṅkaṃ pitāmahenoktaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Don't spit it out! Cover up this poison!'—thus anxiously addressed by <s>Brahmā</s> (the Grandfather) in the morning,
Victorious is <s>Śambhu</s>, bashful, his lips darkened with collyrium [from kissing <s>Pārvatī</s>].
Victorious is the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), with poison as a necklace, at his beloved's feet—
As if seeking refuge from the crooked-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>), with a sword bound to his throat.
Victorious is the sidelong glance from the forehead-eye of the Moon-crested One, full of lashes, directed at the foremost of beloveds—

children.text: dhanuṣi smareṇa nihitaḥ sa-kaṇṭakaḥ ketakeṣur iva ||GAss_*4||
children.translated_text: Like a thorny <s>ketakī</s>-flower arrow placed on his bow by <s>Smara</s> (Love).
Victorious is this face of <s>Śambhu</s>, a lotus born from the mud of throat-poison,
With matted locks as filaments, <s>Gaṅgā</s> as nectar, and skull-garlands as seeds.
Not noticing that even his water-offering at twilight prayers was being drunk by the serpent-bracelet [on his arm],
His mind fixed on <s>Gaurī</s>'s face—victorious is <s>Śiva</s>, laughed at by <s>Vijayā</s> (Gaurī's friend).
Victorious is <s>Śambhu</s>'s water-offering, which slipped from his hand loosened by the thrill of seeing <s>Gaurī</s>'s face reflected [in the water],
Being replenished by the flood of his perspiration.
Victorious is <s>Śiva</s>, whose moon [on the crest] is made sweet-red by the lac-dye from the feet of his love-angered beloved,
Whose neck serves as a touchstone for the gold of her bracelets.
Victorious is <s>Hara</s>'s crescent moon—[appearing as] a full moon-nail, doubled anklets, and a chain of love—
At <s>Gaurī</s>'s toes, between her fingers, and at her ankles.
May the eye of the Lotus-eyed One (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), covered by <s>Śrī</s>'s (<s>Lakṣmī</s>'s) hand, delight you—
As if it had come, lotus-like, through the navel-aperture to behold her hips.
Victorious is the chest of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), dark, stained saffron-yellow by <s>Śrī</s>'s breast-<s>kuṅkuma</s>,
Like the dawn sky, which the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem adorns as its radiant [sun].
Victorious is the chest of <s>Madhubhid</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), reflecting his beloved's form along with the <s>Kaustubha</s>—

children.text: puruṣāyitam abhyasyati lakṣmīr yad vīkṣya mukuram iva ||GAss_*12||
children.translated_text: Seeing which as a mirror, <s>Lakṣmī</s> practices the <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top posture).
Victorious is the foot of <s>Murāri</s>, which during play has grasped <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s navel with its moving toes—

children.text: sa jayati yena kṛtā śrīr anurūpā padmanābhasya ||GAss_*13||
children.translated_text: By which <s>Śrī</s> was made befitting of [the name] <s>Padmanābha</s> ('Lotus-naveled').
May <s>Murāri</s>'s line of hair, with its upper portion attended by the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark,
Remove your distress, like the shadow of a lotus with a tall stalk rising from the navel.

children.text: ādāya sapta-tantrocitāṃ vipañcīm iva trayīṃ gāyan |
children.translated_text: Taking up the three <s>Vedas</s> like a <s>vīṇā</s> suited to seven strings, singing sweetly in a manner fitting for a horse-faced one,
Victorious is <s>Hari</s> in his <s>Hayagrīva</s> (horse-headed) form.

children.text: sa jayati mahābāho jala-nidhi-jaṭhare ciraṃ nimagnāpi |
children.translated_text: Victorious is the mighty-armed One, by whom the Earth, though long submerged in the ocean's belly,

children.text: yenāntrair iva saha phaṇi-gaṇair balād uddhṛtā dharaṇī ||GAss_*16||
children.translated_text: Was forcefully lifted up together with the hosts of serpents, as if with entrails.
I bow to <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the potter of the cosmic egg, in his serpent form,
On whose vast disc of hoods, the Earth bears the beauty of a potter's saucer.
The shin of <s>Caṇḍī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) is victorious when her beloved touches her feet with his head—
Like a victory-pillar of <s>Smara</s> (Love), whose conquest extends even to <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
By which even <s>Śambhu</s> appears like [a bee on] the long-stemmed navel-lotus—
Victorious is that face of the Mountain's Daughter (<s>Pārvatī</s>) in the <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top) posture.
Victorious are the breasts of the Himalaya's daughter, whose garment has been stolen by <s>Skanda</s> (<s>Bāhuleya</s>) anxious about <s>Gaṇeśa</s> (<s>Gajānana</s>) nestled in her lap,
[Now] held in the smiling <s>Hara</s>'s hands.
Though worthy of [her] embrace, cast away by a mere 'huṃ!' and fallen at her feet—

children.text: yasyāś candra-śikhaḥ smara-bhalla-nibho jayati sā caṇḍī ||GAss_*21||
children.translated_text: Victorious is that <s>Caṇḍī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), [to whom] the Moon-crested One [looks like] a crescent-arrow of <s>Smara</s>.
When the garland of choice is placed on the God (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), she who is full of wonder assumes the appearance of a <s>Kaiṭabhī</s> (a bee)—
Victorious is <s>Lakṣmī</s>, laughed at by gods and demons, with eyes averted in bashfulness.

children.text: tān asurān api harim api taṃ vande kapaṭa-kaiṭabhī-rūpam |
children.translated_text: I bow to those demons and to <s>Hari</s> himself, who assumed the deceitful form of <s>Kaiṭabhī</s> (the enchantress)—

children.text: yair yad bimbādhara-madhu-lubdhaiḥ pīyuṣam api mumuce ||GAss_*23||
children.translated_text: By whom—those who were greedy for the honey of [her] <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips—even the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) was let go.

Victorious is the amorous play of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), blinded by passion, in which the serpent (<s>Śeṣa</s>) is made a bed, <s>Garuḍa</s> is disregarded, <s>Brahmā</s> (Vidhi) is struck by her necklace,
And her breath is drunk by a hundred hoods.

children.text: smerān anena hariṇā yat spṛham ākāra-vedinākalitam |
children.translated_text: Victorious is the meditation of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) on the <s>Kaiṭabhī</s> form during the <s>puruṣāyita</s> posture—
In which the smiling <s>Hari</s>, though a perceiver of expressions, did not grasp [her] desire.
<s>Brahmā</s> (Vidhi) is victorious [sitting] in the navel-lotus, lulled to sleep by the sprinkling of <s>Śrī</s>'s cool sighs as she delights in amorous play with her beloved,
His snoring sounding like rhythmic hand-clapping [accompanying their sport].
One-tusked, born of two mothers, beyond the three <s>guṇas</s>, though four-armed yet five-handed,
Victory to you, praised by the six-faced (<s>Skanda</s>), O son of the eight-bodied (<s>Śiva</s>), whose rut smells of the seven-leaved tree!
Worship without pretense the elephant-faced <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, whose forehead-globes (<s>kumbha</s>) are a pair of auspicious water-vessels—
With bees clinging to sesame [offerings], trembling in the flowing waters of his rut-fluid.

children.text: yābhir anaṅgaḥ sāṅgī-kṛtaḥ striyo 'strī-kṛtāś ca tā yena |
children.translated_text: By whom (women) the Bodiless One (<s>Anaṅga</s>) was made whole, and those [women] were made to lose composure by him (<s>Kāma</s>)—
I bow to both <s>Kāminī</s> (<s>Rati</s>) and <s>Kāma</s>, who are inclined to the left-hand way.
Adorned with dense ornaments, flashing with garlands of varied colors,

children.text: śakrāyudham iva vakraṃ valmīka-bhuvaṃ kaviṃ naumi ||GAss_*30||
children.translated_text: I bow to the poet (<s>Vālmīki</s>), born of an anthill, curved like <s>Indra</s>'s bow (the rainbow).

children.text: vyāsa-girāṃ niryāsaṃ sāraṃ viśvasya bhārataṃ vande |
children.translated_text: I bow to the <s>Bhārata</s> (<s>Mahābhārata</s>), the extract of <s>Vyāsa</s>'s words, the essence of the universe—

children.text: bhūṣaṇayaiva sañjñāṃ yad aṅkitāṃ bhāratī vahati ||GAss_*31||
children.translated_text: By which <s>Bhāratī</s> (the goddess of speech) bears a name marked as her very ornament.
When the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, which elevates the <s>Kākutstha</s> lineage, exists, what need is there for anything else?

children.text: rohati kulyā gaṅgā-pūre kiṃ bahurase vahati ||GAss_*32||
children.translated_text: Does a canal grow when the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is in flood? What use if it carries much flavor?
Alas! <s>Vyāsa</s>'s fame was stolen by the fault of living too long!

children.text: kair nocyeta guṇāḍhyaḥ sa eva janmāntarāpannaḥ ||GAss_*33||
children.translated_text: By whom would <s>Guṇāḍhya</s> not be called the very same [<s>Vyāsa</s>] born in another life?
We bow to the poets of the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Bhārata</s>, and <s>Bṛhatkathā</s>—

children.text: trisrotā iva sarasā sarasvatī sphurati yair bhinnā ||GAss_*34||
children.translated_text: By whom <s>Sarasvatī</s> (the goddess of eloquence) flows divided, like the tri-streamed [<s>Gaṅgā</s>], full of <s>rasa</s>.
In the utterances of <s>Kālidāsa</s>, which are mostly like the sweet, soft, suggestive cooing from a coquette's throat—
Even the instruction in [poetic] convention delights, like amorous play.

children.text: bhavabhūteḥ sambandhād bhūdhara-bhūr eva bhāratī bhāti |
children.translated_text: Through association with <s>Bhavabhūti</s>, <s>Bhāratī</s> (Speech) shines as the domain of mountains—
For why else would a stone weep, except through the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (pathos) created by him?

children.text: jātā śikhaṇḍinī prāg yathā śikhaṇḍī tathāvagacchāmi |
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s> was previously born as <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> (a woman), so I understand—

children.text: prāgalbhyam adhikam āptuṃ vāṇī bāṇo babhūveti ||GAss_*37||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāṇī</s> (the goddess of speech) became <s>Bāṇa</s> (the poet) in order to attain greater boldness.

children.text: yaṃ gaṇayati guror anu yasyās te dharma-karma saṅkucitam |
children.translated_text: Whom [Sarasvatī] reckons second only to [my] guru, through whom her duties of <s>dharma</s> and <s>karma</s> are duly fulfilled—

children.text: kavim aham uśanasam iva taṃ tātaṃ nīlāmbaraṃ vande ||GAss_*38||
children.translated_text: I bow to that father <s>Nīlāmbara</s>, a poet like <s>Uśanas</s> (<s>Śukra</s>).

children.text: sakala-kalāḥ kalpayituṃ prabhuḥ prabandhasya kumuda-bandhoś ca |
children.translated_text: Capable of fashioning all arts in both poetic composition and [the blooming of] the water-lily's friend (the moon)—
One alone [suffices]: the <s>Sena</s>-dynasty king, ornament of his line; and the full-moon evening.

children.text: kāvyasyākṣara-maitrī-bhājo na ca karkaśā na ca grāmyāḥ |
children.translated_text: In poetry, those that partake of the friendship of syllables, that are neither harsh nor vulgar—

children.text: śabdā api puruṣā api sādhava evārtha-bodhāya ||GAss_*40||
children.translated_text: Words, like men, should be virtuous (<s>sādhu</s>) for the sake of conveying meaning.

children.text: vaṃśe ghuṇa iva na viśati doṣo rasa-bhāvite satāṃ manasi |
children.translated_text: A fault does not enter the mind of the virtuous, cultivated in <s>rasa</s>, just as a woodworm does not enter bamboo—

children.text: rasam api tu na pratīcchati bahu-doṣaḥ sannipātīva ||GAss_*41||
children.translated_text: But one who is full of faults does not receive <s>rasa</s> either, like one afflicted with a fever of all three humors.

children.text: viguṇo 'pi kāvya-bandhaḥ sādhūnām ānanaṃ gataḥ svadate |
children.translated_text: Even a flawed poetic composition, when it reaches the mouths of the virtuous, becomes delightful—
Even a mere breath, when echoed by fine bamboo [flutes], captivates the ear.

children.text: svayam api bhūri-cchidraś cāpalam api sarvatomukhaṃ tanvan |
children.translated_text: Though itself full of holes and spreading fickleness in all directions,
The sieve, betrayer of chaff, is appointed to the discrimination of faults.
Of a composition that does not reveal the meanings hidden within, devoid of lucidity—

children.text: sandarbhasya nadasya ca na rasaḥ prītyai rasa-jñānām ||GAss_*44||
children.translated_text: Neither its <s>rasa</s> nor [that of] a river delights the connoisseurs.
We regard as equal: poetry—inaccessible to the wicked, almost like nectar, beautifully arranged in golden words, filled with divine meaning—

children.text: surasārthamayaṃ kāvyaṃ triviṣṭapaṃ vā samaṃ vidmaḥ ||GAss_*45||
children.translated_text: And <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> (heaven) itself.
Sated by the refined rice of words, winnowed by the sieve-tongue of a good poet—

children.text: tṛpto dayitādharam api nādriyate kā sudhā dāsī ||GAss_*46||
children.translated_text: One does not even desire the beloved's lip; what is nectar (<s>sudhā</s>) but its handmaid?
A fine verse (<s>sūkti</s>), endowed with sublime <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), delights—
Even with unadorned words and stumbling placement, like an <s>abhisārikā</s> (woman going to meet her lover).

children.text: adhvani pada-graha-paraṃ madayati hṛdayaṃ na vā na vā śravaṇam |
children.translated_text: Poetry in an assembly of connoisseurs, an anklet during the time of love-play—
Does it not intoxicate the heart devoted to grasping [its] steps on the path? Does it not [delight] the ear?
Sweet verses belong only to one who has tasted the nectar of the beloved's lips—
A cuckoo that has not tasted the mango-bud does not raise its melodious song.
Emotion (<s>bhāva</s>) that is threaded by a maiden's sidelong glance, commented upon by the three-fold [glance] of a wanton woman—
Young poets study [it] as explained by the go-between.
The <s>āryā</s> verses of <s>Govardhana</s>—moving in smooth meters of song, seeking out the hearts of the virtuous, full of <s>rasa</s>—
Are the clear secret teachings (<s>upaniṣads</s>) of Love that is without a second.
Speech (<s>Vāṇī</s>), whose <s>rasa</s> is suited to <s>Prākṛta</s> (the vernacular), has been brought to Sanskrit by sheer force—
Like the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (the river <s>Yamunā</s>), whose waters naturally flow downward, [carried] to the heavens.
This <s>Āryā-saptaśatī</s>, if disregarded by those of bold minds—

children.text: dūtī-rahitā iva te na kāminī-manasi niviśante ||GAss_*53||
children.translated_text: They do not enter a beloved woman's heart, like one without a go-between.
Speech, though pure, gives delight when moist [with <s>rasa</s>] and stripped of garments by the ways of love, like a beloved—

children.text: arasā sālaṅkṛtir api na rocate śālabhañjīva ||GAss_*54||
children.translated_text: When tasteless, even if ornamented, it does not please, like a wooden doll (<s>śālabhañjī</s>).
Thus ends the Opening Section (<s>Granthārambha-vrajyā</s>).
The A-section (<s>Akāra-vrajyā</s>)
'May the wives of travelers live only until the appointed day of return—be gracious!
Cover your breasts, those impassable mountain-barriers on the road, O row of water-stations!'
Exceedingly affectionate, virtuous in conduct, clever in service, agreeable to the mind—
She became a modest housewife the very moment her co-wife's breasts developed.
O <s>Kāverī</s>, babbling with wicked waves that uproot the <s>Nicula</s> trees at your banks—
Before long you will become nothing but mud, the leavings of cranes!

children.text: ayi vividha-vacana-racane dadāsi candraṃ kare samānīya |
children.translated_text: O go-between, skilled in composing various messages, you give [me] the moon brought to hand—

children.text: vyasana-divaseṣu dūti kva punas tvaṃ darśanīyāsi ||GAss_4||
children.translated_text: But on days of calamity, where then are you to be seen?

children.text: astu mlānir loko lāñchanam apadiśatu hīyatām ojaḥ |
children.translated_text: Let there be wilting, let the world point out the blemish, let vigor diminish—

children.text: tad api na muñcati sa tvāṃ vasudhā-chāyām iva sudhāṃśuḥ ||GAss_5||
children.translated_text: Even so, he does not abandon you, just as the moon [does not abandon] the shadow of the earth.
Spreading excessive fickleness, penetrating deep inside, thoroughly hard—

children.text: mukharayasi svayam etāṃ sad-vṛttāṃ śaṅkur iva ghaṇṭām ||GAss_6||
children.translated_text: You yourself make this well-rounded one resound, like a bell-clapper.
The surge of desire in the limbs of the young wagtail pair ages only in the body—
Not so their love-play on the surface of the earth, which has inexhaustible treasures concealed within.
Assuming blindness at the time of the blind, deafness at the time of the deaf—
<s>Prajāpati</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), the devoted [servant] of <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Keśava</s>, dwells in the navel.

children.text: ayi koṣa-kāra kuruṣe vanecarāṇāṃ puro guṇodgāram |
children.translated_text: O silkworm, you extol [your] merits before the forest-dwellers—

children.text: yan na vidārya vicārita-jaṭharas tvaṃ sa khalu te lābhaḥ ||GAss_9||
children.translated_text: That you were not ripped open to have your belly examined—that indeed is your profit.
Heedless of greatness, disregarding elders, craving the needless, hostile to the nursing babe—
Her passion for you is regardless of life itself.

children.text: aparādhād adhikaṃ māṃ vyathayati tava kapaṭa-vacana-racaneyam |
children.translated_text: This fabrication of your deceitful words pains me more than [your actual] offense—
A sword-blow does not hurt as much as the pain of a needle-prick.

children.text: asatī-locana-mukure kim api pratiphalati yan manovarti |
children.translated_text: Whatever is in the mind is reflected in the mirror of a wanton woman's eyes—

children.text: sārasvatam api cakṣuḥ satimiram iva tan na lakṣayati ||GAss_12||
children.translated_text: But a learned eye, as if afflicted with cataract, does not perceive it.

children.text: anya-mukhe durvādo yaḥ priya-vadane sa eva parihāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: What is slander in another's mouth is jest in the beloved's—
What is smoke when born from other fuel is incense when born from <s>aguru</s> (aloewood).
O beautiful one, wandering about with trembling curiosity, following the trail of fragrance—

children.text: tvayi mohāya varākī patitā madhupīva viṣa-kusume ||GAss_14||
children.translated_text: the poor girl has fallen for you to her delusion, like a bee upon a poisonous flower. [GAss 14]
O naive one, merely at the suspicion of a rutting elephant's scent, [real] elephants are crushed—

children.text: upabhuñjate kareṇūḥ kevalam iha mat-kuṇāḥ kariṇaḥ ||GAss_15||
children.translated_text: only bedbugs here enjoy the female elephants acting as bull elephants! [GAss 15]
The bride, her body dwarfed by excessive modesty, does not cross the threshold of the house—
but her boldness? Only the safflower garden knows that! [GAss 16]

children.text: antar-gatair guṇaiḥ kiṃ dvitrā api yatra sākṣiṇo viralāḥ |
children.translated_text: What use are inner virtues, where even two or three witnesses are rare?

children.text: sa guṇo gīter yad asau vanecaraṃ hariṇam api harati ||GAss_17||
children.translated_text: That is the virtue of song: that it captivates even the wild deer of the forest. [GAss 17]

children.text: alulita-sakala-vibhūṣāṃ prātar bālāṃ vilokya muditaṃ prāk |
children.translated_text: Seeing the young woman in the morning with all her ornaments undisturbed, the co-wives were first delighted;

children.text: priya-śirasi vīkṣya yāvakam atha niḥśvasitaṃ sapatnībhiḥ ||GAss_18||
children.translated_text: then, seeing the lac-dye on her beloved's head, they sighed. [GAss 18]
O bashful one, your body exhausted from the intense lovemaking of deep midnight, sleeping blissfully—
open the petals of your lotus-eyes: it is a beautiful dawn for you! [GAss 19]
With face not kissed, with breasts not pressed, with hips and thighs kept far apart—
only with her arms, after a hundred oaths, was I embraced by her. [GAss 20]
This gaze of yours, O slender one, excessively honored by the pupils, capable of transgressing the ears—

children.text: jina-siddhānta-sthitir iva sa-vāsanā kaṃ na mohayati ||GAss_21||
children.translated_text: like the doctrine of the <s>Jinas</s>, imbued with passion (<s>vāsanā</s>), whom does it not delude? [GAss 21]

children.text: alam aviṣaya-bhaya-lajjā-vañcitam ātmānam iyam iyat samayam |
children.translated_text: Enough! This girl, cheated by inexperience, fear, and modesty, grieves for herself all this while,
now acquainted with the newly-learned virtues of her beloved; she does not call out to her bed-companions. [GAss 22]
Seized in body by the fierce separation born of her passion for you,
like <s>Gaurī</s> by the enemy of the three cities (<s>Tripura-ripu</s>, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>), the beautiful woman seems to have only half remaining. [GAss 23]
When one's beloved is inclined toward another, like those who have placed their hopes in a river flowing the wrong way,

children.text: tad-gatim icchantyaḥ sakhi bhavanti viphala-śramāḥ hāsyāḥ ||GAss_24||
children.translated_text: those who desire that course, O friend, become objects of ridicule with efforts all in vain. [GAss 24]

children.text: adhikaḥ sarvebhyo yaḥ priyaḥ priyebhyo hṛdi sthitaḥ satatam |
children.translated_text: He who is dearest of all dear ones, constantly dwelling in the heart—

children.text: sa luṭhati virahe jīvaḥ kaṇṭhe'syās tvam iva sambhoge ||GAss_25||
children.translated_text: that life-breath rolls about in separation at her throat, just as you do in lovemaking. [GAss 25]

children.text: anayana-pathe priye na vyathā yathā dṛśya eva duṣprāpe |
children.translated_text: When the beloved is beyond the reach of the eyes, the pain is not as great as when he is visible yet unattainable—

children.text: mlānaiva kevalaṃ niśi tapana-śilā vāsare jvalati ||GAss_26||
children.translated_text: the sun-stone merely withers at night; it burns by day. [GAss 26]
Imperceptible even to a friend, delighting the beloved merely by his presence—

children.text: rahasi vyapadeśād ayam arthaḥ ivārājake bhogyaḥ ||GAss_27||
children.translated_text: this secret affair, through pretexts of privacy, is enjoyable like wealth in a lawless land. [GAss 27]

children.text: aśrauṣīr aparādhān mama tathyaṃ kathaya man-mukhaṃ vīkṣya |
children.translated_text: 'You have heard of my offenses—tell the truth, looking at my face!'

children.text: abhidhīyate na kiṃ yadi na māna-caurānanaḥ kitavaḥ ||GAss_28||
children.translated_text: 'Why is nothing said? Because the gambler does not have the face of one who steals pride?' [GAss 28]

children.text: anyonyam anu srotasam anyad athānyat taṭāt taṭaṃ bhajatoḥ |
children.translated_text: Following each other along the stream, moving from one bank to another,
even when the sun has risen, the young couple's <s>Māgha</s>-bath is not completed. [GAss 29]
O mango-vine, your body bowed with the weight of fruit, your fragrance spreading in all directions—
yet marked by the water-pot of an outcaste, even when you have borne fruit, you are indeed fruitless! [GAss 30]

children.text: añjalir akāri lokair mlānim anāptaiva rañjitā jagatī |
children.translated_text: The world makes <s>añjali</s> (salutation); though not yet fading, the world is colored—

children.text: sandhyāyā iva vasatiḥ svalpāpi sakhe sukhāyaiva ||GAss_31||
children.translated_text: like the dwelling of twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>), even a brief stay, O friend, is only for happiness. [GAss 31]

children.text: agṛhītānunayāṃ mām upekṣya sakhyo gatā bataikāham |
children.translated_text: 'Having neglected me whose entreaties were not accepted, my friends have gone—I am alone!'

children.text: prasabhaṃ karoṣi mayi cet tvad upari vapur adya mokṣyāmi ||GAss_32||
children.translated_text: 'If you force yourself upon me, I shall hurl my body down from above you today!' [GAss 32]

children.text: asthira-rāgaḥ kitavo mānī capalo vidūṣakas tvam asi |
children.translated_text: 'You are fickle in passion, a cheat, proud, flighty—you are a buffoon!'

children.text: mama sakhyāḥ patasi kare paśyāmi yathā ṛjur bhavasi ||GAss_33||
children.translated_text: 'You fall into my friend's hand—let me see how you become honest!' [GAss 33]
O merciless one, her gaze—shown full of tears, of a timid heart, without interruption—

children.text: tvām anu dhāvati vimukhaṃ gaṅgeva bhagīrathaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ ||GAss_34||
children.translated_text: chases after you as you turn away, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> after <s>Bhagīratha</s>. [GAss 34]
By her whose passion is blocked by inner turbidity, like a wine-vessel [whose flow is obstructed]—

children.text: apy unmukhasya vihitā varavarṇini na tvayā tṛptiḥ ||GAss_35||
children.translated_text: O woman of excellent complexion, even though I was eager, no satisfaction was given by you. [GAss 35]
O honest one! Between the <s>sarala</s> (pine) tree and the temple-streaks of an elephant delighted with rut—
the mutual exchange of intoxicating fragrances speaks of their rubbing together. [GAss 36]
Her gaze, emerging through a torn strip of cloth parted by her fingernails,
tastes, freed from impurity through the parted cloth, like a stream of nectar. [GAss 37]
When she departs for her husband's house, the mother makes the path slippery with tears,

children.text: guṇa-garvitā punar asau hasati śanaiḥ śuṣka-rudita-mukhī ||GAss_38||
children.translated_text: while she, proud of her virtues, smiles softly with a face feigning weeping. [GAss 38]

children.text: aṅke niveśya kūṇita-dṛśaḥ śanair akaruṇeti śaṃsantyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Placing her upon my lap, her eyes half-closed, as she softly declares 'merciless!'—
when shall I untie her hair-braid with nails anointed with fragrant oil? [GAss 39]
Enough, O you who are beautiful without ornaments! Jewelry is a subject of mockery for other women;
you make it so, like a flower on a barren vine among flowering trees. [GAss 40]

children.text: abudhā ajaṅgamā api kayāpi gatyā paraṃ padam avāptāḥ |
children.translated_text: Unintelligent, immobile—yet they have attained the highest position through some means;

children.text: mantriṇa iti kīrtyante naya-bala-guṭikā iva janena ||GAss_41||
children.translated_text: they are called 'ministers' (<s>mantrin</s>) by people, like pills of political power. [GAss 41]
Our friend, with a creeper of excessive modesty-born coolness, has gentle power in the world;
her lover, scorched by even a moment's contrariness, knows her power. [GAss 42]

children.text: anyāsv api gṛhiṇīti dhyāyann abhilaṣitam āpnoti |
children.translated_text: Even while thinking of other women as 'wife,' one obtains what is desired—
just as one sees stone images as deities. [GAss 43]
O boy, without having attained a lowly state, you are not a worthy vessel

children.text: asyāḥ premṇaḥ pātraṃ na bhavasi sarito rasasyeva ||GAss_44||
children.translated_text: for her love, which is deep and sweet on all sides—like a river's current. [GAss 44]

children.text: adhivāsanam ādheyaṃ guṇa-mārgam apekṣate na ca grathanām |
children.translated_text: A garland to be worn looks to the path of virtues, not to its stringing;
the <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine) bud, by its very nature, adorns the crown of young men. [GAss 45]
O fortunate one, the garland placed with your own hand, all her suffering removed—
she wears it as a medicine for the fever of awaiting her turn on the conjugal bed. [GAss 46]

children.text: agaṇita-guṇena sundara kṛtvā cāritram apy udāsīnam |
children.translated_text: O handsome one, by you whose virtues are uncounted, though your conduct is made indifferent,
she has been made one with no other recourse—like a boat caught in a whirlpool. [GAss 47]
By the loving woman who placed back the upper garment upon the one returning,
even though wearing but a single cloth, your splendor exceeds that of all young men. [GAss 48]

children.text: ardhaḥ prāṇity eko mṛta itaro me vidhuntudasyeva |
children.translated_text: One half lives, the other is dead—as with the moon at half-phase (<s>Vidhuntudasya</s>);
for one whose half was embraced on the road by the meeting with the beloved, like nectar. [GAss 49]
Though ignored under the pretext of sleep by the cruel beloved, her greatness—
I, the restless one, was made aware [of it] by the bed, moistened to a limited extent by tears. [GAss 50]
O traveler, merely because of the similarity in the word, having tasted sugar—
the small cutting of the tongue is before you; the great public ridicule is immense! [GAss 51]
Even though her pride is being slain by the unconquerable hostile party of fresh youth,
the fortunate wife bears the arrogance of a favored one, because her son is dear to his father. [GAss 52]

children.text: apamānitam iva samprati guruṇā grīṣmeṇa durbalaṃ śaityam |
children.translated_text: The coolness, now humiliated as it were by the stern summer, weakened—
enters the water held in the pot-like breasts of young women eager to bathe. [GAss 53]

children.text: alasayati gātram akhilaṃ kleśaṃ mocayati locanaṃ harati |
children.translated_text: It makes the whole body languid, releases from toil, captivates the eyes—

children.text: svāpa iva preyān mama moktuṃ na dadāti śayanīyam ||GAss_54||
children.translated_text: like sleep, my beloved does not let me leave the bed. [GAss 54]
Hair held by a hand hanging from the shoulder, with white nail-marks still moist from bathing,

children.text: dhautādhara-nayanaṃ vapur astram anaṅgasya tava niśitam ||GAss_55||
children.translated_text: with washed lips and eyes—your body is the sharpened weapon of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Love-god). [GAss 55]

children.text: avinihitaṃ vinihitam iva yuvasu svaccheṣu vāra-vāma-dṛśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The courtesans, with glances casually amorous, seemingly not intentional yet intentional toward young men who are transparent—
display their hearts, as [one displays] a face in mirror-reflections. [GAss 56]

children.text: atilajjayā tvayaiva prakaṭaḥ preyān akāri nibhṛto 'pi |
children.translated_text: Through your excessive shyness, you yourself made public your secretly hidden beloved—
just as a victory-banner, spreading over the palace roof, [reveals what is within]. [GAss 57]
Cows, by the virtue of being roped to each other, with many hoof-steps,

children.text: khalam api tudanti meḍhī-bhūtaṃ madhya-stham ālambya ||GAss_58||
children.translated_text: kick even the threshing-floor, clinging to the one who has become the central post. [GAss 58]

children.text: ananugraheṇa na tathā vyathayati kaṭu-kūjitair yathā piśunaḥ |
children.translated_text: A slanderer does not cause as much pain by his unkindness as by his harsh whispering;

children.text: rudhirādānād adhikaṃ dunoti karṇe kvaṇan maśakaḥ ||GAss_59||
children.translated_text: a mosquito, more than by drawing blood, torments by its buzzing in the ear. [GAss 59]

children.text: agre laghimā paścān mahatāpi pidhīyate na hi mahimnā |
children.translated_text: First comes smallness of stature; afterward, it cannot be concealed even by the greatest greatness;
the knowers of the ten <s>avatāras</s> call 'the dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>)' <s>Trivikrama</s> (the three-strider). [GAss 60]

children.text: aṅke stanandhayas tava caraṇe paricārikā priyaḥ pṛṣṭhe |
children.translated_text: Your sucklings at your breast, the maid at your feet, your husband at your back—

children.text: asti kim u labhyam adhikaṃ gṛhiṇi yadā śaṅkase bālām ||GAss_61||
children.translated_text: O wife, is there anything more to be obtained? Yet you suspect a young girl! [GAss 61]

children.text: adhara udastaḥ kūjitam āmīlitam akṣi lolito mauliḥ |
children.translated_text: The lip is raised, the cooing [stifled], the eye half-closed, the head turned—
even without touch, the young couple seems to have obtained the pleasure of a kiss. [GAss 62]
This arm, thrust hastily through the lattice-opening into the house,
thrilled by the touch of the beloved, does not come back by that same path. [GAss 63]
Your hip, placed in the midst of cloth, exceedingly restless and not light—

children.text: cātaka iva navam abhraṃ nirīkṣamāṇo na tṛpyāmi ||GAss_64||
children.translated_text: like a <s>cātaka</s> bird gazing at a fresh cloud, I look and am not satisfied. [GAss 64]
This [creature], burdened by the earth weighted down by the elephantine mass of darkness,
with face [raised] toward the lofty eastern mountain, the tortoise spews forth the tears of twilight. [GAss 65]

children.text: antarbhūto nivasati jaḍe jaḍaḥ śiśira-mahasi hariṇa iva |
children.translated_text: Dwelling within a dull [medium], the dull one [stays] within the cold light like a hare in the moon;

children.text: ajaḍe śaśīva tapane sa tu praviṣṭo 'pi niḥsarati ||GAss_66||
children.translated_text: but the one [who enters] a brilliant one, like the moon in the sun—even though he has entered, he emerges. [GAss 66]
Disregarding the censure of all people, trembling with the joy of your hand's touch,
the poor girl prepares the bed of fever for you who are coming. [GAss 67]
Behold these two, born of the same bamboo, partaking of fullness and hollowness—

children.text: jyā-kārmukayoḥ kaścid guṇa-bhūtaḥ kaścid api bhartā ||GAss_68||
children.translated_text: of the bowstring and the bow, one is the string of virtue (<s>guṇa</s>), and the other is the bearer (<s>bhartṛ</s>/husband). [GAss 68]
The young girl, exhausted from fresh love-play, gradually produces drops of perspiration—

children.text: jyām arpayituṃ namitā kusumāstra-dhanur lateva madhu ||GAss_69||
children.translated_text: like a vine of the flower-arrowed one's (<s>Kusumāstra</s>, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>) bow, bent to string the bowstring with honey. [GAss 69]

children.text: asatī kulajā dhīrā prauḍhā prativeśinī yad āsaktim |
children.translated_text: When a faithless woman, well-born, steadfast, mature, a neighbor, becomes passionately attached,

children.text: kurute sarasā ca tadā brahmānandaṃ tṛṇaṃ manye ||GAss_70||
children.translated_text: and she is witty too—then I consider the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> to be a mere straw. [GAss 70]

children.text: avirala-patitāśru vapuḥ pāṇḍu snigdhaṃ tavopanītam idam |
children.translated_text: Profusely tear-stained, pale, tender—this body of yours that has been brought [before me]

children.text: śata-dhautam ājyam iva me smara-śara-dāha-vyathāṃ harati ||GAss_71||
children.translated_text: removes my pain of being burned by <s>Smara's</s> (Love-god's) arrows, like ghee washed a hundred times. [GAss 71]
The rice-field, beautiful within with strings of <s>guñjā</s> berries fallen inside, gleams—
as if with its heart torn open from grief at the loss of its own cowherd-girl's modesty. [GAss 72]

children.text: amunā hatam idam idam iti rudatī prativeśine'ṅgam aṅgam iyam |
children.translated_text: 'This was struck here by him, and this here'—weeping, [showing] limb by limb to the neighbor,
this wife, her modesty shattered under the pretext of anger, displays [her body] before her husband. [GAss 73]
Thus ends the section beginning with the letter 'a,' accompanied by the <s>vibhāva</s> commentary.
The section beginning with the letter 'ā.'

children.text: āntaram api bahiri va hi vyañjayituṃ rasam aśeṣataḥ satatam |
children.translated_text: Always able to express the inner <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) fully, as if it were external—
the unchaste woman, the good poet's verse, and a glass vessel—these three know [how to do] that. [GAss 74]

children.text: āloka eva vimukhī kvacid api divase na dakṣiṇā bhavasi |
children.translated_text: You turn away at the very sight; never during the day are you gracious—

children.text: chāyeva tad api tāpaṃ tvam eva me harasi mānavati ||GAss_75||
children.translated_text: yet like a shadow, even so, you alone remove my burning, O proud one! [GAss 75]

children.text: ājñā kākur yācñā-kṣepo hasitaṃ ca śuṣka-ruditaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Commands, coaxing tones, requests, reproaches, laughter, and feigned weeping—

children.text: iti nidhuvana-pāṇḍityaṃ dhyāyaṃs tasyā na tṛpyāmi ||GAss_76||
children.translated_text: meditating on her expertise in lovemaking, I am never satisfied. [GAss 76]

children.text: ājñāpayiṣyasi padaṃ dāsyasi dayitasya śirasi kiṃ tvarase |
children.translated_text: 'You will command! You will place your foot upon your beloved's head! Why do you hurry?'

children.text: asamaya-mānini mugdhe mā kuru bhagnāṅkuraṃ prema ||GAss_77||
children.translated_text: 'O naive one, sulking at the wrong time—do not make love a plant with broken sprouts!' [GAss 77]
Having encountered defeat by her in a dice game where the stake was a game of love of her choosing—
'Remove the dice!'—with feigned anger, the friends were made to leave. [GAss 78]

children.text: ādaraṇīya-guṇā sakhi mahatā nihitāsi tena śirasi tvam |
children.translated_text: O friend, possessing venerable virtues, you have been placed on his head by that great man;
this fault of your fickleness—like a pennant on a palace—is that you flutter. [GAss 79]

children.text: ārdram api stana-jaghanān nirasya sutanu tvayaitad unmuktam |
children.translated_text: Even though moist from breasts and hips, this cloth you have taken off, O slender one—

children.text: kha-stham avāptum iva tvāṃ tapanāṃśūn aṃśukaṃ pibati ||GAss_80||
children.translated_text: drinks in the sun's rays as if to reach you, standing in the sky. [GAss 80]

children.text: āropitā śilāyām aśmeva tvaṃ bhaveti mantreṇa |
children.translated_text: You have been mounted upon a stone—like a stone, 'may you become so' is the <s>mantra</s>;
Even drowning in the calamity of marriage, upon seeing the face of her lover, she simply smiled. [GAss 81]

children.text: āyāti yāti khedaṃ karoti madhu harati madhukarīvānyā |
children.translated_text: Another woman comes, goes, causes vexation, and steals honey like a female bee;

children.text: adhidevatā tvam eva śrīr iva kamalasya mama manasaḥ ||GAss_82||
children.translated_text: But you alone are the presiding deity — like <s>Śrī</s> of the lotus, of my mind. [GAss 82]

children.text: āsādya dakṣiṇāṃ diśam avilambaṃ tyajati cottarāṃ taraṇiḥ |
children.translated_text: The sun, upon reaching the southern direction, immediately abandons the northern;

children.text: puruṣaṃ haranti kāntāḥ prāyeṇa hi dakṣiṇā eva ||GAss_83||
children.translated_text: Charming women generally attract men indeed when they are skilled (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). [GAss 83]
Some women relieve the burning of poison through application, drinking, and anointing;
But a certain one, a medicinal creeper merely standing in the assembly, gives life. [GAss 84]
Do you remember her in the <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top position), with hair swaying on the swing, with the jingling of the rows of moving waist-bells —
like a staff bearing the fan-insignia of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love)? [GAss 85]

children.text: ākṣipasi karṇam akṣṇā balir api baddhas tvayā tridhā madhye |
children.translated_text: You captivate the ear with your glance; even <s>Bali</s> was bound by you three times at the waist —
thus, O slender one, having conquered all in generosity, are you ashamed of giving your body? [GAss 86]
The slender one, with her eager curiosity for the play of pulling, stepping over, and grasping hair,

children.text: strīṇāṃ patir api gurur iti dharmaṃ na śrāvitā sutanuḥ ||GAss_87||
children.translated_text: has not informed her husband that 'a husband is a woman's lord' — this is <s>dharma</s>. [GAss 87]
I was robbed by him who came without looking back, who sought me like a cowrie shell —

children.text: muṣitāsmi tena jaghanāṃ-śukam api voḍhuṃ naśaktena ||GAss_88||
children.translated_text: by one who was unable to bear even the brightness of my hips. [GAss 88]
With one leg bent, the upper thigh slightly covered, half the thigh concealed,
with the navel visible on her abdomen as her breath rises — this is the bed of the slender one. [GAss 89]

children.text: ādāya dhanam analpaṃ dadānayā subhaga tāvakaṃ vāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, the naive wife of the washerman, having taken no small sum and giving your garments,

children.text: mugdhā rajaka-gṛhiṇyā kṛtā dinaiḥ katipayair niḥsvā ||GAss_90||
children.translated_text: was made destitute within a few days. [GAss 90]

children.text: āstāṃ varam avakeśī mā doha-damasya racaya pūga-taroḥ |
children.translated_text: Never mind being disheveled — do not fashion a braid of the betel-palm tree, O milking-and-taming one;

children.text: etasmāt phalitād api kevalam udvegam adhigaccha ||GAss_91||
children.translated_text: from this one, even when it bears fruit, you will obtain only distress. [GAss 91]

children.text: ārabdham abdhi-mathanaṃ svahastayitvā dvi-jihvam amarair yat |
children.translated_text: The churning of the ocean was undertaken by the gods, using the two-tongued (serpent) as their tool;

children.text: ucitas tat-pariṇāmo viṣamaṃ viṣam eva yaj jātam ||GAss_92||
children.translated_text: that outcome was fitting — what was produced was indeed dangerous poison. [GAss 92]
With curls drawn aside, breath making her breasts quiver, one arm placed on the bed,
I remember the resting place of her whose body was helpless with passion — her garment loosened. [GAss 93]
This mango sprout, O slender one, with its reddish-dark luster, emerged from the seed;
like rising from the hollow shell of a young tortoise, it sprouts upward from the top and quivers. [GAss 94]
The glance of my beloved — slightly curved at the tip, richly layered, long, yielding deep savor —

children.text: karṣati mano madīyaṃ hrada-mīnaṃ baḍiśa-rajjur iva ||GAss_95||
children.translated_text: draws my mind like a fishing line draws a fish from a pool. [GAss 95]

children.text: ālapa yathā yathecchasi yuktaṃ tava kitava kim apavārayasi |
children.translated_text: Speak as you please — O gambler, what fitting thing are you concealing?
That friend of yours, the very brand-mark of womankind, is wretched in her very life, O handsome one. [GAss 96]

children.text: āsvādito 'si mohād bata viditā vadana-mādhurī bhavataḥ |
children.translated_text: Alas, you were tasted out of delusion! Now the sweetness of your mouth is known —
a razor smeared with honey — do you know it is meant to cut the tongue? [GAss 97]
O beautiful one, by what fortunate one was your arm — a lotus stalk, naturally tender, with its bracelet broken by pulling —

children.text: dhanyena bhuja-mṛṇālaṃ grāhyaṃ madanasya rājyam iva ||GAss_98||
children.translated_text: to be grasped, as one grasps the kingdom of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love)? [GAss 98]
Climbing high, disregarding fierce hardships, displaying herself —

children.text: vāta-pratīcchana-paṭī vahitram iva harasi māṃ sutanu ||GAss_99||
children.translated_text: O slender one, you carry me away like a vessel propelled by its wind-catching sail. [GAss 99]
Exertion and cruelty to others are your essence, O hunter's dog!
Removing you, this deer should now be shared by others. [GAss 100]

children.text: ānayati pathika-taruṇaṃ hariṇa iha prāpayann ivātmānam |
children.translated_text: The gentle-toned cuckoo, trembling with the swaying of quick turns, brings a young traveler here
as if presenting himself — though departing, still restless with soft melodies. [GAss 101]

children.text: āsīd eva yad ārdraḥ kim api tadā kim ayam āhato 'py āha |
children.translated_text: When he was moist, what was it he said then? And now, though struck, what does he say?

children.text: niṣṭhura-bhāvād adhunā kaṭūni sakhi raṭati paṭaha iva ||GAss_102||
children.translated_text: O friend, due to his hard nature now, he rattles harshly like a drum. [GAss 102]

children.text: ājñā-karaś ca tāḍana-paribhava-sahanaś ca satyam aham asyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Indeed, I obey her commands and endure her beatings and insults;

children.text: na tu śīla-śītaleyaṃ priyetarad vaktum api veda ||GAss_103||
children.translated_text: but she — cool in her virtue — does not even know how to say anything other than 'beloved.' [GAss 103]
The cowherd woman, her arm-creepers weary from placing the churning rod in the milk-pot,
not having obtained the <s>Pārijāta</s> flower, places the blame on fate. [GAss 104]

children.text: āstāṃ mānaḥ kathanaṃ sakhīṣu vā mayi nivedya-durvinaye |
children.translated_text: Let her pride be — whether speaking to friends or to me, whose poor conduct is to be reported —
that slender one, with her pride in love's qualities slackened, is herself ashamed. [GAss 105]
With whirlpools pale as white gourd giving the beauty of libation,
with waters made vocal, the flavorful river sings an auspicious song of the beloved's union. [GAss 106]
Thus ends the ā-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The i-kāra-vrajyā

children.text: iyam udgatiṃ harantī-netra-nikocaṃ ca vidadhatī purataḥ |
children.translated_text: This daytime drowsiness, taking away the rising of the eyes and causing their closing, presenting itself before you —

children.text: na vijānīmaḥ kiṃ tava vadati sapatnīva dina-nidrā ||GAss_107||
children.translated_text: we do not understand what it says to you, like a rival wife. [GAss 107]
This young girl's body — with a single breast-bud set between the garland-strings stretched across both walls —

children.text: guṭikā-dhanur iva bālā-vapuḥ smaraḥ śrayati kutukena ||GAss_108||
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) takes to it with curiosity, like a pellet-bow. [GAss 108]
Here, on this mountaintop, clinging, with body slightly trembling in play — a tree-deer (monkey) —
see! A bird desires to fall, deluded about her own nest. [GAss 109]

children.text: ikṣur nadī-pravāho dyūtaṃ māna-grahaś ca he sutanu |
children.translated_text: Sugarcane, the river's current, gambling, the seizing of pride, O slender one,

children.text: bhrū-latikā ca taveyaṃ bhaṅge rasam adhikam āvahati ||GAss_110||
children.translated_text: and this creeper of your brow — all yield more flavor in bending. [GAss 110]

children.text: indor ivāsya purato yad vimukhī sāpa-vāraṇā bhramasi |
children.translated_text: That you wander turning away before this face, like the moon, your curses warding off —

children.text: tat kathaya kiṃ nu duritaṃ sakhi tvayā chāyayeva kṛtam ||GAss_111||
children.translated_text: tell me, friend, what sin have you committed, as if by a shadow? [GAss 111]

children.text: iha kapaṭa-kutuka-taralita-dṛśi viśvāsaṃ kuraṅga kiṃ kuruṣe |
children.translated_text: O deer, why do you place trust in one whose eyes tremble with deceitful curiosity?
This hunter's wife, agitated by your haste, wheels around at your tail. [GAss 112]

children.text: iha vahati bahu mahodadhivibhūṣaṇā mānagarvam iyam urvī |
children.translated_text: Here this earth, adorned by the great ocean, bears much pride of vanity;

children.text: devasya kamaṭhamūrteḥ na pṛṣṭhaṃ api nikhilam āpnoti ||GAss_113||
children.translated_text: yet it does not attain even the entire back of the god in his tortoise form. [GAss 113]
Thus ends the i-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ī-kāra-vrajyā
Imagining the union with her own husband, inflamed by jealousy and anger —
I am extinguished by the intense bliss of envisioning her hips with garment fallen. [GAss 114]
O bee, your passion suited for one who belongs to a lord — why do you fall upon this one in vain?
This bud of the cheating-vine, named 'gold' in essence, is devoid of juice. [GAss 115]

children.text: īṣad avaśiṣṭa-jaḍimā śiśire gata-mātra eva ciram aṅgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With her torpor only slightly remaining from winter, just departed for a while, with her limbs —
like a young woman in the freshness of youth, the pool is enjoyed to the full. [GAss 116]
Thus ends the ī-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The u-kāra-vrajyā
By the broad raised bow of your brow, O beautiful-limbed one, by your wide eye —

children.text: acalā api na mahāntaḥ ke cañcala-bhāvam ānītāḥ ||GAss_117||
children.translated_text: even great ones who are unshakable have been brought to a state of fickleness. [GAss 117]

children.text: upanīya yan nitambe bhujaṅgam uccair alambi vibudhaiḥ śrīḥ |
children.translated_text: Since <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), brought near the hip by the gods, hung a serpent high —

children.text: ekaḥ sa mandara-giriḥ sakhi garimāṇaṃ samudvahatu ||GAss_118||
children.translated_text: let that one, Mount <s>Mandara</s>, O friend, alone bear the weight! [GAss 118]
This moon, with its visible marks, raining moonlight, shines —
with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet attached, like an overturned cart with its milk spilled. [GAss 119]
Your polite attentions and entreaties to the gambler have been ignored at a friend's words;

children.text: adhunā niṣṭhuram api yadi sa vadati kalikaitavād yāmi ||GAss_120||
children.translated_text: now, even if he speaks harshly — I shall go to that rogue, out of love's deceit. [GAss 120]
At dawn, as you turned over, the pearl necklace was pulled into the position of a sacred thread —
your skill in the <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top position), O modest one, was noticed by all! [GAss 121]

children.text: uḍḍīnānām eṣāṃ prāsādāt taruṇi pakṣiṇāṃ paṅktiḥ |
children.translated_text: The row of birds flying up from the palace, O young woman,
glitters like a victory banner torn and scattered by the wind. [GAss 122]
O golden <s>ketakī</s> flower, with your petals opened in wakefulness, jagged, blocking the swarms of bees —
may your store of fragrance not bloom forth! [GAss 123]
With brow raised, what past event do you ponder, O still-eyed one?
The ripening of love, when spoiled by petty offenses, becomes insipid — like that of jaggery. [GAss 124]
She, with brows curved in feigned anger, going out ostensibly toward her friend —

children.text: evam avataṃsam ākṣipad āhata-dīpo yathā patati ||GAss_125||
children.translated_text: thus cast her ear-ornament aside, as a struck lamp falls. [GAss 125]

children.text: udito 'pi tuhina-gahane gagana-prānte na dīpyate tapanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though risen, the sun does not shine at the frost-covered edge of the sky —
like a lamp on the lid of a shallow dish filled with hardened ghee. [GAss 126]
In rising, sitting down, lying, turning over, bending, and moving —

children.text: aniśaṃ sa mohayati māṃ hṛl-lagnaḥ śvāsa iva dayitaḥ ||GAss_127||
children.translated_text: my beloved, clinging to my heart like breath itself, constantly bewilders me. [GAss 127]
For the young couple who have abandoned the pride of good fortune, with open longing and fear of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Kāma), their minds unaware —
a single glance serves as a messenger, dispatched with purpose. [GAss 128]
Her body — with hips motionless from the embrace of the supreme serpent, yet restless at the upper limbs —

children.text: mandara-girir iva vibudhair itas tataḥ kṛṣyate kāyaḥ ||GAss_129||
children.translated_text: is pulled this way and that by the gods, like Mount <s>Mandara</s>. [GAss 129]

children.text: upanīya kalama-kuḍavaṃ kathayati sabhayaś cikitsake halikaḥ |
children.translated_text: A farmer, bringing a small measure of paddy, tells the physician fearfully:
'A red disease, resembling a half-moon, has appeared on my bride's breast.' [GAss 130]
With her lower lip slightly parted, her eyes half-closed in fear of the ash-particles —
'O smoke, do not stop here!' — this bee follows the breath. [GAss 131]

children.text: upari pariplavate mama bāleyaṃ gṛhiṇi haṃsa-māleva |
children.translated_text: O housewife, my young one floats above me like a row of geese;

children.text: sarasa iva nalina-nālā tvam āśayaṃ prāpya vasasi punaḥ ||GAss_132||
children.translated_text: and you, like the juicy stalk of a lotus, having reached the depths, dwell there again. [GAss 132]
The thief, his arms slippery with trembling and sweat, more than a handful, having lost his grip —
wishes safety for the silken borders of your breasts, O slender one. [GAss 133]
The mango bud of my friend, displayed with raised arm showing the armpit, being plucked —
it shines! For you, sir, this is a supreme gain of high position. [GAss 134]
Your necklace, O young woman, placed on your high pitcher-like breasts, setting the heart in motion, with its end resting on the hip —
resembles a plank crossing a very deep middle ravine. [GAss 135]
Stars sparkle near the edge of the radiant cool-rayed moon;
they resemble drops of nectar emerging from the bow held by <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (the flower-armed god of love). [GAss 136]

children.text: upanīya priyam asamaya-vidaṃ ca me dagdha-mānam apanīya |
children.translated_text: Having brought my beloved, who knows not the proper time, and having removed my burnt-out pride —
you, O night, have departed at the very onset of playfulness, like a go-between. [GAss 137]
You, whose sole resort is a noble woman — like an elephant seeking pool-water, stealing a friend's composure —
with thigh raised, touching with your very trunk, you steal it away. [GAss 138]
Thus ends the u-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ū-kāra-vrajyā
This woman married to him — carry her on your back! Though she clings, though she is immovable —
O all-enduring one, hard of shell, what need of the lap of a tortoise? [GAss 139]
Thus ends the ū-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ṛ-kāra-vrajyā

children.text: ṛjunā nidhehi caraṇau parihara sakhi nikhila-nāgarācāram |
children.translated_text: Place your feet straight and avoid all urbane manners, O friend!
Here the village chief punishes even a sidelong glance, calling it 'Witch!' [GAss 140]

children.text: ṛṣabho 'tra gīyata iti śrutvā svara-pāragā vayaṃ prāptāḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that 'the <s>ṛṣabha</s> (bull-note) is being sung here,' we, masters of the musical scales, have come —

children.text: ko veda goṣṭham etad go-śāntau vihita-bahu-mānam ||GAss_141||
children.translated_text: who knew this was a cattle-pen, with great honor given to the pacification of cows? [GAss 141]
Thus ends the ṛ-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The e-kāra-vrajyā
<s>Hara</s> (Śiva) alone knows the virtue of his beloved's lip; the other gods are fools —

children.text: viṣam amṛtaṃ vā samam iti yaḥ paśyan garalam eva papau ||GAss_142||
children.translated_text: he who, seeing 'poison or nectar, it is the same,' drank the very poison. [GAss 142]

children.text: eṣyati mā punar ayam iti gamane yad amaṅgalaṃ mayākāri |
children.translated_text: 'May he not come again' — the inauspicious act I performed at his departure —

children.text: adhunā tad eva kāraṇam avasthitau dagdha-geha-pateḥ ||GAss_143||
children.translated_text: that very thing is now the cause of the burnt householder's continued stay. [GAss 143]
Restless, passing over the young men one by one, as if counting dice with her rolling eyes —

children.text: viśrāmyati subhaga tvām aṅgulir āsādya merum iva ||GAss_144||
children.translated_text: her finger, O handsome one, rests when it reaches you, as upon <s>Meru</s>. [GAss 144]

children.text: ekaḥ sa eva jīvati svahṛdaya-śūnyo 'pi sahṛdayo rāhuḥ |
children.translated_text: He alone truly lives — <s>Rāhu</s>, the sympathetic one, though void of his own heart —

children.text: yaḥ sakala-laghima-kāraṇam udaraṃ na bibharti duṣpūram ||GAss_145||
children.translated_text: who does not carry the insatiable belly, the cause of all triviality. [GAss 145]

children.text: ekena cūrṇa-kuntalam apareṇa kareṇa cibukam unnamayan |
children.translated_text: With one hand arranging her dust-powdered curls, with the other hand lifting her chin,
I see at the city gate that face of hers, its cheeks washed with tears.

children.text: ekaṃ jīvana-mūlaṃ cañcalam api tāpayantam api satatam |
children.translated_text: That wretched woman carries you within — the single root of her life, fickle though you are, forever tormenting —

children.text: antar vahati varākī sā tvāṃ nāseva niḥśvāsam ||GAss_147||
children.translated_text: like a breath through the nose.

children.text: ekaṃ vadati mano mama yāmi na yāmīti hṛdayam aparaṃ me |
children.translated_text: One mind of mine says 'I shall go,' another heart of mine [says] 'I shall not go.'
Two hearts are fitting for you, O beautiful one, whose lover's heart has been stolen.
Lying on castor-oil leaves, producing sweat, with her broad hip-slopes,
meeting [him] like a poultice of dust — the plowman's wife dispels the fever of love.
Thus the section of verses beginning with 'e,' together with the <s>Vibhāva</s> commentary, is concluded.
Section of verses beginning with 'ka.'

children.text: keli-nilayaṃ sakhīm iva nayati navoḍhāṃ svayaṃ na māṃ bhajate |
children.translated_text: He leads the new bride to the pleasure-house as if [she were] a friend, [yet] does not himself attend to me.

children.text: itthaṃ gṛhiṇīm arye stuvati prativeśinā hasitam ||GAss_150||
children.translated_text: Thus the wife praises [her husband]. 'Noble lady,' [said] the neighbor — and laughed.
'This lovely bud, becoming beautiful over time, is a <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine)' — such is the prognosis:

children.text: vṛddhir yathā yathā syās tathā tathā kaṇṭakotkarṣaḥ ||GAss_151||
children.translated_text: the more it grows, the more its thorns flourish.
O you who feign sleep, listening with ears attuned to the sound of my breathing — why with intense

children.text: vidhyasi māṃ niḥśvāsaiḥ smaraḥ śaraiḥ śabda-vedhīva ||GAss_152||
children.translated_text: sighs do you pierce me, like <s>Smara</s> (Love) with arrows aimed by sound, as if striking by ear?
Where is that fine silk of sloughed skin? Where are the rows of serpent-jewels for adornment?
Since the departure of the <s>Kāliya</s> serpent, O <s>Yamunā</s>, you can be approached [only] with trust.

children.text: kiñcin na bālayoktaṃ na saprasādā niveśitā dṛṣṭiḥ |
children.translated_text: The young woman said nothing; she did not rest her gaze with favor [upon me].

children.text: mayi pada-patite kevalam akāri śuka-pañjaro vimukhaḥ ||GAss_154||
children.translated_text: When I fell at her feet, she merely turned the parrot-cage away.
Gazed upon by young men with love-trembling eyes, with laughter and clapping of hands —

children.text: kṣiptaḥ kṣipto nipatann aṅge nartayati bhṛṅgas tām ||GAss_155||
children.translated_text: thrown off again and again, landing on her body, the bee makes her dance.
O lotus-faced one, even while preventing [your gaze] in all directions, the dam adorns —
both the rivers of unrestrained current, and those with trembling eyes.
O gambler, she was deceived by you — [now] with languid eyes and slow gait.
Even with many stakes/gifts, like [a piece on] a dice-board, she does not come [to your square] anymore.
Who is that one of praiseworthy birth, whose good fortune even at midnight in <s>Māgha</s> [winter]
is told by this sound of girdle-bells, drawn out long like the snowy wind?

children.text: kim aśakanīyaṃ premṇaḥ phaṇinaḥ kathayāpi yā bibheti sma |
children.translated_text: What is impossible for love? She who used to tremble at the mere mention of a snake —
now sleeps on a pillow of foam from the serpent on <s>Giriśa</s>'s (Śiva's) arm.
For one robbed by courtesans of love [as false] as counterfeit gold —
the pain of losing wealth seems slight, [but] the public ridicule is great.

children.text: kiṃ parva-divasam ārjita-dantoṣṭhi nijaṃ vapur na maṇḍayasi |
children.translated_text: Why, O you with teeth polished on a festival day, do you not adorn your own body?

children.text: sa tvāṃ tyajati na parvasv api madhurām ikṣu-yaṣṭim iva ||GAss_161||
children.translated_text: He will not abandon you even on festival-days — like a sweet sugarcane stalk [even at its joints].

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ sāhasa-kāriṇi tava nayanārdhena so 'dhvani spṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alas, O reckless one! With half a glance, you touched him on the road.

children.text: upavītād api vidito na dvija-dehas tapasvī te ||GAss_162||
children.translated_text: Even from the sacred thread, the body of that brahmin — your ascetic — was not recognized!

children.text: kleśe'pi tanyamāne militeyaṃ māṃ pramodayaty eva |
children.translated_text: Even when distress is prolonged, this meeting delights me —
like a shower of the celestial river's waters from the sky, even when fierce and cloudless.

children.text: kūpa-prabhavāṇāṃ param ucitam apāṃ paṭṭa-bandhanaṃ manye |
children.translated_text: I think a silken covering is most fitting for waters born from a well —

children.text: yāḥ śakyante labdhuṃ na pārthivenāpi viguṇena ||GAss_164||
children.translated_text: [waters] that cannot be obtained even by a king who is without virtue.
Pierced by fingernail-tips, having wandered and rested, hard to attain at night —

children.text: ravir iva yantrollikhitaḥ kṛśo 'pi lokasya harasi dṛśam ||GAss_165||
children.translated_text: like the sun etched on a mechanical device, though emaciated, you steal the eyes of the world.

children.text: kiṃ karavāṇi divā-niśam api lagnā sahaja-śītala-prakṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: What can I do? Clinging day and night, yet innately cool in nature —

children.text: hanta sukhayāmi na priyam ātmānam ivātmanaś chāyā ||GAss_166||
children.translated_text: alas, I do not please my beloved, like one's own shadow to oneself.
If [there is] heaviness of the head from hair, death from falling into a pool of nectar,

children.text: dayita-vahanena vakṣasi yadi bhāras tad idam acikitsyam ||GAss_167||
children.translated_text: burden on the chest from carrying a beloved — then this is incurable.

children.text: kiñcit karkaśatām anu rasaṃ pradāsyan nisarga-madhuraṃ me |
children.translated_text: After a bit of harshness, about to yield its naturally sweet juice to me —

children.text: ikṣor iva te sundari mānasya granthir api kāmyaḥ ||GAss_168||
children.translated_text: like sugarcane, O beautiful one, even the knot of your sulking is desirable.

children.text: kena giriśasya dattā buddhir bhujagaṃ jaṭāvane'rpayitum |
children.translated_text: Who gave <s>Giriśa</s> (Śiva) the idea to place a serpent in his matted hair,
by which he is deprived of the passionate pulling of his hair by his beloved's hand during lovemaking?
Not heeding the strikes of hands, feet, girdle, and necklace, having seized her hair by force,
the lover kisses the face of his beloved — [her] lip trembling, [her] eyes reddened.

children.text: kurutāṃ cāpalam adhunā kalayatu surasāsi yādṛśī tad api |
children.translated_text: Let him be fickle now; let him consider you as a mere potion, whatever [you are].
O beautiful one, like a stream of water drunk after a <s>harītakī</s> (bitter fruit) [tastes sweet by contrast].
With your moon-face spotted by a collyrium-mark, with water-drops falling from your hair —
O cotton for the fire of fresh separation, whom among [your lovers] are you to keep alive?

children.text: kṛcchrānuvṛttayo 'pi hi paropakāraṃ tyajanti na mahāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even when their sustenance comes with difficulty, great ones do not abandon beneficence.
Even elephants, though living on mere grass, have their temples moist with the flow of rut-fluid (<s>dāna</s>).

children.text: kiṃ hasatha kiṃ pradhāvatha kiṃ janam āhvayatha bālakā viphalam |
children.translated_text: Why do you laugh? Why do you run? Why do you call people in vain, O children?

children.text: tad atha darśayati yathāriṣṭaḥ kaṇṭhe'munā jagṛhe ||GAss_174||
children.translated_text: That [tree] shows how the <s>ariṣṭa</s> (calamity) has seized him by the throat.
With eyes softly sweet from timidity, moaning, passion, shame, and anger —

children.text: yoktuṃ na moktum athavā valate'sāv artha-labdha-ratiḥ ||GAss_175||
children.translated_text: she struggles neither to embrace nor to release [him], she who has obtained the goal of love.

children.text: ketaka-garbhe gandhādareṇa dūrād amī drutam upetāḥ |
children.translated_text: Rushing eagerly from afar toward the heart of the <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine), out of love for its fragrance —
these bees, as if yoked to <s>Madana</s>'s (Love's) chariot, gather the pollen.

children.text: ko vakrimā guṇāḥ ke kā kāntiḥ śiśira-kiraṇa-lekhānām |
children.translated_text: What crookedness? What virtues? What beauty do the moon's rays possess —
into which, having entered from within, a particular beast [the hare] has taken hold?
Having made various churning efforts, lord for the defeat of gods and demons alike —

children.text: icchati saubhāgyam adāt svayaṃvareṇa śriyaṃ viṣṇuḥ ||GAss_178||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, desiring good fortune, won <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) through a self-choice ceremony (<s>svayaṃvara</s>).
Why, daughter, deluded by the mountain-cheek, do you sleep among the fresh clouds?
Experience the lightning's sport, the thunder, the roaming to other lands!

children.text: kāntaḥ padena hata iti saralām aparādhya kiṃ prasādayatha |
children.translated_text: 'The beloved was kicked!' — having offended the innocent one, why do you try to appease [her]?

children.text: so 'py evam eva sulabhaḥ pada-prahāraḥ prasādaḥ kim ||GAss_180||
children.translated_text: That [kick] was just as easily obtained; is a kick not a [form of] favor?

children.text: karṇa-gateyam amoghā dṛṣṭis tava śaktir indra-dattā ca |
children.translated_text: Your glance that reaches the ear is unfailing, and [it is] a power given by <s>Indra</s>.
It has never failed to achieve victory; this [glance] has never fallen anywhere in vain.

children.text: kleśayasi kim iti dūtīr yad aśakyaṃ sumukhi tava kaṭākṣeṇa |
children.translated_text: Why do you trouble messengers, O fair-faced one? What is impossible for your sidelong glance?

children.text: kāmo 'pi tatra sāyakam akīrti-śaṅkī na sandhatte ||GAss_182||
children.translated_text: Even <s>Kāma</s> (Love), fearing disgrace, does not fit his arrow to the bow there.

children.text: ko veda mūlyam akṣa-dyūte prabhuṇā paṇīkṛtasya vidhoḥ |
children.translated_text: Who knows the value of the moon wagered by the lord in a dice game?

children.text: prativijaye yat pratipaṇam adharaṃ ghara-nandinī vidadhe ||GAss_183||
children.translated_text: — since the household beauty placed her lip as the counter-stake for the counter-victory.

children.text: kupitāṃ caraṇa-praharaṇa-bhayena muñcāmi na khalu caṇḍi tvām |
children.translated_text: Though angry, I shall not release you, O fierce one, for fear of a kick.
The bee, enduring the wind-tossed tender-leaf's slapping, still courts the creeper.
On the bow of <s>Smara</s> (Love) that is your anger-drawn eyebrow, O beloved, cover the falling
drops of tear-water stained with collyrium — like bees [falling] from a cut bowstring.

children.text: kāmenāpi na bhettuṃ kim u hṛdayam apāri bāla-vanitānām |
children.translated_text: Could even <s>Kāma</s> (Love) not pierce the hearts of young women?
— [for] their chest appears swollen, as if from the blows of blunted arrows.

children.text: kiṃ para-jīvair dīvyasi vismaya-madhurākṣi gaccha sakhi dūram |
children.translated_text: Why do you gamble with others' lives, O you of sweet, wonder-filled eyes? Go far away, friend!
Let the snake-charmer play with the snake in the courtyard undisturbed.
The more the one with anger-trembling eyes strikes with hands and feet upon his limbs,

children.text: roṣayati paruṣa-vacanais tathā tathā preyasīṃ rasikaḥ ||GAss_188||
children.translated_text: the more the connoisseur provokes his beloved with harsh words.

children.text: kas tāṃ nindati lumpati kaḥ smara-phalakasya varṇakaṃ mugdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Who can blame her? What fool would strip the paint from <s>Smara</s>'s (Love's) canvas?

children.text: ko bhavati ratna-kaṇṭakam amṛte kasyārucir udeti ||GAss_189||
children.translated_text: Who finds a thorn in a jewel? In whom does distaste for nectar arise?
When you, [O beloved,] in anger playfully brandish the mango-shoot in your hand,

children.text: kara-kampita-karavāle smara iva sā mūrcchitā sutanuḥ ||GAss_190||
children.translated_text: that slender woman swoons, like one [felled] by <s>Smara</s> (Love) with his hand-shaken sword.
'I court her for her good family lineage' — <s>Smara</s> (Love) validates the mongoose [argument].
Since I contemplate that [lineage], my slip of the clan-name while courting her is unavoidable.

children.text: kuta iha kuraṅga-śāvaka kedāre kalam amañjarīṃ tyajasi |
children.translated_text: Whence [have you come] here, O deer-fawn? You leave behind the unblossomed rice in the field!
This deceitful fellow has a grass-arrow, a grass-bow — he is made entirely of grass!
Thus the section of verses beginning with 'ka,' together with the <s>Vibhāva</s> commentary, is concluded.
Section of verses beginning with 'kha.'

children.text: khala-sakhyaṃ prāṅ madhuraṃ vayo 'natarāle nidāgha-dinam ante |
children.translated_text: Friendship with a scoundrel is sweet at first, [bitter] in the middle of life — like a summer's day at its end.
Friendship with good people is delightful at the beginning, middle, and conclusion.
Thus the section of verses beginning with 'kha,' together with the <s>Vibhāva</s> commentary, is concluded.
Section of verses beginning with 'ga.'

children.text: guṇam adhigatam api dhanavān na cirān nāśayati rakṣati daridraḥ |
children.translated_text: A wealthy man quickly destroys even an acquired virtue; a poor man preserves it.

children.text: majjayati rajjum ambhasi pūrṇaḥ kumbhaḥ sakhi na tucchaḥ ||GAss_194||
children.translated_text: A full pitcher, dear friend, sinks the rope in the water — not an empty one.

children.text: gurur api laghūpanīto na nimajjati niyatam āśaye mahataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even something heavy, when brought by something light, does not sink in the receptacle of a great one —
like a mountain brought by a monkey to the abode of sea-monsters [the ocean].

children.text: gaurī-pater garīyo garalaṃ gatvā gale jīrṇam |
children.translated_text: The severe poison, having gone to the throat of <s>Gaurī</s>'s lord (<s>Śiva</s>), was digested.

children.text: jīryati karṇe mahatāṃ durvādo nālpam api viśati ||GAss_196||
children.translated_text: Slander reaches the ears of great ones [but] is digested — it does not penetrate even slightly.
Before her husband, the young woman, describing her paramour's love-state through deceitful stories,

children.text: prīṇayati pīḍayati ca bālā niḥśvasya niḥśvasya ||GAss_197||
children.translated_text: both pleases and torments [him], sighing again and again.
Let the elephant, whose gait shames the finest women, make his temples stained with rut-fluid.
O <s>Lambodara</s> (Fat-Belly, i.e., <s>Gaṇeśa</s>), [you who are] an elephant only in the band across your face — why do you bear rut?
Hearing the wife's sulking arising from [his] slip of a [wrong] clan-name,

children.text: snigdhāṃ priye sa-garvāṃ sakhīṣu bālā dṛśaṃ diśati ||GAss_199||
children.translated_text: the young woman casts a glance among her friends — affectionate and proud, O beloved.
In this summer season, behold at the foot of the pleasure-grove —
as if under the pretext of water-basin rings around [the trees], coolness has coiled up.

children.text: guṇa-baddha-caraṇa iti mā līlā-vihagaṃ vimuñca sakhi mugdhe |
children.translated_text: 'His feet are bound by virtues' — thus, O naive friend, do not release the pet bird!
On this branch full of curves, the string-restraint snaps in an instant.
Before those whose ears and eyes are shut from fear of heavy thunder and dense lightning —

children.text: bālā cumbati jāraṃ vajrād adhiko hi madaneṣuḥ ||GAss_202||
children.translated_text: the young woman kisses her paramour. Indeed, <s>Madana</s>'s (Love's) arrow is mightier than a thunderbolt.

children.text: gṛhiṇī-guṇeṣu gaṇitā vinayaḥ sevā vidheyateti guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Among a wife's virtues are counted modesty, service, and obedience as qualities.
But pride, authority, and perversity are the ornaments of the fair-eyed ones [courtesans].

children.text: guṇam āntaram aguṇaṃ vā lakṣmīr gaṅgā ca veda hari-harayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether there is inner virtue or vice in <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) and <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Gaṅgā</s> know.

children.text: ekā pade'pi ramate na vasati nihitā śirasy aparā ||GAss_204||
children.translated_text: One delights even at his feet [yet] does not stay; the other, placed on his head, does not depart.

children.text: gatvā jīvita-saṃśayam abhyastaḥ soḍhum aticirād virahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having gone to the brink of death, separation has been endured for so very long.

children.text: akaruṇaḥ punar api ditsasi surata-durabhyāsam asmākam ||GAss_205||
children.translated_text: O merciless one, do you wish to give us once more the hard practice of lovemaking?
Even when questioned about a slip of the clan-name, having given an answer exceedingly calm and composed,

children.text: niḥśvasya mogha-rūpe sva-vapuṣi nihitaṃ tayā cakṣuḥ ||GAss_206||
children.translated_text: sighing, she placed her gaze upon her own body — useless in its beauty.
O fragrance-seeker, having placed your whole body in the exuded resin of the opened <s>śāla</s> tree —
having enjoyed and abandoned hundreds of trees, O bee-woman, do you not now wander?

children.text: guruṣu militeṣu śirasā praṇamasi laghuṣūnnatā sameṣu samā |
children.translated_text: Before the heavy [elders], you bow your head; before the light [insignificant], you rise up; before equals, you are even.

children.text: ucitajñāsi tule kiṃ tulayasi guñjā-phalaiḥ kanakam ||GAss_208||
children.translated_text: O balance, you know propriety — but why do you weigh gold with <s>guñjā</s> berries?
Pulled by the wife, held back by the new bride, before me —

children.text: mama naukā-dvitayārpita-guṇa iva hṛdayaṃ dvidhā bhavati ||GAss_209||
children.translated_text: my heart becomes split in two, like a rope attached to two boats.
A single virtue capable of drawing, like [the string] of a bow, suffices for hitting the mark.

children.text: lūtātantubhir iva kiṃ guṇair vimardāsahair bahubhiḥ ||GAss_210||
children.translated_text: What use are many virtues that cannot withstand friction, like spider-threads?

children.text: gāyati gīte vaṃśe vādayati sa vipañcīṣu |
children.translated_text: She sings along when a song [plays], plays on the <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes),
She teaches the caged parrot the syllables of your message, O <s>Rāmā</s> (beloved woman).

children.text: gaṇayati na madhu-vyayam ayam aviratam āpibatu madhukaraḥ kumudam |
children.translated_text: He does not count the expense of honey—let the bee drink the night-lily unceasingly;
Proud of [his] beauty, the moon is jealous of the sun.

children.text: guṇa-vidhṛtā sakhi tiṣṭhasi tathaiva dehena kiṃ tu hṛdayaṃ te |
children.translated_text: O friend, you stand sustained by your virtues, and your body remains the same, but your heart
Has been stolen by him, like the fragrance [stolen] from a garland by the breeze.

children.text: guru-sadane nedīyasi caraṇa-gate mayi ca mūkayāpi tayā |
children.translated_text: When I was nearby at the <s>guru</s>'s house, and at her feet, even though she was silent,

children.text: nūpuram apāsya padayoḥ kiṃ na priyam īritaṃ priyayā ||GAss_214||
children.translated_text: Did not the beloved express her love by removing the anklets from her feet?

children.text: granthilatayā kim ikṣoḥ kim apabhraṃśena bhavati gītasya |
children.translated_text: What use is a knot to sugarcane? What good comes from the corruption of a song?

children.text: kim anārjavena śaśinaḥ kiṃ dāridryeṇa dayitasya ||GAss_215||
children.translated_text: What use is crookedness to the moon? What use is poverty to a lover?
Even with eyes closed from the hiss at the moment of hair-grasping by the wife,
Seeing the goosebumps on the young girl's cheek, I was placed with a foot on my head.
With heavy lashes, reddened from wakefulness, the rolling pupil somehow turns—
This eye, with brow curved in anger due to the impression of visible nail-marks.
Thus ends the ga-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The gha-kāra section.
With hips pressed together, plump thighs squeezed, the entire weight of her breasts placed upon him,

children.text: āliṅganty api bālā vadaty asau muñca muñceti ||GAss_218||
children.translated_text: Even while embracing, the young woman says, 'Let go! Let go!'

children.text: ghaṭita-palāśa-kapāṭaṃ niśi niśi sukhino hi śerate padmāḥ |
children.translated_text: With their doors of <s>palāśa</s> leaves closed, lotuses sleep happily night after night;

children.text: ujjāgareṇa kairava kati śakyā rakṣituṃ lakṣmīḥ ||GAss_219||
children.translated_text: O night-lily, how long can you guard your beauty through wakefulness?
The deceived lamp-buds flicker, failing from the loss of affection;
At dawn, the heart of the woman whose traveler-husband has departed bursts open, like the lotus.
Thus ends the gha-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ca-kāra section.
Seeing the crown of her fickle husband's head marked with grey hairs,
Even at a moment that called for sorrow, the wife felt only delight.

children.text: caṇḍi prasāritena spṛśan bhujenāpi kopanāṃ bhavatīm |
children.translated_text: O angry one, even while touching you, who are furious, with an outstretched arm,

children.text: tṛpyāmi paṅkilām iva piban nadīṃ nalina-nālena ||GAss_222||
children.translated_text: I am satisfied—like drinking a muddy river through a lotus stalk.
O night-breeze, cooled after being enjoyed and abandoned by the fickle serpent-woman, wandering at night—
Go! Come at dawn as always, to fulfill the remaining hope.
O long-absent traveler, the gaze of the doe-eyed one, matted with tangles of creeper-like locks meeting in length,
Is now always tear-filled, like a mountain stream.
O angry one, though relishing only the sight of your thighs revealed by slightly moving garments,

children.text: dhūli-bhayād api na mayā caraṇa-hṛtau kuñcitaṃ cakṣuḥ ||GAss_225||
children.translated_text: I did not even squint my eyes, despite the fear of dust.
With earrings swaying, locks flying, the garment slipping from her breasts and catching at her thighs,
Eyes narrowed from the fatigue of heavy hips—this gait of hers captivates.

children.text: caraṇaiḥ parāga-saikatam aphalam idaṃ likhasi madhupa ketakyāḥ |
children.translated_text: O bee, you fruitlessly trace with your feet [patterns on] the pollen-sand of the <s>ketakī</s>;
Here dwells the ocean of honey—with the essence of beauty, yet not even with water within.
O innocent one whose traveler-husband has been long absent, why do you look with eyes wavering in suspicion?
This is the row of calluses from the wounds of that woman's sword-like embrace.

children.text: capalāṃ yathā madāndhaś chāyāmayam ātmanaḥ karo hanti |
children.translated_text: Just as a rut-blinded elephant strikes its own shadow-form thinking it lightning,

children.text: āsphālayati karaṃ pratigajas tathāyaṃ puro ruddhaḥ ||GAss_229||
children.translated_text: So does this rival elephant, blocked before him, slap his trunk.
Remembering her thigh-pair—the tethering post for the elephant of my heart—from which the saffron was stolen by my kiss-eager lip,
I am not satisfied.
With neck bent sideways as she loosens her hair, seemingly turned away in demeanor,
This girl still watches you through a gap made in her tresses by her finger.
You cast a glance with collyrium stolen by kisses, reddened by obvious wakefulness—
Why at dawn, anxious with separation, like a half-arrow of the unmatched archer [<s>Kāma</s>]?
Thus ends the ca-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The cha-kāra section.

children.text: chāyā-grāhī candraḥ kūṭatvaṃ satatam ambujaṃ vrajati |
children.translated_text: The moon seizes shadows; the lotus constantly resorts to deceit;
Abandoning both, people in the assembly praise only your face.
Even gazing downward, seeing only a shadow, with upwelling composure,
