<s>Rādhā</s>, skilled at [piercing] my heart, strikes like <s>Kirīṭī</s> [<s>Arjuna</s>] [striking] <s>Rādhā</s>'s [<s>Karṇa</s>'s] chariot-wheel.
Thus ends the cha-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ja-kāra section.

children.text: jala-bindavaḥ katipaye nayanād gamanodyame tava skhalitāḥ |
children.translated_text: A few drops of water fell from your eyes as you prepared to depart;

children.text: kānte mama gantavyā bhūr etair eva picchilitā ||GAss_235||
children.translated_text: O beloved, by these alone the ground I must walk has been made slippery.
Arms raised stiff in a yawn, the earring pressing against her cheek, her collyrium smeared by drops of water,
I remember her face with its languid gaze.

children.text: jāgaritvā puruṣaṃ paraṃ vane sarvato mukhaṃ harasi |
children.translated_text: O wild jasmine, having stayed awake, you turn your face in every direction in the forest seeking the supreme man;

children.text: ati śarad-anurūpaṃ tava śīlam idaṃ jāti-śālinyāḥ ||GAss_237||
children.translated_text: This conduct of yours, O noble-born one, is most fitting for autumn.
Thus ends the ja-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The jha-kāra section.
With hand-gestures accompanied by jingling bangles, by leaning on pillars, by silences,
And even by dry weeping, O beautiful one, you adorn the doorway of the mansion.
Thus ends the jha-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ḍha-kāra section.

children.text: ḍhakkām āhatya madaṃ vitanvate kariṇa iva ciraṃ puruṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having beaten the drum, men extend their intoxication for a long time, like male elephants;

children.text: strīṇāṃ kariṇīnām iva madaḥ punaḥ sva-kula-nāśāya ||GAss_247||
children.translated_text: But for women, as for female elephants, their intoxication leads only to the ruin of their own family.
Thus ends the ḍha-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ta-kāra section.

children.text: tāṃ tāpayanti manmatha-bāṇās tvāṃ prīṇayanti bata subhaga |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s>'s (Love's) arrows torment her, yet delight you, O fortunate one!
The sun's rays make the sun-stone blaze but make the moon sweet.
O slender one, with your consent, from her whose hip-coloring arises from many minerals,
Like gaining heaven from the mountain-queen's summit, I attain heaven by two finger-widths.

children.text: tyakto muñcati jīvanam ujjhati nānugrahe'pi lolutvam |
children.translated_text: Abandoned, he gives up his life; discarded, yet he does not give up his longing even without favor—

children.text: kiṃ prāvṛṣeva padmākarasya karaṇīyam asya mayā ||GAss_250||
children.translated_text: What am I to do with this one, as [what is to be done] with a lotus-pond in the rainy season?
O fortunate one, pale from the calamity of your absence, the slender-limbed one
Can be recognized only by her shadow, like a goose in moonlight.

children.text: tvayi viniveśita-cittā subhaga gatā kevalena kāyena |
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, having fixed her heart upon you, she has departed with her body alone,
Like a river with only its waters, whose fish are blocked by a net of clouds.

children.text: tvayi saṃsaktaṃ tasyāḥ kaṭhoratara hṛdayam asama-śara-taralam |
children.translated_text: O hard-hearted one, her heart, fixed upon you, trembling with the arrows of the unmatched one [<s>Kāma</s>],
Has burst from contact with thorns, like a garment fluttering in the wind.

children.text: tvam asūryaṃpaśyā sakhi padam api na vināpavāraṇaṃ bhramasi |
children.translated_text: O friend, you who are not to be seen by the sun—you do not step out a single pace without a screen;

children.text: chāye kim iha vidheyaṃ muñcanti na mūrtimantas tvām ||GAss_254||
children.translated_text: O shadow, what is to be done here? Embodied beings will not release you!
In your absence, with the night stretched out, having developed hatred for the moon and sandal-paste,

children.text: visinīva māgha-māse vinā hutāśane sā dagdhā ||GAss_255||
children.translated_text: She was burned without fire, like a lotus-plant in the month of <s>M��gha</s>.
O young woman, the cluster of <s>kaṅkellī</s> buds that blossomed from the kick of your foot—

children.text: kuṭila-caritā sapatnī na pibati bata śoka-vikalāpi ||GAss_256||
children.translated_text: The crooked co-wife, though distressed with grief, does not drink [its beauty].

children.text: talpe prabhur iva gurur iva manasija-tantre śrame bhujiṣyeva |
children.translated_text: On the bed, like a master; in the doctrine of love, like a <s>guru</s>; in labor, like a maidservant;

children.text: gehe śrīr iva guru-jana-purato mūrteva sā vrīḍā ||GAss_257||
children.translated_text: In the house, like <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī); before the elders—she is the very embodiment of modesty.

children.text: tvam alabhyā mama tāvan moktum aśaktasya saṃmukhaṃ vrajataḥ |
children.translated_text: For me, unable to obtain you and unable to let go, as you come face to face—
Like a shadow receding, you cannot be stopped even by a wall.

children.text: tapasā kleśita eṣa prauḍha-balo na khalu phālgune'py āsīt |
children.translated_text: Tormented by austerities, this one had no full strength even in <s>Phālguna</s>;

children.text: madhunā pramattam adhunā ko madanaṃ mihiram iva sahate ||GAss_259||
children.translated_text: Now intoxicated by spring, who can endure <s>Kāma</s> (Love), as [who can endure] the sun?
O fortunate one, the wall of her house too, marked with tally-lines indistinct from counting the days of your journey,
Has turned pale, like the surface of her cheek.
O friend, I have been pierced by that rustic one's glance—curved, tender, and sweet—

children.text: viddhā tad-eka-neyā potriṇa iva daṃṣṭrayā dharaṇī ||GAss_261||
children.translated_text: Led by him alone, like the earth by the tusk of a boar.

children.text: tvayi kugrāma-vaṭa-druma vaiśravaṇo vasatu vā lakṣmīḥ |
children.translated_text: O banyan tree of the wretched village! Let <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) or <s>Lakṣmī</s> dwell in you—
Your only protection from the axe of the lowborn is through a buffalo's head [hung upon you].

children.text: tava mukhara vadana-doṣaṃ sahamānā moktum akṣamā sutanuḥ |
children.translated_text: O libertine, enduring the fault of your talkative mouth, yet unable to abandon you,

children.text: sā vahati viṭa bhavantaṃ ghuṇamantaḥ śālabhañjīva ||GAss_263||
children.translated_text: The slender woman bears you like a <s>śālabhañjī</s> tree [bearing] a wood-worm within.

children.text: tṛṇa-mukham iva na khalu tvāṃ tyajanty amī hariṇa vairiṇaḥ śavarāḥ |
children.translated_text: O deer, these hostile hunters do not merely leave you like a blade of grass;
Stake your life on glory—fight with horns locked in combat!

children.text: tripura-ripor iva gaṅgā mama mānini janita-madana-dāhasya |
children.translated_text: O proud one, like <s>Gaṅgā</s> for the enemy of <s>Tripura</s> [<s>Śiva</s>], burning with the fire of desire,
You grant life to me who offers his head, by merely grasping my hair.
Chattering about you among her friends—with feigned scorn, delight, and dissimulation—

children.text: sa khalu sakhīnāṃ nibhṛtaṃ tvayā kṛtārthīkṛtaḥ subhagaḥ ||GAss_266||
children.translated_text: He, that fortunate one, was secretly made content by you.

children.text: tvayi sarpati pathi dṛṣṭiḥ sundara vṛti-vivara-nirgatā tasyāḥ |
children.translated_text: As you walk on the path, O handsome one, her glance emerging through a gap in the curtain
Flickers like a <s>sapharī</s> fish breaking through a net of moss, slightly trembling.

children.text: te sutanu śūnya-hṛdayā ye śaṅkhaṃ śūnya-hṛdayam abhidadhati |
children.translated_text: O slender one, empty-hearted are they who call the conch 'empty-hearted';
[So too is he] who, having accepted the lotus-leaf in hand, takes your hand in marriage.

children.text: te śreṣṭhinaḥ kva samprati śakra-dhvaja yaiḥ kṛtas tavocchrāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>'s banner-pole, where are those merchants now by whom your height was raised?

children.text: īṣāṃ vā meḍhiṃ vādhunātanās tvāṃ vidhitsanti ||GAss_269||
children.translated_text: The moderns wish to make you either a plowshare or a sacrificial post.
Having become thin, cut off, pieced together by another's applied passion and love—

children.text: karṇa iva kāminīnāṃ na śobhate nirbharaḥ premā ||GAss_270||
children.translated_text: Like women's ears, excessive love does not look beautiful.

children.text: tasmin gatārdra-bhāve vīta-rase śuṇṭhi-śakala iva puruṣe |
children.translated_text: When that man's passion is gone and sentiment spent—like a piece of dried ginger—
Even though he possesses wealth, [yet] is dirty, the word 'urbane' is but a mockery.

children.text: tamasi ghane viṣame pathi jambukam ulkā-mukhaṃ prapannāḥ smaḥ |
children.translated_text: In dense darkness, on a dangerous path, we have taken recourse to a jackal with a firebrand-face;

children.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ so 'pi sakhe sthito mukhaṃ mudrayitvaiva ||GAss_272||
children.translated_text: What can we do? He too, O friend, has stopped, having simply shut his mouth.

children.text: tvām abhilaṣato mānini mama garima-guṇo 'pi doṣatāṃ yātaḥ |
children.translated_text: O proud one, for me who desires you, even the quality of gravity has become a fault—

children.text: paṅkila-kūlāṃ taṭinīṃ yiyāsataḥ sindhur asy eva ||GAss_273||
children.translated_text: Like the ocean for one who wishes to cross a river with muddy banks.

children.text: timire'pi dūra-dṛśyā kaṭhināśleṣe ca rahasi mukharā ca |
children.translated_text: Visible even in darkness from afar, loud even in private during a rough embrace—
May this row of conch-shell bangles shatter along with the husband's head!
O beautiful one, by your conduct and virtues, fit for a well-endowed throat to roll upon,

children.text: hāra-sraja iva sundari kṛtaḥ punar nāyakas taralaḥ ||GAss_275||
children.translated_text: The hero, like a necklace-garland, has been made fickle again.
Thus ends the ta-kāra section with <s>Vibh��va</s>'s commentary.
The da-kāra section.
The wife, her pride subdued upon seeing [him], her cheek-surface sparkling with joy,
Covers her face with her hands on the pretext of forbidding a kiss.
Bodily rigidity, stumbling, weakness, trembling, thoughts of the beloved,

children.text: pathi pathi gaganāśleṣaḥ kāmini kas te'bhisāra-guṇaḥ ||GAss_277||
children.translated_text: Embracing the sky at every step on the path—O lover, which of these is a virtue of your tryst?
Her life has been diminished by the intense heat of your separation, lengthening the days—
Like [the water of] a lotus-pond [diminished] by summer.

children.text: durjana-sahavāsād api śīlotkarṣaṃ na sajjanas tyajati |
children.translated_text: Even from association with the wicked, a noble person does not abandon excellence of character;
The moon, dwelling at each quarter with the sun, is cool the moment it emerges.

children.text: dayita-prahitāṃ dūtīm ālambya kareṇa tamasi gacchantī |
children.translated_text: O fair-limbed one, going in the darkness, holding the hand of the messenger-woman sent by your beloved,
You are visible from afar by the musk dripping from your perspiration.
The beloved's virtue has been made public by the fault of his own mouth;
Why do you torment yourself with daily breaching and mending the fence-enclosure?

children.text: dākṣiṇyān mradimānaṃ dadhataṃ mā bhānum enam avamaṃsthāḥ |
children.translated_text: Out of courtesy, bearing a gentle warmth—do not scorn this sun;

children.text: raudrīm upāgate'smin kaḥ kṣamate dṛṣṭim api dātum ||GAss_282||
children.translated_text: when it assumes its fierce [form], who can endure even to cast a glance? [GAss 282]
With her gaze alone—its pupils trembling with the anguish of separation—offered upon the beloved's face,
the life-breaths of the doe, wounded by the hunter's arrow, depart. [GAss 283]
With heart kept at a distance, secrets well-concealed, utterly full of suspicion—

children.text: āśleṣo bālānāṃ bhavati khalānāṃ ca sambhedaḥ ||GAss_284||
children.translated_text: the embrace of children and the alliance of villains are the same. [GAss 284]

children.text: dvāre guravaḥ koṇe śukaḥ sakāśe śiśur gṛhe sakhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Elders at the door, a parrot in the corner, a child nearby, friends in the house—'
'O impatient one, be patient, dear! Be gracious—the day has passed.' [GAss 285]
With limbs languid from the toil of churning, the <s>gopī</s> (cowherd-woman) embraces her beloved—
charming with the offering of her breasts heaving with her breath, adorned with drops of curd and pearl ornaments. [GAss 286]

children.text: dalitodvegena sakhi priyeṇa lagnena rāgam āvahatā |
children.translated_text: 'O friend, by my beloved—who dispelled my anxiety, clung close, brought passion,
and bewildered me—I was led to the bed, as if by a betel-leaf!' [GAss 287]

children.text: dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭa-prāyaṃ dayitaṃ kṛtvā prakāśitas tanayā |
children.translated_text: Having treated her glimpsed-but-barely-seen beloved as revealed, the daughter—

children.text: hṛdayaṃ kareṇa tāḍitam atha mithyā vyañjita-trapayā ||GAss_288||
children.translated_text: struck her heart with her hand, then falsely displayed bashfulness. [GAss 288]
In your eye, displaying the height of the <s>Yamunā</s>, playing with the coquetry of your brows,

children.text: kṣipta-hale haladhara iva sarvaṃ puramarjitaṃ sutanu ||GAss_289||
children.translated_text: O slender one, like <s>Haladhara</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>, the plough-bearer) when the plough was cast, everything previously won [is swept away]. [GAss 289]
The <s>bakula</s> tree, delicate with the sprinkling of mouth-wine—hard to obtain even when sought by the beloved—

children.text: vyathayati virahe bakulaḥ kva paricayaḥ prakṛti-kaṭhinānām ||GAss_290||
children.translated_text: causes pain in separation. Where is such intimacy among those hard by nature? [GAss 290]

children.text: dvitrair eṣyāmi dinair iti kiṃ tad vacasi sakhi tavāśvāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I shall return in two or three days'—what is your assurance in those words, O friend?

children.text: kathayati cira-pathikaṃ taṃ dūra-nikhāto nakhāṅkas te ||GAss_291||
children.translated_text: Your nail-mark, deeply imprinted, declares him a long-absent traveler. [GAss 291]
O friend, her feet slipping on the water flowing from passion awakened by the beloved's touch, her eyes faltering,
her words made loud by the burden of pride—why do you offend her locks? [GAss 292]

children.text: duṣṭa-graheṇa gehini tena kuputreṇa kiṃ prajātena |
children.translated_text: O housewife, what use is that wicked son, born under an evil planet (<s>graha</s>)?
By whom, like [the planet] <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars), his own family has been reduced to embers! [GAss 293]
With diamonds—radiant, displaying the arc of a bow, born of good lineage—

children.text: hīrair apsv api vīrair āpatsv api gamyate nādhaḥ ||GAss_294||
children.translated_text: and with heroes, even in waters, even in calamities, one does not sink. [GAss 294]
O naive one, that gaze of yours, even upon <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god) half-asleep, drove out my life-breaths by its art—

children.text: mugdhe tava dṛṣṭir asāv arjuna-yantreṣur iva hanti ||GAss_295||
children.translated_text: it slays like <s>Arjuna's</s> arrow guided by the mechanism. [GAss 295]

children.text: durgata-gṛhiṇī tanaye karuṇārdrā priyatame ca rāgamayī |
children.translated_text: The destitute man's wife—compassionate toward her son, passionate toward her beloved—

children.text: mugdhā ratābhiyogaṃ na manyate na pratikṣipati ||GAss_296||
children.translated_text: the naive one neither considers the labor of lovemaking an offense, nor rejects it. [GAss 296]
O destitute wife, sleeping in your crumbling house, you worship the moon just the same;
we, whose eyes are deceived by the moon, are women who sport on concealed swings. [GAss 297]
A lamp-wick, a woman of good family—only through expertise does she become darkened;

children.text: doṣā api bhūṣāyai gaṇikāyāḥ śaśi-kalāyāś ca ||GAss_298||
children.translated_text: yet faults serve as ornaments for a courtesan and for the crescent moon. [GAss 298]
The red rays of the sun, falling through the openings of tall windows,
enter the palace floor like the claws of <s>Nṛhari</s> (<s>Narasiṃha</s>, the Man-Lion) into the demon's chest. [GAss 299]

children.text: dara-tarale'kṣaṇi vakṣasi daronnate tava mukhe ca dara-hasite |
children.translated_text: With your eyes slightly trembling, your breast slightly raised, and your face slightly smiling—
let the flower be; the hero <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god) now [conquers] even with his painted bow alone! [GAss 300]
She of the full-moon face, accompanied by wicked friends, is not for pleasure now;
like a full-moon night conjoined with rain, let her be for your delight at night. [GAss 301]

children.text: dalite palāla-puñje vṛṣabhaṃ paribhavati gṛha-patau kupite |
children.translated_text: When the chaff-heap is trampled and the master of the house is angry, [and he] berates the bull,
the farmer's daughter-in-law and brother-in-law, their faces secretly observed, laugh. [GAss 302]

children.text: dīpyantāṃ ye dīptyai ghaṭitā maṇayaś ca vīra-puruṣāś ca |
children.translated_text: Let those who were made to shine blaze forth—gems and heroic men alike;

children.text: tejaḥ sva-vināśāya tu nṛṇāṃ tṛṇānām iva laghūnām ||GAss_303||
children.translated_text: but brilliance leads to the destruction of small men, as of straw. [GAss 303]
Thus ends the section beginning with the letter 'da,' accompanied by the <s>vibhāva</s> commentary.
The section beginning with the letter 'dha.'

children.text: dhūmair aśru nipātaya daha śikhayā dahana-malinayāṅgāraiḥ |
children.translated_text: O fire! Shed tears with your smoke, burn with your flame, blacken with your coals—

children.text: jāgarayiṣyati durgata-gṛhiṇī tvāṃ tad api śiśira-niśi ||GAss_304||
children.translated_text: the destitute wife will keep you awake nonetheless on a winter night. [GAss 304]

children.text: dhairyaṃ nidhehi gacchatu rajanī so 'py astu sumukhi sotkaṇṭhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Be steadfast! Let the night pass. Let him too be longing, O fair-faced one!

children.text: praviśa hṛdi tasya dūraṃ kṣaṇa-dhṛta-muktā smareṣur iva ||GAss_305||
children.translated_text: Enter his heart deeply—like <s>Smara's</s> arrow, held for a moment then released. [GAss 305]
With faint white nail-marks, weakened, with toilette unattended, her eyes hidden by stray locks—
I shall behold that form at the city gate, tears doubled at the sight of me. [GAss 306]
Even in the undertaking of <s>dharma</s>, the wicked are motivated only by harming others;
at the ceremonial bathing of crows, rain experiences its own purposelessness. [GAss 307]
Thus ends the section beginning with the letter 'dha,' accompanied by the <s>vibhāva</s> commentary.
The section beginning with the letter 'na.'
In winter, with their banks thick from the mingling of sand, jagged from descents into the water,
the rivers shine as if draped with cloths thick as heaps of cotton. [GAss 308]
Resting in the shadow of her own body, to avert the calamity of summer heat—
alas, this naive young doe performs various postures of her body. [GAss 309]

children.text: na hasanti jaraṭha iti yad vallava-vanitā namanti nandam api |
children.translated_text: Because the cowherd-women do not laugh at him as 'old' but bow to <s>Nanda</s> too—
O friend, he is <s>Yaśodā's</s> son, in whom <s>Kandarpa</s> (the Love-god) is eternally budding. [GAss 310]

children.text: nītā svabhāvam arpita-vapur api vāmyaṃ na kāminī tyajati |
children.translated_text: Even when brought to her natural state, even when she has surrendered her body, a passionate woman does not abandon her contrariness;
<s>Pārvatī</s>, bound to half of <s>Hara's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) body, is the example of that. [GAss 311]
Of the weaver, whose pride in his own wife's beauty—inferred from the pleasures of city men—trembles,

children.text: nipatati padaṃ na bhūmau jñāti-puras tantu-vāyasya ||GAss_312||
children.translated_text: his foot does not touch the ground before his kinsmen! [GAss 312]

children.text: nipatati caraṇe koṇe praviśya niśi yan nirīkṣate kas tat |
children.translated_text: 'He falls at my feet in a corner, entering at night—but who sees that?'

children.text: sakhi sa khalu loka-purataḥ khalaḥ sva-garimāṇam udgirati ||GAss_313||
children.translated_text: 'O friend, that villain before the public belches forth his own greatness!' [GAss 313]

children.text: na vimocayituṃ śakyaḥ kṣamāṃ mahān mocito yadi kathaṃcit |
children.translated_text: A great [offender] cannot be pardoned; if pardoned somehow,

children.text: mandara-girir iva garalaṃ nivartate nanu samutthāpya ||GAss_314||
children.translated_text: like Mount <s>Mandara</s> [that churned up] poison, does he not return, having raised [trouble]? [GAss 314]
To be served with measured steps, bringing disaster if one stumbles—who, having other options,

children.text: sambhavad anya-gatiḥ kaḥ saṅkrama-kāṣṭhaṃ durīśaṃ ca ||GAss_315||
children.translated_text: resorts to a crossing-plank or a wretched lord? [GAss 315]
Of elephants and good poets, who enchant the world by the merit of the gait of their own strides—

children.text: vahatām api mahimānaṃ śobhāyai sajjanā eva ||GAss_316||
children.translated_text: even for those who bear greatness, only the virtuous serve as an ornament. [GAss 316]

children.text: nottapane na snehaṃ harati na nirvāti na malino bhavati |
children.translated_text: It does not burn, does not steal affection, does not extinguish, does not become tarnished—

children.text: tasyojjvalo niśi niśi premā ratna-pradīpa iva ||GAss_317||
children.translated_text: her love, brilliant night after night, is like a jewel-lamp. [GAss 317]

children.text: nihitān nihitān ujjhati niyataṃ mama pārthivān api prema |
children.translated_text: My love certainly abandons even kings, one after another, whom I fix upon,

children.text: bhrāmaṃ bhrāmaṃ tiṣṭhati tatraiva kulāla-cakram iva ||GAss_318||
children.translated_text: and spinning and spinning, remains in the same place—like a potter's wheel. [GAss 318]

children.text: nirbharam api sambhuktaṃ dṛṣṭyā prātaḥ piban na tṛpyāmi |
children.translated_text: Even though fully enjoyed, drinking it in the morning with my eyes, I am not satisfied—
her hip without its cloth, like a <s>cakravāka</s> bird [gazing at] the orb of the still-warm [sun]. [GAss 319]
With thighs tightly pressed together, her fan placed against breasts raised by heavy breathing,
I remember that slender woman, her gaze tenderly angry, exhausted from lovemaking. [GAss 320]

children.text: nirguṇa iti mṛta iti ca dvāv ekārthābhidhāyinau viddhi |
children.translated_text: 'Without virtue' and 'dead'—know these two as synonymous expressions;

children.text: paśya dhanur-guṇa-śūnyaṃ nirjīvaṃ tad iha śaṃsanti ||GAss_321||
children.translated_text: look: they call a bow without a string 'lifeless.' [GAss 321]

children.text: nija-sūkṣma-sūtra-lambī vilocanaṃ taruṇa te kṣaṇaṃ haratu |
children.translated_text: O young one, let this [creature] hanging by its own fine thread captivate your eyes for a moment—

children.text: ayam udgṛhīta-vaḍiśaḥ karkaṭa iva markaṭaḥ purataḥ ||GAss_322||
children.translated_text: this spider before you, like a monkey that has seized a fish-hook! [GAss 322]

children.text: nāgara gītir ivāsau grāma-sthityāpi bhūṣitā sutanuḥ |
children.translated_text: O urbane one, that slender woman, like a song, is adorned even by her village dwelling;
musk does not become malodorous by residing in a deer's navel. [GAss 323]
With breasts marked by nails, with back [bruised by] a bed of <s>kurubaka</s> flowers, with body listlessly rolling on the ground—
like an arrow of flower-blood issuing from a torn heart, you steal my mind. [GAss 324]

children.text: nītā laghimānam iyaṃ tasyāṃ garimāṇam adhikam arpayasi |
children.translated_text: You have brought her to lightness, while you bestow upon the other greater weight;

children.text: bhāra iva viṣama-bhāryaḥ sudurvaho bhavati gṛha-vāsaḥ ||GAss_325||
children.translated_text: like a burden, a wife with an unfaithful husband finds household life most difficult to bear. [GAss 325]

children.text: na ca dūtī na ca yācñā na cāñjalir na ca kaṭākṣa-vikṣepaḥ |
children.translated_text: No messenger, no entreaty, no folded hands, no sidelong glance—
for women proud of their good fortune, O friend, seizing the hair is the first advance! [GAss 326]
At night, the married couple, impelled by the uneven flower-arrows [of <s>Kāma</s>], having attained the pleasure of love through silence—
their pride nonetheless shines on, its knot unloosened. [GAss 327]
A female serpent, having deposited her sloughed skin—placed indistinguishable from her own body with all its essence taken—abandons it;

children.text: nirmokaṃ ca bhujaṅgī muñcati puruṣaṃ ca vāra-vadhūḥ ||GAss_328||
children.translated_text: and so does a courtesan abandon a man. [GAss 328]
O slender one, you remove with difficulty your bodice, moist with sweat from the exertion of dancing—
like the vine of <s>Madana's</s> (Love-god's) bow [shedding] its bark moistened with nectar-water. [GAss 329]

children.text: nāhaṃ vadāmi sutanu tvam aśīlā vā pracaṇḍa-caritā vā |
children.translated_text: 'I do not say, O slender one, that you are unchaste or of fierce conduct;'

children.text: prema-svabhāva-sulabhaṃ bhayam udayati mama tu hṛdayasya ||GAss_330||
children.translated_text: 'but a fear easily born from the nature of love arises in my heart.' [GAss 330]
She has certainly not been appraised by you, friend, with a mere third-of-a-glance,

children.text: hārayati yena kusumaṃ vimukhe tvayi kaṇṭha iva deve ||GAss_331||
children.translated_text: for which reason a garland captivates [your] neck—as if it were a god—when you are turned away. [GAss 331]
With merciless scratching, biting, blows of fists, and embraces of the fortunate one—
while declaring his offenses, passionate women fashion reconciliation. [GAss 332]

children.text: na guṇe na lakṣaṇe'pi ca vayasi ca rūpe ca nādaro vihitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither virtue, nor auspicious marks, nor age, nor beauty has been honored—
yet to you, O fragrant one, a bell is tied as to a cow named <s>Kapilā</s>. [GAss 333]
Offense without cause, satisfaction in quarrels and anger without cause,
shared death and life, happiness and sorrow—victorious is married life! [GAss 334]

children.text: na prāpyase karābhyāṃ hṛdayān nāpaiṣi vitanuṣe bādhām |
children.translated_text: You cannot be grasped by the hands, nor do you depart from the heart; you increase the pain—
you are to me like the broken-off arrowhead of the flower-weaponed one (<s>Kāma</s>). [GAss 335]

children.text: nātheti paruṣam ucitaṃ priyeti dāsety anugraho yatra |
children.translated_text: Where 'Lord!' is the harsh [word], 'Beloved!' the servile, 'Slave!' the favor—

children.text: tad-dāmpatyam ito 'nyan nārī rajjuḥ paśuḥ puruṣaḥ ||GAss_336||
children.translated_text: that is [true] married life; otherwise, the woman is a rope and the man a beast. [GAss 336]

children.text: nihitāyām asyām api saivaikā manasi me sphurati |
children.translated_text: Even when this one is placed [before me], that same one alone flashes in my mind—
my beloved, like a line of leaf-letters [showing through] from a sheet placed beneath. [GAss 337]
As if a vine were placed above as a marker over the spot where treasure is buried,

children.text: lobhayati tava tanūdari jaghana-taṭād upari romālī ||GAss_338||
children.translated_text: the line of fine hair from the edge of your hip upward entices, O slender-waisted one. [GAss 338]
You steal from her—whose eyes are half-closed—all the way to the heart;

children.text: na subhaga samucitam īdṛśam aṅguli-dāne bhujaṃ gilasi ||GAss_339||
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, this is not fitting: when given a finger, you swallow the arm! [GAss 339]

children.text: nītvāgāraṃ rajanī-jāgaram ekaṃ ca sādaraṃ dattvā |
children.translated_text: Having taken [her] home, kept her awake one night, and given one respectful [gift],

children.text: acireṇa kair na taruṇair durgā-pattrīva muktāsi ||GAss_340||
children.translated_text: by which young men have you not soon been released, like a [used] <s>durgā</s>-leaf? [GAss 340]

children.text: nakṣatre'gnāv indāv udare kanake maṇau dṛśi samudre |
children.translated_text: In the stars, in fire, in the moon, in the belly, in gold, in gems, in the eye, in the ocean—

children.text: yat khalu tejas tad akhilam ojāyitam abja-mitrasya ||GAss_341||
children.translated_text: whatever brilliance there is, all of it is the vitality of the friend of the lotus (the Sun). [GAss 341]

children.text: na savarṇo na ca rūpaṃ na saṃskriyā kāpi naiva sā prakṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither her speech-sounds, nor her beauty, nor any refinement, nor her very nature [is the same]—
the girl, in the calamity of separation from you, is like a language that has undergone phonetic corruption. [GAss 342]

children.text: na vibhūṣaṇe tavāsthā vapur guṇenaiva jayasi sakhi yūnaḥ |
children.translated_text: Your interest is not in ornamentation; you conquer young men by your body's virtue alone, O friend—
like the wrestling art of the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>), which has cast aside weapons and arms. [GAss 343]

children.text: netrākṛṣṭo bhrāmaṃ bhrāmaṃ preyān yathā yathāsti tathā |
children.translated_text: Drawn by the eyes, spinning and spinning, my beloved just as he is—

children.text: sakhi manthayati mano mama dadhi-bhāṇḍaṃ mantha-daṇḍa iva ||GAss_344||
children.translated_text: O friend, churns my mind like a churning-stick does a pot of curd. [GAss 344]
Fashioning various colorful forms, captivating, the slender woman—
like a painter's brush, she paints you as a wall [to display her art upon]. [GAss 345]
Thus ends the section beginning with the letter 'na,' accompanied by the <s>vibhāva</s> commentary.
The section beginning with the letter 'pa.'

children.text: pathikāsaktā kiṃcin na veda ghana-kalam agopitā gopī |
children.translated_text: Attached to the traveler, the <s>gopī</s> (cowherd-woman), not at all aware of the dense darkness, unhidden—
in vain you drive away the row of parrots with your amorous playful exclamations! [GAss 346]

children.text: praṇamati paśyati cumbati saṃśliṣyati pulaka-mukulitair aṅgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: She bows, gazes, kisses, embraces with limbs covered in goosebumps —
the quivering left arm-creeper of the separated woman, eager for union with her beloved. [GAss 347]

children.text: praviśasi na ca nirgantuṃ jānāsi vyākulatvam ātanuṣe |
children.translated_text: You enter but do not know how to exit; you spread confusion —
O child, in her heart you are like <s>Abhimanyu</s> in the wheel-array of battle. [GAss 348]
See — fittingly, the crest of the mango tree is made vocal by the cuckoo;

children.text: api ca picu-manda-mukule maukuli-kulam ākulaṃ milati ||GAss_349||
children.translated_text: and moreover, the swarm of bees meets in confusion upon the bud of the neem tree. [GAss 349]
O fair-faced one, you wish in vain to take from my friend's hand the mirror that has gathered your reflected face —
why this infatuation with a play-lotus? [GAss 350]
Just as the moon from the crown of the eastern mountain settles in the middle of the sky,

children.text: tvāṃ sakhi paśyāmi tathā chāyām iva saṅkucan mānām ||GAss_351||
children.translated_text: so, O friend, I see your pride contracting like a shadow. [GAss 351]

children.text: prāṅgaṇa-koṇe'pi niśāpatiḥ sa tāpaṃ sudhāmayo harati |
children.translated_text: Even in the corner of the courtyard, that lord of night (the moon), made of nectar, removes suffering —

children.text: yadi māṃ rajani-jvara iva sakhi sa na niruṇaddhi geha-patiḥ ||GAss_352||
children.translated_text: if only, O friend, that lord of the house does not confine me like a nocturnal fever. [GAss 352]
She whose limbs are pricked by her husband's goosebumps, who is fearful even at seeing her own shadow —

children.text: abhisarati subhaga sā tvāṃ vidalantī kaṇṭakaṃ tamasi ||GAss_353||
children.translated_text: she goes to meet you, O handsome one, splitting thorns in the darkness. [GAss 353]

children.text: pratibhūḥ śuko vipakṣe daṇḍaḥ śṛṅgāra-saṅkathā guruṣu |
children.translated_text: The parrot is the surety, on the other side the punishment; erotic talk before elders;
the woman-on-top position is the wager — consider, O girl, the stakes in this game! [GAss 354]

children.text: para-mohanāya mukto niṣkaruṇe taruṇi tava kaṭākṣo 'yam |
children.translated_text: Your sidelong glance, O merciless young woman, released for the bewitching of others —

children.text: viśikha iva kalita-karṇaḥ praviśati hṛdayaṃ na niḥsarati ||GAss_355||
children.translated_text: like an arrow placed at the ear, it enters the heart but does not come out. [GAss 355]
Touching the ground on tiptoe, kissing, with eyes sweet from love and fear —
the slender one has not fallen, because her chin rests on the parapet-edge. [GAss 356]

children.text: prātar upāgatya mrṣā vadataḥ sakhi nāsya vidyate vrīḍā |
children.translated_text: Coming in the morning and speaking falsehoods, O friend, he has no shame —
he who is not embarrassed even by the burnt lampblack stuck to his face! [GAss 357]
See, O slender-waisted one! The sun, having reached <s>Phālguna</s> (spring), having conquered its foe —

children.text: vairāṭir iva pataṅgaḥ pratyānayanaṃ karoti gavām ||GAss_358||
children.translated_text: like <s>Uttara</s> son of <s>Virāṭa</s>, brings back the cows. [GAss 358]

children.text: pramada-vanaṃ tava ca stana-śailaṃ mūlaṃ gabhīra-sarasāṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Your pleasure-garden, your breast-mountains, and the depths of deep pools —
in the world, the coolness dispelled by summer takes refuge in these three strongholds. [GAss 359]

children.text: proñchati tavāparādhaṃ mānaṃ mardayati nirvṛtiṃ harati |
children.translated_text: The night, drawn out by wakefulness, O handsome one, wipes away your offense, crushes your pride, steals your pleasure,

children.text: svakṛtān nihanti śapathāñ jāgara-dīrghā niśā subhaga ||GAss_360||
children.translated_text: and kills your self-made oaths. [GAss 360]

children.text: priya āyāte dūrād abhūta iva saṅgamo 'bhavat pūrvaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the beloved returned from afar, the previous meeting seemed as if it had never been —
and again, pride, tears, conciliation, and the beginning of renewed lovemaking came close. [GAss 361]
On the peak of the eastern mountain, the darkness touched by the approaching rays of the sun
appears like the blood-smeared body of <s>Andhaka</s>, impaled on a trident. [GAss 362]
With navel displaced, the three folds of the belly vanished, the tips of the breasts dark, the eyes languid,
with many white scratch-marks on the hips — the body cannot endure the <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top position). [GAss 363]
O soft-limbed one, having already begun lovemaking, why do you carry drops of perspiration?
Like a creeper-bow of the flower-armed (<s>Kāma</s>), bent to string the bowstring, you drip honey. [GAss 364]

children.text: puṃsāṃ darśaya sundari mukhendum īṣat trpām apākṛtya |
children.translated_text: Show your moon-face to the men, O beautiful one, slightly removing the veil —

children.text: jāyājita iti rūḍhā jana-śrutir me yaśo bhavatu ||GAss_365||
children.translated_text: let the popular saying 'defeated by his wife' become my fame! [GAss 365]

children.text: prasaratu śarat-triyāmā jaganti dhavalayatu dhāma tuhināṃśoḥ |
children.translated_text: Let the autumn night spread! Let the light of the moon whiten the worlds!
For the caged <s>cakora</s> birds, even a speck makes no difference. [GAss 366]
She who came first, eager with longing, who departed long ago — regarding the fault of delay,

children.text: vakṣyanti sāṅga-rāgāḥ pathi taravas tava samādhānam ||GAss_367||
children.translated_text: the trees on the path, their limbs reddened, will speak of your acquittal. [GAss 367]
When her garment fell, her hand placed on her breast, her thighs pressed tight covering her hips —
the mind remembers her, with a hundred hissing breaths that made the lamp flicker from her tooth-marks. [GAss 368]
On the mountain, with radiant great herbs sparkling all around, as if on a bed of play —

children.text: kāñcī-guṇa iva patitaḥ sthitaika-ratnaḥ phaṇī sphurati ||GAss_369||
children.translated_text: like a girdle-string, a serpent with a single jewel lies fallen and gleams. [GAss 369]
In the rainy season, carrying the buttock of the mountain range, you wander at the horizon —

children.text: capalāntara ghana kiṃ tava vacanīyaṃ pavana-vaśyo 'si ||GAss_370||
children.translated_text: O cloud, faithless between lightning-flashes, what can be said to you who are subject to the wind? [GAss 370]
Your garment-hem, pulled excessively, diminishing in condition day by day —

children.text: nija-nāyakam atikṛpaṇaṃ kathayati kugrāma iva viralaḥ ||GAss_371||
children.translated_text: tells of its impoverished master, sparse like a poor village. [GAss 371]
O traveler, how do you endure the raincloud's water-drops — sparkling with lightning, unbearable —
like the liquid gold of <s>Mayapura</s>, infused by <s>Śiva</s>'s fire-arrows? [GAss 372]

children.text: pathikaṃ śrameṇa suptaṃ dara-taralā taruṇi sumadhura-cchāyā |
children.translated_text: O young woman, with your slightly trembling, very sweet shade and your hanging braid —
you delight the traveler asleep with fatigue, like a branch with its climber. [GAss 373]
She whose hips and thighs are plump and high, who does not grant entry even to others —

children.text: yā lupta-kīla-bhāvaṃ yātā hṛdi bahir adṛśyāsi ||GAss_374||
children.translated_text: who has transcended the state of a threshold, dwelling in the heart, invisible outside. [GAss 374]

children.text: prātar nidrāti yathā yathātmajā lulita-niḥsahair aṅgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The more the daughter sleeps in the morning with languid, helpless limbs,

children.text: jāmātari mudita-manās tathā tathā sādarā śvaśrūḥ ||GAss_375||
children.translated_text: the more the mother-in-law, with delighted mind, becomes attentive toward the son-in-law. [GAss 375]
Though moved by love, through my feigned-anger sidelong glances I planted a pillar of resistance —
trembling with fear, I was seized, and with laughing impetuosity, my beloved embraced my neck. [GAss 376]

children.text: priya-durnayena hṛdaya sphuṭasi yadi sphuṭanam api tava ślāghyam |
children.translated_text: O heart, if you break due to the beloved's misconduct, even your breaking is praiseworthy —
like the garment-hem that was made into a bed for the battle of love's sport. [GAss 377]
The bee, greedy for the lotus-pond far away, drawn by the fragrance carried by the wind —
not having examined its own wings, will go and come to grief. [GAss 378]
The naive bride, her breast-pitchers ample with goosebumps, the chest-burden of <s>Keśava</s> (Kṛṣṇa) made light by love —
quietly laughs at the weight of <s>Govardhana</s> mountain. [GAss 379]
The doe-eyed women, helpless in the absence of their beloved, are protected even by rival wives —
natural enemies though they be — who fear the collapse of the household. [GAss 380]

children.text: prakaṭayasi rāgam adhikaṃ lapanam idaṃ vakrimāṇam āvahati |
children.translated_text: You display excessive passion; this prattle brings a curve of suspicion —

children.text: prīṇayati ca pratipadaṃ dūti śukasyeva dayitasya ||GAss_381||
children.translated_text: yet it pleases at every step, O messenger, like the speech of the beloved's parrot. [GAss 381]
For the young girl entering the heart of her beloved, pervaded by powerful youth —
the path is blazed by the newly sharpened, slightly wavering sword made of her eyes. [GAss 382]
By the arts of affection, offense, anger, conciliation, trust, and playful skill —
is one of established love to be drawn by the mere curiosity of a young girl? [GAss 383]

children.text: pūrvair eva caritair jarato 'pi pūjyatā bhavataḥ |
children.translated_text: Your respectability even in old age comes from former deeds alone —

children.text: muñca madam asya gandhād yuvabhir gaja gaūjanīyo 'si ||GAss_384||
children.translated_text: give up your arrogance! O elephant, you are honored by the young merely for your scent. [GAss 384]

children.text: prathamaṃ praveśitā yā vāsāgāraṃ kathañcana sakhībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: She who was somehow first ushered by her friends into the love-chamber —

children.text: na śṛṇotīva prātaḥ sā nirgamanasya saṅketam ||GAss_385||
children.translated_text: does not seem to hear the signal for departure in the morning. [GAss 385]

children.text: pūjā vinā pratiṣṭhāṃ nāsti na mantraṃ vinā pratiṣṭhā ca |
children.translated_text: Without consecration there is no worship, and without mantras there is no consecration —
baffled by both, behold the stone of the gods! [GAss 386]
The wife shows more honor, love, banter, and trust than before;

children.text: bhīr adhikeyaṃ kathayati rāgaṃ bālā-vibhaktam iva ||GAss_387||
children.translated_text: yet this increased timidity speaks of her passion, as if distributed to a young girl. [GAss 387]
Knowing the sensation of embracing the pitcher-like breasts, hard and plump with goosebumps —
<s>Śambhu</s>'s (Śiva's) serpent-sacred-thread desires to seize the pride of the Goddess. [GAss 388]

children.text: priya āyāto dūrād iti yā prītir babhūva gehinyāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The beloved has returned from afar!' — such was the joy of the housewife;

children.text: pathikebhyaḥ pūrvāgata iti garvāt sāpi śata-śikharā ||GAss_389||
children.translated_text: and from pride at having arrived before the other travelers, that joy was multiplied a hundredfold. [GAss 389]

children.text: pṛṣṭhaṃ prayaccha mā spṛśa dūrād apasarpa vihita-vaimukhya |
children.translated_text: 'Give your back! Don't touch! Move away!' — having shown this aversion —

children.text: tvām anudhāvati taraṇis tad api guṇākarṣa-taraleyam ||GAss_390||
children.translated_text: the sun pursues you, yet this woman is restless with the pull of virtue. [GAss 390]
The garment sent by my beloved, marked with the imprints of both her saffron-smeared palms —
teaches me to make a thousand supplicating <s>añjalis</s> (joined palms). [GAss 391]
Separated by the parapet, she offers her lip to the face of her beloved —
like the night, hidden behind the eastern mountain, offers the twilight-glow to the day. [GAss 392]
Dried up by the merciless adulteress of another's husband, O rogue — you cannot lead me with anger!
Burnt by ruined affection, I weep at seeing your emaciation. [GAss 393]

children.text: prāṅgaṇa eva kadā māṃ śliṣyantī many-kampi-kuca-kalaśā |
children.translated_text: When in the very courtyard will she embrace me, her breast-pitchers trembling with pride-and-love,

children.text: aṃsa-niṣaṇṇa-mukhī sā snapayati bāṣpeṇa mama pṛṣṭham ||GAss_394||
children.translated_text: her face resting on my shoulder, bathing my back with tears? [GAss 394]

children.text: pretaiḥ praśasta-sattvā sāśru vṛkair vīkṣitā skhalad-grāsaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Praised for her goodness by the ghosts, gazed upon with tears by wolves whose morsels have slipped —
the young wife kisses the face of the dead man, lit by the torch-mouths of spirits. [GAss 395]

children.text: piśunaḥ khalu sujanānāṃ khalam eva puro vidhāya jetavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: A slanderer among the virtuous should indeed be conquered by placing a villain before him —

children.text: kṛtvā jvaram ātmīyaṃ jigāya bāṇaṃ raṇe viṣṇuḥ ||GAss_396||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> conquered <s>Bāṇa</s> in battle by deploying his own Fever. [GAss 396]

children.text: piba madhupa bakula-kalikāṃ dūre rasanāgra-mātram ādhāya |
children.translated_text: Drink the <s>bakula</s> bud, O bee! Place merely the tip of your tongue from afar —
when the honey of the lip-ointment is exhausted, you offer your mouth in vain. [GAss 397]

children.text: prāyeṇaiva hi malinā malinānām āśrayatvam upayānti |
children.translated_text: Generally, the impure indeed take refuge among the impure —
the splitting of the fold of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) becomes the splitting of <s>Kāliya</s>'s hood. [GAss 398]
See! <s>Umā</s>, fearing separation from her beloved's body, clinging to the body of <s>Śiva</s> the crescent-crowned,
O fortunate one whose sole deity he is — bears the <s>Gaṅgā</s> on her head. [GAss 399]
In the lands watered by the river of tears from travelers' wives' eyes —
the rainbow of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> (Indra) appears like a bracelet of wealth fashioned by fate. [GAss 400]
Though the husband returned from afar with difficulty, among neighbors, friends, and kinsmen —
the housewife, exceedingly fond of sport, hid him for one day. [GAss 401]

children.text: para-paṭa iva rajakībhir malino bhuktvāpi nirdayaṃ tābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Like another's cloth by washerwomen — soiled and consumed without mercy by them —
O wretch, you have been released by the harlots without receiving any payment! [GAss 402]
Thus ends the pa-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ba-kāra-vrajyā
When the friend laughed at the beloved, his head red with lac, in the company of many women —
the shame acquired at that moment broadcasts her good fortune among her friends. [GAss 403]
The heart of her hair-braid, released from its bonds and now free —
under the pretext of the sindūra-smeared parting, seems to be split open. [GAss 404]

children.text: balam api vasati mayīti śreṣṭhini guru-garva-gadgadaṃ vadati |
children.translated_text: 'Strength also resides in me!' — the prominent man speaks, stammering with heavy swollen pride;
his wife, with concealed smile, looked at the faces of the people. [GAss 405]
The bee, drawn by the fragrance of fresh lotuses broken open and carried by a strong wind from distant waters —
is pulled by the lotus-pond like one by a hook-and-line cast into the nose. [GAss 406]

children.text: bāṇaṃ harir iva kurute sujano bahudoṣam apy adoṣam iva |
children.translated_text: A noble person, like <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) [treating] <s>Bāṇa</s>, treats even the very faulty as if faultless —

children.text: yāvad doṣaṃ jāgrati malimlucā iva punaḥ piśunāḥ ||GAss_407||
children.translated_text: while slanderers, like demons, keep awake only as long as there are faults. [GAss 407]

children.text: bauddhasyeva kṣaṇiko yadyapi bahu-vallabhasya tava bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Though your love, O man of many lovers, is momentary like a Buddhist's [view of things] —

children.text: bhagnā bhagnā bhrūr iva na tu tasyā vighaṭate maitrī ||GAss_408||
children.translated_text: broken and broken again, like a brow, her friendship does not break apart. [GAss 408]

children.text: bāṣpākulaṃ pralapator gṛhiṇi nivartasva kānta gaccheti |
children.translated_text: 'Turn back, O husband!' 'Go on, O beloved!' — speaking thus, choked with tears —
the day passed for the couple at the lake-shore, up to the limit of following. [GAss 409]
Unable in my mind, pondering first the bonds of the young girl's coquetry —
I now grieve only for that wife, deprived of respect. [GAss 410]
Thus ends the ba-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The bha-kāra-vrajyā

children.text: bhramasi prakaṭayasi radaṃ karaṃ prasārayasi tṛṇam api śrayasi |
children.translated_text: You wander, you show your tusk, you stretch out your trunk, you grasp even a straw —

children.text: dhiṅ mānaṃ tava kuñjara jīvaṃ na juhoṣi jaṭharāgnau ||GAss_411||
children.translated_text: shame on your pride, O elephant! You do not sacrifice your life in the fire of your belly! [GAss 411]

children.text: bhūtimayaṃ kurute'gnis tṛṇam api saṃlagnam enam api bhajataḥ |
children.translated_text: Fire makes even a straw glorious when it touches it; even to one who serves it —

children.text: saiva suvarṇa daśā te śaṅke garimoparodhena ||GAss_412||
children.translated_text: that same, O gold, is your condition—I suspect, due to the obstruction of heaviness. [GAss 412]

children.text: bhavati nidāghe dīrghe yatheha yamuneva yāminī tanvī |
children.translated_text: As in the long summer here the night becomes slender like the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: dvīpā iva divasā api tathā krameṇa prathīyāṃsaḥ ||GAss_413||
children.translated_text: so too the days, like islands, gradually become broader. [GAss 413]
O traveler, placed by you in the great fire of love, like a pellet of gold,

children.text: tanvī hastenāpi spraṣṭum aśuddhair na sā śakyā ||GAss_414||
children.translated_text: the slender woman cannot be touched even by the hand when it is impure. [GAss 414]
With one earring lying on the ground, a strip of cloth tucked behind the ear, this naive girl—
gazing [at her beloved], she scatters with her sighs even a cloud of <s>Mano</s>-pollen (Love-god's). [GAss 415]

children.text: bhavatāliṅgi bhujaṅgī jātaḥ kila bhogi-cakravartī tvam |
children.translated_text: 'A serpent-woman was embraced by you'—indeed you have become an emperor of serpent-wealth, O [bodice]!

children.text: kañcuka vanecarī-stanam abhilaṣataḥ sphurati laghimā te ||GAss_416||
children.translated_text: O bodice, your lightness becomes apparent when you desire the breast of a forest-dwelling woman. [GAss 416]
'One who eats alms, a village-chief!'—so is he praised by the good-looking wife of that man;

children.text: rakṣaka jayasi yad ekaḥ śūnye sura-sadasi sukham asmi ||GAss_417||
children.translated_text: 'O guard, you are victorious in that you are alone! In the empty assembly of the gods, I am happy.' [GAss 417]
Of an old man—incapable of enjoyment, guarding merely with a glance, not facing [her]—

children.text: vṛddhasya pramadāpi śrīr api bhṛtyasya bhogāya ||GAss_418||
children.translated_text: even his wife, even his wealth, exists for the enjoyment of a servant. [GAss 418]

children.text: bhavitāsi rajani yasyām adhva-śrama-śāntaye padaṃ dadhatīm |
children.translated_text: 'You shall be, O night, in which, as she places her foot to relieve the fatigue of travel,

children.text: sa balād valayita-jaṅghā-baddhāṃ mām urasi pātayati ||GAss_419||
children.translated_text: he forcibly pulls me, with legs bent and clasped, down onto his chest.' [GAss 419]
For gold that has attained the state of ornament, purified by rubbing, O friend—

children.text: puruṣasya ca kanakasya ca yukto garimā sarāgasya ||GAss_420||
children.translated_text: the weight of a man and of gold, when passionate, is fitting. [GAss 420]

children.text: bhasma-puruṣe'pi giriśe snehamayī tvam ucitena subhagāsi |
children.translated_text: Even though <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) is an ash-covered man, you, being full of love, are beautiful with him fittingly;
vain is the public gossip about you—that you are the daughter of the herb-plateau (<s>Oṣadhiprastha</s>, i.e., <s>Himālaya</s>). [GAss 421]
The plump pair of thighs of the girl, closed with fear—<s>Smara</s> (the Love-god), fully awakened,
gazes upon them in her sleep, tender with love, sighing again and again. [GAss 422]

children.text: bhramarīva koṣa-garbhe gandha-hṛtā kusumam anusarantī tvām |
children.translated_text: Like a female bee drawn by fragrance, following a flower inside a cocoon—pursuing you,

children.text: avyaktaṃ kūjantī saṅketaṃ tamasi sā bhramati ||GAss_423||
children.translated_text: humming indistinctly, she wanders to the rendezvous in the darkness. [GAss 423]

children.text: bhrāmaṃ bhrāmaṃ sthitayā snehe tava payasi tatra tatraiva |
children.translated_text: Having stood spinning and spinning in your affection, like water, here and there—
she has been made, her modesty swept away, like a boat fallen into a whirlpool by this one. [GAss 424]
O daughter of the farmer, you who are full of virtues, at the edge of your own house, you spin around
young bulls fit for the neck-yoke—like a tethering-rope around a post. [GAss 425]
Fire in the eye on the forehead, the moon on the crown, on the body serpent-jewel lamps—

children.text: tad api tamo-maya eva tvam īśa kaḥ prakṛtim atiśete ||GAss_426||
children.translated_text: yet even so, you are indeed made of darkness, O Lord (<s>Īśa</s>, <s>Śiva</s>)! Who surpasses [their own] nature? [GAss 426]
Thus ends the section beginning with the letter 'bha,' accompanied by the <s>vibhāva</s> commentary.
The section beginning with the letter 'ma.'

children.text: madhu-mada-vīta-vrīḍā yathā yathā lapati saṃmukhaṃ bālā |
children.translated_text: As the girl, her modesty dissolved by the intoxication of spring wine, prattles face to face—

children.text: tan-mukham ajāta-tṛptis tathā tathā vallabhaḥ pibati ||GAss_427||
children.translated_text: so her beloved, never sated, drinks her face in equal measure. [GAss 427]

children.text: mitrair ālocya samaṃ guru kṛtvā kadanam api samārabdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having consulted with friends, having treated the matter gravely, though a campaign has been launched—

children.text: arthaḥ satām iva hato mukha-vailakṣyeṇa māno 'yam ||GAss_428||
children.translated_text: this pride, like the fortune of the virtuous, is destroyed by the embarrassment of the face. [GAss 428]

children.text: mama rāgiṇo manasvini karam arpayato dadāsi pṛṣṭham api |
children.translated_text: O proud one, even when I, who am passionate, extend my hand, you give me your back;

children.text: yadi tad api kamala-bandhor iva manye svasya saubhāgyam ||GAss_429||
children.translated_text: even so, like [the turning of] the friend of the lotus (the Sun), I consider it my own good fortune. [GAss 429]

children.text: mā spṛśa mām iti sakupitam iva bhaṇitaṃ vyañjitā na ca vrīḍā |
children.translated_text: 'Don't touch me!'—spoken as if angrily, yet no modesty was revealed;
when embraced, she said with a smile: 'O shameless one, what are you doing?' [GAss 430]

children.text: mūlāni ca niculānāṃ hṛdayāni ca kūla-vasati-kulaṭānām |
children.translated_text: The roots of the <s>nīpa</s> trees and the hearts of wanton women dwelling on the river-banks—
O <s>Godāvarī</s>, intoxicated by cloud-wine, why do you tear them apart? [GAss 431]
Like the excellence of virtues of <s>Malaya</s> (sandal) trees, even the pre-eminence of the steadfast—
when fallen in dull times—serves only for disregard, not for benefit. [GAss 432]

children.text: madhumathana-mauli-māle sakhi tulayasi tulasi kiṃ mudhā rādhām |
children.translated_text: O friend, O <s>Tulasī</s> (holy basil), garland upon the crown of <s>Madhumathana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), why do you vainly compare yourself with <s>Rādhā</s>?

children.text: yat tava padam adasīyaṃ surabhayituṃ saurabhodbhedaḥ ||GAss_433||
children.translated_text: Your fragrance-burst was given to the place beneath [his feet] to perfume it. [GAss 433]
When I was about to depart, having counted the days of the appointed term, a kiss and then an embrace—
that night, lamented by my beloved, was so long it could not endure lovemaking. [GAss 434]

children.text: mṛgamada-nidānam aṭavī kuṅkumam api kṛṣaka-vāṭikā vahati |
children.translated_text: The forest bears musk-deer, and even the farmer's garden bears saffron;
O charming market-woman, you alone are the entire wealth of the townspeople. [GAss 435]

children.text: madhu-divaseṣu bhrāmyan yathā viśati mānasaṃ bhramaraḥ |
children.translated_text: As a bee, wandering in the days of spring, enters the <s>Mānasa</s> (lake of the mind)—
so too, O friend, does <s>Madana's</s> (Love-god's) arrow, sharp as an iron thorn. [GAss 436]

children.text: mayi calite tava muktā dṛśaḥ svabhāvāt priye sa-pānīyāḥ |
children.translated_text: When I depart, O beloved, your glances, released by nature, are moist with tears;

children.text: satyam amūlyāḥ sadyaḥ prayānti mama hṛdaya-hāratvam ||GAss_437||
children.translated_text: truly priceless, they instantly attain the power of stealing my heart. [GAss 437]

children.text: mugdhe mama manasi śarāḥ smarasya pañcāpi santataṃ lagnāḥ |
children.translated_text: O naive one, in my mind all five arrows of <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god) are constantly lodged;

children.text: śaṅke stana-guṭikā-dvayam arpitam etena tava hṛdaye ||GAss_438||
children.translated_text: I suspect that he has placed two bullet-like [arrows as] your breasts in your heart. [GAss 438]
The <s>rāgas</s> (melodies/passions) following the holes of the flute placed at the mouth of <s>Madhumathana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)—

children.text: hanta haranti mano mama nalikā-viśikhāḥ smarasyeva ||GAss_439||
children.translated_text: alas, they steal my mind, like arrows of <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god) shot through a pipe. [GAss 439]
O friend, of two great ones, well-rounded, fit for capturing the heart, lofty—

children.text: sajjanayoḥ stanayor iva nirantaraṃ saṅgataṃ bhavati ||GAss_440||
children.translated_text: of two good persons, as of two breasts, the union is constant. [GAss 440]

children.text: mama vāritasya bahubhir bhūyo bhūyaḥ svayaṃ ca bhāvayataḥ |
children.translated_text: Though restrained by many, and though I myself deliberate again and again,

children.text: jāto diśīva tasyāṃ sakhe na vinivartate mohaḥ ||GAss_441||
children.translated_text: my delusion, O friend, once born in that direction, does not turn back. [GAss 441]
You are drowned in the current of the <s>Narmadā</s>, carried away by the casting of wave-glances;

children.text: yady ucyase taruvara bhraṣṭo bhraṃśo 'pi te ślāghyaḥ ||GAss_442||
children.translated_text: if it is said of you, O best of trees, that you have fallen—even your fall is praiseworthy. [GAss 442]

children.text: menām ullāsayati smerayati hariṃ giriṃ ca vimukhayati |
children.translated_text: [The trembling hand of <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)] delights <s>Menā</s>, makes <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) smile, and makes the mountain (<s>Himālaya</s>) turn away—
the trembling of <s>Giriśa's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) hand at the wedding, delayed by making the hand-binding. [GAss 443]
When shall I drink, having pushed aside [the veil from], that face—the <s>tilaka</s> mark melting with honey-fragrant perspiration, words faltering, eyes rolling fiercely—
the nectar of her lips? [GAss 444]

children.text: medinyāṃ tava nipatati na padaṃ bahu-vallabheti garveṇa |
children.translated_text: 'Your foot does not touch the earth, out of the pride of having many lovers!'

children.text: āśliṣya kair na taruṇais turīva vasanair vimuktāsi ||GAss_445||
children.translated_text: 'Embraced by what young men have you not been released, like a garment?' [GAss 445]

children.text: mūle nisarga-madhuraṃ samarpayanto rasaṃ puro virasāḥ |
children.translated_text: Offering sweetness natural at the root, but tasteless at the tip—

children.text: ikṣava iva para-puruṣā vividheṣu raseṣu vinidheyāḥ ||GAss_446||
children.translated_text: other men, like sugarcane, should be experienced in their various flavors [accordingly]. [GAss 446]

children.text: mahati snehe nihitaḥ kusumaṃ bahu dattam arcito bahuśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Though great affection was invested, many flowers given, and he was worshipped many times,

children.text: vakras tad api śanaiścara iva sakhi duṣṭa-graho dayitaḥ ||GAss_447||
children.translated_text: even so, O friend, the beloved is crooked like <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn)—an evil planet. [GAss 447]

children.text: mā śabara-taruṇi pīvara-vakṣoruhayor bhareṇa bhaja garvam |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śabara</s> maiden, do not be proud of the weight of your ample breasts,

children.text: nirmokair api śobhā yayor bhujaṅgībhir unmuktaiḥ ||GAss_448||
children.translated_text: for even their sloughed skins look beautiful—those released by serpent-women! [GAss 448]

children.text: mama kupitāyāś chāyāṃ bhūmāv āliṅgya sakhi milat-pulakaḥ |
children.translated_text: O friend, embracing my shadow on the ground when I am angry, his hair standing on end—

children.text: snehamayatvam anujjhan karoti kiṃ naiṣa mām aruṣam ||GAss_449||
children.translated_text: not abandoning his loving nature, does he not make me not angry? [GAss 449]

children.text: muṣita iva kṣaṇa-virahe ripur iva kusumeṣu-keli-saṅgrāme |
children.translated_text: Like one robbed in a moment's separation, like an enemy in the battle of love-play with the Flower-bannered one (<s>Kāma</s>),

children.text: dāsa iva śrama-samaye bhajan natāṅgīṃ na tṛpyāmi ||GAss_450||
children.translated_text: like a servant at the time of exertion—adoring her whose body bows, I am never satisfied. [GAss 450]
'Why do you release the proud woman from your resolve? Her fury of anger will double!'

children.text: sneha-bhavaḥ payasāgniḥ sāntvena ca roṣa unmiṣati ||GAss_451||
children.translated_text: 'The fire born of love in water—by soothing, anger blazes forth.' [GAss 451]

children.text: malayajam apasārya ghanaṃ vījana-vighnaṃ vidhāya bāhubhyām |
children.translated_text: Pushing aside the sandalwood paste, obstructing the fanning with their arms,
the couple, disregarding the summer heat because of the burning of love, embraces. [GAss 452]

children.text: mahato 'pi hi viśvāsān mahāśayā dadhati nālpam api laghavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Great ones, indeed, from great trust harbor [secrets]; small ones [harbor] not even a little;
the ocean, churned by mountains, conceals [all]; summer rivers do not conceal even a frog. [GAss 453]

children.text: madhu-dhāreva na muñcasi mānini rūkṣāpi mādhurīṃ sahajām |
children.translated_text: O proud one, even when harsh, you do not relinquish your innate sweetness, like a stream of honey;

children.text: kṛta-mukha-bhaṅgāpi rasaṃ dadāsi mama sarid ivāmbhodheḥ ||GAss_454||
children.translated_text: even with your face contorted, you give delight to me—like a river to the ocean. [GAss 454]
O wife, by the strokes of <s>Madana's</s> (Love-god's) bowstring, as it were—by the twanging of <s>vīṇā</s> strings
of young traveling men—whose heart does not tremble? [GAss 455]

children.text: mama bhayam asyāḥ kopo nirvedo 'syā mamāpi mandākṣam |
children.translated_text: My fear, her anger; her weariness, my too-dim glance—
when did the interval arise between the two, with heads bowed concealing their smiles? [GAss 456]

children.text: muktāmbaraiva dhāvatu nipatatu sahasā trimārgagā vāstu |
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Gaṅgā</s> run cloth-free, let her fall headlong, let the triple-pathed one be—
this <s>Narmadā</s> alone is suited to me, her flavor appropriate to my lineage. [GAss 457]

children.text: mṛgamada-lepanam enaṃ nīla-nicolaiva niśi niṣeva tvam |
children.translated_text: O friend, wear this musk-paste at night like a dark <s>nīpa</s>-garland—
like a beautiful <s>Indindira</s> (firefly/wasp) woman [wearing] a blue lotus on the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>). [GAss 458]

children.text: mama sakhyā nayana-pathe militaḥ śakto na kaścid api calitum |
children.translated_text: Once met in the path of my friend's eyes, no one is able to move;
O traveler, you have fallen into a difficult spot—this is the toll-house of the Flower-bannered one (<s>Kāma</s>). [GAss 459]

children.text: mahatā priyeṇa nirmitam apriyam api subhaga sahyatāṃ yāti |
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, even what is unpleasant, when fashioned by a great beloved, becomes bearable;
the destruction of youth through the birth of a son is not, indeed, a cause for grief. [GAss 460]

children.text: māna-graha-guru-kopād anu dayitāty eva rocate mahyam |
children.translated_text: After the heavy anger of her pride-born sulk, the beloved pleases me all the more—
like golden jewelry whose pure essence is revealed through firing. [GAss 461]
Thus ends the section beginning with the letter 'ma,' accompanied by the <s>vibhāva</s> commentary.
The section beginning with the letter 'ya.'
Abandoning the thorn-bushes that clutch at her garment-hem, she, the young man's [beloved],

children.text: vana iva pure'pi vicarati puruṣaṃ tvām eva jānantī ||GAss_462||
children.translated_text: wanders in the city as in a forest, knowing only you, her man. [GAss 462]
'We have approached you, O learned ones, merely through skill in words;'

children.text: antarbhavati bhavatsv api nābhaktas tan na vijñātam ||GAss_463||
children.translated_text: 'even among you there is inner insincerity—but that has not been perceived.' [GAss 463]

children.text: yatra na dūtī yatra snigdhā na dṛśo 'pi nipuṇayā nihitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where there is no messenger, where even the glances of the affectionate one are not skillfully placed,
where no words [are exchanged]—even now, that feeling has been made manifest by love alone. [GAss 464]

children.text: yā nīyate sapatny praviśya yāvarjitā bhujaṅgena |
children.translated_text: She who is led away by the co-wife, entering [the household], won over by the serpent [of a husband]—

children.text: yamunāyā iva tasyāḥ sakhi malinaṃ jīvanaṃ manye ||GAss_465||
children.translated_text: like the <s>Yamunā's</s>, O friend, I consider her life to be polluted. [GAss 465]

children.text: yasminn ayaśo 'pi yaśo hrīr vighno māna eva dauḥśīlyam |
children.translated_text: In whom even infamy is fame, modesty is an obstacle, pride itself is misconduct,

children.text: laghutā guṇajñatā kiṃ navo yuvā sakhi na te dṛṣṭaḥ ||GAss_466||
children.translated_text: lightness is knowledge of virtue—O friend, have you not seen the new young man? [GAss 466]

children.text: yad vīkṣyate khalānāṃ māhātmyaṃ kvāpi daiva-yogena |
children.translated_text: Whatever greatness of villains is seen anywhere by a stroke of fate—

children.text: kākānām iva śauklyaṃ tad api hi na cirād anarthāya ||GAss_467||
children.translated_text: like the whiteness of crows, even that too soon leads to ruin. [GAss 467]

children.text: yat khalu khala-mukha-huta-vaha-vinihitam api śuddhim eva parameti |
children.translated_text: That which, even when cast into the fire of a villain's mouth, attains only purification—

children.text: tad anala-śaucam ivāṃśukam iha loke durlabhaṃ prema ||GAss_468||
children.translated_text: such love, like a garment purified by fire, is rare in this world. [GAss 468]

children.text: yan nāvadhim arthayate pātheyārthaṃ dadāti sarvasvam |
children.translated_text: She who sets no limit to the term [of his stay] and gives her all for provisions—
by her, a most terrible suspicion has been implanted upon that man's mind. [GAss 469]
O young woman, by your hip, lovely as a wheel, spreading the enmity of jealousy among young men—
the entire village is agitated, as if by a villain. [GAss 470]
Lifelong, of two whose minds are equal, utterly inseparable—

children.text: nadayor ivaiṣa yuvayoḥ saṅgo rasam adhikam āvahatu ||GAss_471||
children.translated_text: may this union of the two of you, like that of two rivers, bring ever greater delight. [GAss 471]

children.text: yan nihitāṃ śekharayasi mālāṃ sā yātu śaṭha bhavantam iti |
children.translated_text: 'That garland you place as a crest—let it go to you, O scoundrel!' [she said,]

children.text: praharantīṃ śirasi padā smarāmi tāṃ garva-guru-kopām ||GAss_472||
children.translated_text: striking [him] on the head with her foot—I remember her, heavy with the anger of pride. [GAss 472]

children.text: yauvana-guptiṃ patyau bandhuṣu mugdhatvam ārjavaṃ guruṣu |
children.translated_text: Displaying concealment of youth before the husband, naïveté before kinsmen, honesty before elders—
the farmer's wife is praised by young men on false pretexts. [GAss 473]

children.text: yo na gurubhir na mitrair na vivekenāpi naiva ripu-hasitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: He who was never before restrained by elders, nor by friends, nor by discrimination, nor even by the mockery of enemies—

children.text: niyamita-pūrvaḥ sundari sa vinītatvaṃ tvayā nītaḥ ||GAss_474||
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, he has been brought to a state of humility by you. [GAss 474]

children.text: yan-mūlam ārdram udakaiḥ kusumaṃ pratiparva phala-bharaḥ paritaḥ |
children.translated_text: O tree, your root is moist with waters, flowers at every joint, the weight of fruit all around—
yet you revel, without considering the consequences of the waves' approach. [GAss 475]
He, in whose lap his beloved sleeps with palms joined after the rest from the battle of love—
let him bear the pride of [possessing] virtues, like the bark of <s>Madana's</s> (Love-god's) bow-vine. [GAss 476]
If female elephants dwell even on the <s>saptacchada</s> (seven-leaved) tree, merely from the scent of rut,

children.text: kim iti mada-paṅka-malināṃ karī kapola-sthalīṃ vahati ||GAss_477||
children.translated_text: why then does the bull elephant bear a temple-surface stained with rut-ichor? [GAss 477]
From the time when the rows of hemp, their buds fully grown, their flowers in full bloom—
This daughter of the village chief has loved yellow garments ever since.

children.text: yamunā-taraṅga-taralaṃ na kuvalayaṃ kusuma-lāvi tava sulabham |
children.translated_text: O flower-gatherer, the <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) trembling on the waves of the <s>Yamunā</s> is not easily obtained by you;

children.text: yadi saurabhānusārī jhaṅkārī bhramati na bhramaraḥ ||GAss_479||
children.translated_text: If the bee, following the fragrance, does not buzz and hover [around it].
Thus ends the ya-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ra-kāra section.
In stories of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> whose crown was washed with the waters of royal consecration,
<s>Rādhā</s>, her eyes heavy-lidded with the weight of pride, gazes at his lotus feet.
A house where the husband is delighted by the hair-pulling of his lover angered in the quarrel of passion—

children.text: bhavati bhavanaṃ tad anyat prāg-vaṃśaḥ parṇa-śālā vā ||GAss_491||
children.translated_text: Any other dwelling is but a front-porch or a leaf-hut.

children.text: rogo rājāyata iti janavādaṃ satyam adya kalayāmi |
children.translated_text: 'The king has fallen ill'—I now see this popular saying is true,
O fortunate one, now that you in full health have come to the edge of my bed.

children.text: ruddha-svarasa-prasarasyālibhir agre nataṃ priyaṃ prati me |
children.translated_text: Before my friends, who block the flow of sentiment, my passion toward the beloved who bows before me

children.text: srotasa iva nimnaṃ prati rāgasya dviguṇa āvegaḥ ||GAss_493||
children.translated_text: Doubles in intensity, like a current toward a low place.

children.text: rūpam idaṃ kāntir asāv ayam utkarṣaḥ suvarṇa-racaneyam |
children.translated_text: 'This is beauty, that is radiance, this is excellence, that is golden craftsmanship'—
O graceful one, having met with misfortune, you wander before the doors of temples.
In a begging bowl made of bower-leaves, the young wife disdainfully gives
Even stale food, heated by her intensely hot sighs.

children.text: rakṣati na khalu nija-sthitim alaghuḥ sthāpayati nāyakaḥ sa yathā |
children.translated_text: The hero does not truly guard his own position, nor does he maintain it as he sets it;
Pierced by his qualities, she remains just as she is, like a necklace-string.
O slender-limbed one, you shine like a <s>maṅgala-kalaśī</s> (auspicious vessel) with a mango shoot—
Your face kissed by that same [lover] whose passion has freshly arisen.
A woman swayed by one without beauty or virtue is light, like dust tossed by a fickle wind;

children.text: prathayati pṛghu-guṇa-neyā taruṇī taraṇir iva garimāṇam ||GAss_498||
children.translated_text: But a young woman led by one of great qualities reveals weightiness, like the sun.
As fresh passion swells, and her eyes grow slow and languid from the course of separation,

children.text: sasmita-salajjam īkṣitam idam iṣṭaṃ siddham ācaṣṭe ||GAss_499||
children.translated_text: This glance, smiling and shy, proclaims that the desired [union] has been accomplished.

children.text: roṣo 'pi rasavatīnāṃ na karkaśo vā cirānubandhī vā |
children.translated_text: The anger of passionate women is neither harsh nor long-lasting;

children.text: varṣāṇām upalo 'pi hi susnigdhaḥ kṣaṇika-kalpaś ca ||GAss_500||
children.translated_text: Even the hailstone of the rains is quite soft and lasts but a moment.

children.text: rodanam etad dhanyaṃ sakhi kiṃ bahu mṛtyur api mamānarghaḥ |
children.translated_text: This weeping is blessed, O friend! Why [say] much? Even death is precious to me,
For he was created, as if in a dream, to steal both eyes and heart.

children.text: roṣeṇaiva mayā sakhi vakro 'pi granthilo 'pi kaṭhino 'pi |
children.translated_text: O friend, with my anger I shall straighten this one immediately—though crooked, knotted, and hard—

children.text: ṛjutām anīyatāyaṃ sadyaḥ svedena vaṃśa iva ||GAss_502||
children.translated_text: Like a bamboo [softened] by heat.

children.text: rajanīm iyam upanetuṃ pitṛ-prasūḥ prathamam upatasthe |
children.translated_text: This [evening twilight], born of the father [the sun], first arrived to bring forth the night;
She herself colors the moon, that poor lover, like a wicked messenger-woman.
Thus ends the ra-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The la-kāra section.

children.text: lagnāsi kṛṣṇa-vartmani susnigdhe varti hanta dagdhāsi |
children.translated_text: O wick, you have clung to a dark path [the lampblack]—smooth indeed—but alas, you are burned!

children.text: ayam akhila-nayana-subhago nu bhukta-muktāṃ punaḥ spṛśati ||GAss_504||
children.translated_text: Does this one, pleasing to all eyes, touch again one who has been enjoyed and discarded?

children.text: lakṣmīḥ śikṣayati guṇān amūn punar durgatir vidhūnayati |
children.translated_text: Prosperity teaches virtues, while misfortune shakes them off;

children.text: pūrṇo bhavati suvṛttas tuṣāra-rucir apacaye vakraḥ ||GAss_505||
children.translated_text: The moon is full and well-rounded [when waxing], but crooked in its waning.
With cut threads blocking its door, an empty dwelling, with insects falling—
O friend, [the house] weeps, as it were, with its mouth covered by a hem, for that traveler.
Clinging to her broad hips, which sport with the play of an elephant's trunk,

children.text: vapre saktaṃ dvipam iva śṛṅgāras tvāṃ vibhūṣayati ||GAss_507||
children.translated_text: Passion adorns you like an elephant stuck on a rampart.

children.text: liptaṃ na mukhaṃ nāṅgaṃ na pakṣatī na caraṇāḥ parāgeṇa |
children.translated_text: Neither face nor body smeared, nor wings, nor feet [touched] with pollen—
The clever bee has drunk the honey of the lotus as if without touching it.

children.text: lagnaṃ jaghane tasyāḥ śuṣyati nakha-lakṣma mānasaṃ ca mama |
children.translated_text: The nail-mark clinging to her hip fades, and so does my heart;
This [love] was enjoyed without clarity, without awareness—now excessively passionate and troubled.
<s>Rādhā</s>, to embarrass <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> whose heart was drunk by all the <s>gopīs</s>,
Asks, as if innocently, the story of <s>Śambhu</s> [<s>Śiva</s>] who was satisfied with half of his beloved.
The beautiful women on the shore of the Ocean of Milk, whose arms are masses of solidified fire from <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s sighs,
Sing the glories of <s>Rādhā</s>.

children.text: līlāgārasya bahiḥ sakhīṣu caraṇātithau mayi priyayā |
children.translated_text: Outside the pleasure-pavilion, among her friends, when I, a supplicant at her feet, [arrived], the beloved
Made her favor manifest by giving [me] a fan at the window.
Thus ends the la-kāra section with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The va-kāra section.

children.text: varṇa-hṛtir na lalāṭe na lulitam aṅgaṃ na cādhare daṃśaḥ |
children.translated_text: No color was stolen from her forehead, no limb was disheveled, no bite-mark on her lip,

children.text: utpalam ahāri vāri ca na spṛṣṭam upāya-catureṇa ||GAss_513||
children.translated_text: A lotus was taken and the water not even touched—by this one skilled in stratagems.
On the chest of her dearest, rough with masses of wounds from various weapons,

children.text: śrīr api vīra-vadhūr api garvotpulakā sukhaṃ svapiti ||GAss_518||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) as well as the hero's wife, their hair bristling with pride, sleeps happily.
Even when you turn away, your sighs, like arrows of an unjust warrior,

children.text: bhindanti pṛṣṭha-patitāḥ priya hṛdayaṃ mama tava śvāsāḥ ||GAss_519||
children.translated_text: Falling upon my back, pierce my heart, O beloved.

children.text: vyaktam adhunā sametaḥ khaṇḍo madirākṣi daśana-vasane te |
children.translated_text: Clearly he has just now met [you], O wine-eyed one—there is a fragment on your tooth-cloth;

children.text: yan nava-sudhaika-sāre lobhini tat kim api nādrākṣam ||GAss_520||
children.translated_text: Yet in that [mouth] whose sole essence is fresh nectar, O covetous one, I noticed nothing.
As the young couple fan each other, all their limbs are separated;

children.text: san maitrīva śroṇī paraṃ nidāghe'pi na vighaṭitā ||GAss_521||
children.translated_text: Only their hips, like true friendship, are not parted even in the heat of summer.

children.text: vyāroṣaṃ māninyās tamo divaḥ kāsaraṃ kalam abhūmeḥ |
children.translated_text: The dawn-twilight dispels, as if with anger, the darkness of the proud woman, the daylight of the buffalo, the waterlily of the earth,
And the bee trapped in the lotus.

children.text: vakṣasi vijṛmbhamāṇe stana-bhinnaṃ truṭati kañcukaṃ tasyāḥ |
children.translated_text: As her chest heaves, her bodice, split by her breasts, tears;

children.text: pūrva-dayitānurāgas tava hṛdi na manāg api truṭati ||GAss_523||
children.translated_text: But the love for your former beloved does not tear in your heart even slightly.

children.text: vyaktim avekṣya tad anyāṃ tasyām eveti viditam adhunā tu |
children.translated_text: Having observed that [your affection] manifests now in that other one—as 'it was in her alone'—I now realize:

children.text: harmya-hari-mukham iva tvām ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇaṃ vedmi ||GAss_524||
children.translated_text: I know you as common to both, like a lion-face on a palace [visible from both sides].
Like a fan, by your comings and goings you remove the heat of [my] suffering;

children.text: añcalam iva cañcalatāṃ mama sakhyāḥ prāpitaṃ cetaḥ ||GAss_525||
children.translated_text: But, like a garment-hem, you have made my friend's heart flutter.

children.text: vitarantī rasam antar mamārdra-bhāvaṃ tanoṣi tanu-gātri |
children.translated_text: O slender-bodied one, yielding nectar within, you spread my tender sentiment;

children.text: antaḥ-salilā sarid iva yan nivasasi bahir adṛśyāpi ||GAss_526||
children.translated_text: Like a river with underground water, you flow unseen yet dwell within.
A proud man, spurned by her whose pride is elevated, though he has made various entreaties—

children.text: labhate kutaḥ prabodhaṃ sa jāgaritvaiva nidrāṇaḥ ||GAss_527||
children.translated_text: From where shall he find awakening? He has fallen asleep even while staying awake.
Suspecting the beloved has turned her face away from shyness and lost affection, the young woman,
Sweet in her plaintive words, casts upon her beloved a glance that is love-moistened yet guilt-laden.
O slender one, with your breast as lover, your deep sighs as champion, your dense perspiration [as battlefield],
Your forehead resting on his forehead—stand! You are conquered.
As <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> moves about, <s>Rādhā</s>, whose eyes are restless with passion,
The crooked-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>] lets fly an arrow purified by piercing the ten directions.
When the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] turned away, and even <s>Īśa</s> [<s>Śiva</s>] took on powerlessness,
<s>Hari</s> [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], rescuing the submerged earth, was simply frozen with bristling hair.
On the bank of the pool: residence; thorny enclosures; wakeful bees;

children.text: ketaka-viṭapa kim etair nanu vāraya mañjarī-gandham ||GAss_533||
children.translated_text: O <s>ketaka</s> (pandanus) tree, with all these, why not simply stop the fragrance of your flower-clusters?
