children.text: vicalasi mugdhe vidhṛtā yathā tathā viśasi hṛdaya-madaye me |
children.translated_text: O innocent one, however you move, you enter my heart's delight;
Like the power of the flower-bowed one [<s>Kāma</s>], seeming to touch even a trembling target.
O friend, having waged war with the unmatched-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>], having surpassed <s>Gāṅgeya</s> [<s>Bhīṣma</s>] in splendor, adorned with martial display,

children.text: puruṣāyite virājati dehas tava sakhi śikhaṇḍīva ||GAss_535||
children.translated_text: Your body shines in its masculine role like <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>.
The lord of gods himself, having spurned ambrosia, craves to drink the honey
Of the woman's <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip emerging through a gap in the curtain.
In the fragranced spring, as an ornament on young women's ears and a crown-decoration for young men,
She sports among the many blossoms like a bee among forest flowers.

children.text: vrīḍā-prasaraḥ prathamaṃ tad anu ca rasa-bhāva-puṣṭa-ceṣṭeyam |
children.translated_text: First a surge of shyness, then this gesture nourished by sentiment and mood—

children.text: javanī-vinirgamād anu naṭīva dayitā mano harati ||GAss_538||
children.translated_text: Like an actress emerging from behind the curtain, the beloved steals the heart.

children.text: vāsasi haridrayeva tvayi gaurāṅgyā niveśito rāgaḥ |
children.translated_text: Like turmeric-dye on a garment, the fair-limbed woman's passion was fixed upon you;
It was removed by the informer, suddenly, like falling water.
O deer, whose musk [navel] is assailed by fragrance-blinded insects buzzing all around from the widely spreading scent—

children.text: kvacid api kuraṅga bhavato nābhīm ādāya na sthānam ||GAss_540||
children.translated_text: There is no safe place for you anywhere, even without your navel.
Banyan, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>śāla</s>, <s>śālmalī</s>, mango, many-essenced, ocean, and sandal trees—
There is a difference among them, even when they share the fragrance of <s>Malaya</s> mountain origin.
Having placed the tip of your matted locks [upon <s>Śiva</s>'s head], then abandoning <s>Śaṅkara</s> for the fault of fickleness,

children.text: vaṭam ekam anusarantī jāhnavi luṭhasi prayāga-taṭe ||GAss_542||
children.translated_text: Following a single banyan tree, O <s>Jāhnavī</s> [<s>Gaṅgā</s>], you roll on the bank at <s>Prayāga</s>.

children.text: veda caturṇāṃ kṣaṇadā praharāṇāṃ saṅgamaṃ viyogaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: The night knows the four watches—their union and separation,

children.text: caraṇānām iva kūrmī saṅkocam api prasāram api ||GAss_543||
children.translated_text: And also the contraction and expansion, like a tortoise with its limbs.

children.text: vṛti-vivareṇa viśantī subhaga tvām īkṣituṃ sakhī dṛṣṭiḥ |
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, the glance of your friend, entering through a gap in the curtain to see you,
Captivates, like <s>Kāma</s>'s arrow stationed within the cage of a young man's heart.
O one skilled in evaluation, do not weigh him on the marketplace balance of equivalence;

children.text: dharma-ghaṭo 'sāv adharīkaroti laghum upari nayati gurum ||GAss_545||
children.translated_text: That is a dharma-vessel—it brings down the light and raises up the heavy.

children.text: vāsara-gamyam anūror ambaram avanī ca vāmanaika-padam |
children.translated_text: The sky can be traversed in a day by the sun; the earth is but a single step for <s>Vāmana</s>;

children.text: jaladhir api potalaṅghyaḥ satāṃ manaḥ kena tulayāmaḥ ||GAss_546||
children.translated_text: The ocean too can be crossed by a boat—with what shall we compare the mind of the virtuous?
O doe-eyed one, the stars shine in the sky, clearly visible
In the inkline of widespread darkness, on the lap of misfortune, like clusters of leaf-letters.
The <s>guru</s> <s>Manobhava</s> [<s>Kāma</s>], heavy in various bodily gestures, [takes] the young woman as his new pupil;
Like a cane-vine, he makes her dance upon the bed in the manner of lovemaking.

children.text: viparītam api rataṃ te sroto nadyā ivānukūlam idam |
children.translated_text: Even your inverted lovemaking is like the current of a river flowing downstream—

children.text: taṭa-tarum iva mama hṛdayaṃ samūlam api vegato harati ||GAss_549||
children.translated_text: It uproots my heart completely, with its very root, like a tree on the bank [swept by] the current.

children.text: vaibhava-bhājāṃ dūṣaṇam api bhūṣaṇa-pakṣa eva nikṣiptam |
children.translated_text: Even the faults of the powerful are placed in the category of ornaments;

children.text: ugṇam ātmanām adharmaṃ dveṣaṃ ca gṛṇanti kāṇādāḥ ||GAss_550||
children.translated_text: The <s>Kāṇādas</s> [Vaiśeṣika philosophers] declare heat, self, unrighteousness, and hatred as inherent qualities.
Crooked, deceitfully smooth, stained, attaching themselves near the ear—

children.text: kaṃ vañcayanti na sakhe khalāś ca gaṇikā-kaṭākṣāś ca ||GAss_551||
children.translated_text: Whom do they not deceive, O friend—the wicked and the sidelong glances of courtesans alike?
From the pot-bellied interior of a cloud encircled by lightning-flames,
Hailstones emerge together with water, O beloved, stealing the luster of white rice.

children.text: vyajanādibhir upacāraiḥ kiṃ maru-pathikasya gṛhiṇi vihitair me |
children.translated_text: O wife, what use to me, a desert traveler, are your attentions with fans and such?
My heat finds its peace only between the two plantain-trees of your thighs.

children.text: vaiguṇye'pi hi mahatā vinirmitaṃ bhavati karma śobhāyai |
children.translated_text: Even when made with a great fault, a work of art becomes a thing of beauty;
Even the dance of a woman with hips heavy to bear captivates with its slow-hipped sway.

children.text: vīkṣya satīnāṃ gaṇane rekhām ekāṃ tayā sva-nāmāṅkām |
children.translated_text: Seeing in the tally of faithful wives a single line marked with her own name,

children.text: santu yuvāno hasituṃ svayam evāpāri nāvaritum ||GAss_555||
children.translated_text: She herself began to laugh—the young men had no power to stop her.
Your body, like the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, with hips [undulating] like the <s>Narmadā</s> with its many whirlpools,
Arrests the movement even of a sage—like one esteemed for blocking the chariot of the sun.
O fence-breaker, endurer of censure, utterly unrestrained, garden of wicked conduct,
O wicked bull, lusting after a hundred neighboring pastures—do you even remember home?

children.text: vaṃśāvalambanaṃ yad yo vistāro guṇasya yāvanatiḥ |
children.translated_text: The dependence on lineage, the breadth of the noose, the bowing of the bow—
These belong equally to a net and to a villain, for the destruction of those sleeping in their own lap.
On the peak of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, the wind [wields] a sword made of rows of rain-clouds.
the rising lightning-flash shatters, as if for the traveler's wife alone. [GAss 559]
The dust shaken from her hanging braid, first washed with tears,

children.text: āyātasya padaṃ mama gehinyā tad anu salilena ||GAss_560||
children.translated_text: then with water — the footstep of her husband who has arrived — by my housewife. [GAss 560]

children.text: vakṣaḥ-sthala-supte mama mukham upadhātuṃ na maulim ālabhase |
children.translated_text: When I sleep upon your chest, you cannot place your face upon my head —
kept at a distance by the weight of your plump, high breasts, weary from lovemaking. [GAss 561]
Concealing the true intent behind the business of your mouth, you who bring love's passion —
O messenger, you are the fang of that serpent, meant for the destruction of a chaste woman! [GAss 562]
Thus ends the va-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The śa-kāra-vrajyā

children.text: śrīr api bhujaṅga-bhoge mohana-vijñena śīlitā yena |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) too was trained upon the coils of the serpent by one skilled in the science of enchantment —

children.text: so 'pi hariḥ puruṣo yadi puruṣā itare'pi kiṃ kurmaḥ ||GAss_563||
children.translated_text: if even he, <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), is such a man, what shall we other men do? [GAss 563]

children.text: śaṅke yā sthairyamayī ślathayati bāhū manobhavasyāpi |
children.translated_text: I suspect she, who is made of steadfastness, loosens the arms of even <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāma) —

children.text: darpa-śilām iva bhavatīṃ kataras taruṇo vicālayati ||GAss_564||
children.translated_text: what young man could move you, who are like a stone of pride? [GAss 564]
O you who are fashioned harder than a tiger-claw, made of rigid gold —

children.text: bālānām api bālāsā yasyās tvam api hṛdi vasasi ||GAss_565||
children.translated_text: yet you are the hope of the young among young women — in whose heart you dwell. [GAss 565]

children.text: śruta eva śruti-hāriṇi rāgotkarṣeṇa kaṇṭham adhivasati |
children.translated_text: Merely heard, O captivator of ears, with the excess of passion, you take up residence in the throat —

children.text: gīta iva tvayi madhure karoti nārtha-grahaṃ sutanuḥ ||GAss_566||
children.translated_text: like a song; when you are sweet, O slender one, one does not grasp the meaning. [GAss 566]
<s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) obtained her kingdom through the bilva fruit, and the grass-king through slight resemblance —
but the water-pot, through perfect resemblance to the breasts, has attained universal sovereignty. [GAss 567]

children.text: śroṇī bhūmāv aṅke priyo bhayaṃ manasi pati-bhuje mauliḥ |
children.translated_text: Her hip on the ground, her beloved in her lap, fear in her mind, her head upon her husband's arm,

children.text: gūḍhaśvāso vadane suratam idaṃ cet tṛṇaṃ tridivam ||GAss_568||
children.translated_text: stifled breath at her mouth — if this lovemaking exists, then heaven is but a straw. [GAss 568]

children.text: śliṣyann iva cumbann iva paśyann iva collikhann ivātṛptaḥ |
children.translated_text: As if embracing, as if kissing, as if gazing, as if scratching — unsatisfied,

children.text: dadhad iva hṛdayasyāntaḥ smarāmi tasyā muhur jaghanam ||GAss_569||
children.translated_text: as if holding her within my heart — I remember her hips again and again. [GAss 569]

children.text: śirasi caraṇa-prahāraṃ pradāya niḥsāryatāṃ sa te tad api |
children.translated_text: Having struck his head with a kick of your foot, let him be cast out — yet even so,

children.text: cakrāṅkito bhujaṅgaḥ kāliya iva sumukhi kālindyāḥ ||GAss_570||
children.translated_text: that serpent, marked with the discus, is like <s>Kāliya</s> in the <s>Kālindī</s>, O fair-faced one! [GAss 570]

children.text: śocyaiva sā kṛśāṅgī bhūtimayī bhavatu guṇamayī vāpi |
children.translated_text: That slender woman is pitiable indeed — whether she be glorious or full of virtues —

children.text: snehaika-vaśya bhavatā tyaktā dīpena vartir iva ||GAss_571||
children.translated_text: abandoned by you, who are governed by affection alone, like a wick by a lamp. [GAss 571]
Like a parrot in a cage of wooden sticks, growing day by day,
grief, with its face sharp as <s>Smara</s>'s (Kāma's) arrow, gnaws at the beloved's heart. [GAss 572]
Hearing of the sudden death of the parrot's son, the sole treasure of all delights —
the traveler, upon arriving, understood the expenditure of the housewife's good conduct. [GAss 573]
Though trained upon the coils of a serpent and lifted by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with his chest —

children.text: acalaiva kīrtyate bhūḥ kim aśakyaṃ nāma vasumatyāḥ ||GAss_574||
children.translated_text: the earth is still called immovable! What indeed is impossible for the rich earth? [GAss 574]

children.text: śyāmā vilcana-harī bāleyaṃ manasi hanta sajjantī |
children.translated_text: The dark girl, captivating the eyes — alas, this young one, clinging to the mind —
like a creeper of smoke, destroys the former wife like a painting on a wall. [GAss 575]

children.text: śataśo gatir āvṛttiḥ śataśaḥ kaṇṭhāvalambanaṃ śataśaḥ |
children.translated_text: A hundred times going, a hundred times returning, a hundred times clinging to the neck,

children.text: śataśo yāmīti vacaḥ smarāmi tasyāḥ pravāsa-dine ||GAss_576||
children.translated_text: a hundred times saying 'I'm going' — I remember all this of hers on the day of departure. [GAss 576]
Asked by the cowherd women who had heard the cries of the cuckoo raised by another,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> declares what is agreeable through the murmuring of his flute, his eyes fixed on their breasts. [GAss 577]
O moon-phase, do not carry pride because 'your foot is placed on <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s (Śiva's) head' —
the fruit of this will be the wiping away by the dust of <s>Caṇḍī</s>'s (Pārvatī's) feet. [GAss 578]
On the treetop, content in a nest swaying on the wind's swing,
the bird-couple dwells — their sole shelter being destiny, heedless of danger, their play unceasing. [GAss 579]
O parrot, you <s>Nārada</s> of love's battles, whose essence is the secrets of the heart alone, O omniscient one —
mute in the presence of elders, be gracious — split open the rose-apple fruit! [GAss 580]

children.text: śirasā vahasi kapardaṃ rudra ruditvāpi rajatam arjayasi |
children.translated_text: On your head you bear matted locks, O <s>Rudra</s> (Śiva)! Even by weeping you acquire silver!

children.text: asyāpy udarasyārdhaṃ bhajatas tava vetti kas tattvam ||GAss_581||
children.translated_text: Who knows the truth of you, who share even half of your belly with another? [GAss 581]
To be heard like nectar, to be seen from afar like a crescent of the white-rayed moon —

children.text: duṣṭa-bhujaṅga-parīte tvaṃ ketaki na khalu naḥ spṛśyā ||GAss_582||
children.translated_text: but you, O <s>ketakī</s> flower, surrounded by evil thorns, are truly not to be touched by us! [GAss 582]
By you, O messenger, who brought virtues to my ear and offered flowers with a bow —
like the bow-creeper of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma), I have been brought under control. [GAss 583]
O you who are honored by <s>Śākhoṭaka</s>-born, <s>Vaikhānasa</s> (hermit), and elephant — proclaim loudly for a long time!

children.text: nādara-padam iha gaṇakāḥ pramāṇa-puruṣo bhavān ekaḥ ||GAss_584||
children.translated_text: Here the astrologers find no interest, but you alone, sir, are the authority. [GAss 584]
Of you who have gone to marry another's hand, O one whose beauty resembles a streak of moonlight —
like a sword-doll of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma), it mocks your bodily beauty. [GAss 585]

children.text: śaithilyena bhṛtā api bhartuḥ kāryaṃ tyajanti na suvṛttāḥ |
children.translated_text: Well-bred women, even when maintained loosely by their husband, do not abandon their duty —
when the arm is forcefully pulled, the bracelets jingle and slide, but do not leave. [GAss 586]
Thus ends the śa-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The ṣa-kāra-vrajyā
Having abandoned the weapon infested with six-legged insects and filled with pollen-worms —

children.text: tvāṃ muṣṭimeya-madhyām adhunā śaktiṃ smaro vahati ||GAss_587||
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) now carries you as his spear, O you whose waist fits within a fist! [GAss 587]
Thus ends the ṣa-kāra-vrajyā with <s>Vibhāva</s>'s commentary.
The sa-kāra-vrajyā
That housewife is merely the pretext for daytime duties —

children.text: dvitither divasasya parā tithir iva sevyā niśi tvam asi ||GAss_588||
children.translated_text: like a second day after the calendar date; you are the one to be served at night. [GAss 588]
The mass of perspiration drops clinging to the fresh nail-marks on your breasts —
appears like a stream of pearls entering a silk thread. [GAss 589]

children.text: saubhāgya-garvam ekā karotu yūthasya bhūṣaṇaṃ kariṇī |
children.translated_text: Let one she-elephant, the ornament of the herd, carry the pride of beauty —

children.text: atyāyām avator yā madāndhayor madhyam adhivasati ||GAss_590||
children.translated_text: she who dwells between two maddened bulls of excessive length. [GAss 590]
Inferring the pain on your head from the pain on my own feet, my jealousy humbled —

children.text: aparāddhā subhaga tvāṃ svayam aham anunetum āyātā ||GAss_591||
children.translated_text: though I am the offender, O handsome one, I have come myself to conciliate you. [GAss 591]
What use is even the wheel of the oil-maker, which presses those made of affection?

children.text: cālayati pārthivān api yaḥ sa kulālaḥ paraṃ cakrī ||GAss_592||
children.translated_text: He who shakes even kings — that potter is the true wheel-bearer! [GAss 592]

children.text: sarale na veda bhavatī bahu-bhaṅgā bahu-rasā bahu-vivartā |
children.translated_text: O guileless one, you do not know the course — full of bends, full of flavor, full of twists —
of the eyes of unchaste women, of loves, and of rivers. [GAss 593]
O friend, the shadow at midday, oppressed by the doubled rows of the sun's rays,
takes refuge all around the tree-root, as if to submerge in a pond. [GAss 594]

children.text: sakhi śṛṇu mama priyo 'yaṃ gehaṃ yenaiva vartmanāyātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Listen, O friend — my beloved, by the very path by which he came home,
now asks others who arrived with him about the cities, villages, and rivers of that region. [GAss 595]

children.text: sāyaṃ ravir analam asau madana-śaraṃ sa ca viyoginī-cetaḥ |
children.translated_text: The evening sun is like fire, that fire like <s>Madana</s>'s (Kāma's) arrow, and that arrow like the heart of a separated woman —

children.text: idam api tamaḥ-samūhaṃ so 'pi nabho nirbharaṃ viśati ||GAss_596||
children.translated_text: this one too enters the mass of darkness, and that one too fully enters the sky. [GAss 596]
With its neck-tube, resembling a conch filled at the time of love's battle, doubled and swollen —
atop the ruined palace, as if eager to conquer, the soft-voiced [pigeon] coos. [GAss 597]
With quivering lip, unceasing tears, breasts trembling from the effort to suppress sobs — this weeping,
with hands placed on the knees, face resting upon them — is of one noble in nature. [GAss 598]

children.text: svayam upanītair aśanaiḥ puṣṇantī nīḍa-nirvṛtaṃ dayitam |
children.translated_text: Nourishing her beloved with food brought by herself, content in the nest —
let the female crane, who by nature knows the essence of love, carry the pride of a fortunate wife! [GAss 599]

children.text: sva-rasena badhnatāṃ karam ādāne kaṇṭakotkarais tudatām |
children.translated_text: Of jackfruits, which bind the hand with their own juice when you take them, and prick with clusters of thorns —
even the inner flesh of those informers is not to be trusted! [GAss 600]

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ dākṣiṇyān nety upadiṣṭaṃ hareṇa taruṇīnām |
children.translated_text: Good fortune does not come from courtesy — this was taught by <s>Hari</s> (Śiva) to young women,
by placing only the left half of the goddess in the sculpture of his own body. [GAss 601]

children.text: subhaga sva-bhavana-bhittau bhavatā saṃmardya pīḍitā sutanuḥ |
children.translated_text: O handsome one, the slender woman was pressed and squeezed by you against the wall of your house —

children.text: sā pīḍayaiva jīvati dadhatī vaidyeṣu vidveṣam ||GAss_602||
children.translated_text: she lives only through that squeezing, bearing hatred toward physicians. [GAss 602]
She, that slender one, full of virtues, naturally transparent, dependent on marriage —
has been spun about by you, O knower of many spells, like a <s>Kāśmīra</s> (crystal) garland. [GAss 603]
O beautiful one, with your bashful smile, barely touched yet somewhat withdrawing —

children.text: apasarasi sundari yathā yathā tathā spṛśasi mama hṛdayam ||GAss_604||
children.translated_text: the more you withdraw, O lovely one, the more you touch my heart. [GAss 604]

children.text: sakhi sukhayaty avakāśa-prāptaḥ preyān yathā tathā na gṛhī |
children.translated_text: O friend, the lover, having found the opportunity, pleases — but not so the householder;

children.text: vātād avāritād api bhavati gavākṣānilaḥ śītaḥ ||GAss_605||
children.translated_text: even when unblocked, the breeze through a lattice-window is cooler than the open wind. [GAss 605]

children.text: satatam aruṇita-mukhe sakhi nigirantī garalam iva girāṃ gumpham |
children.translated_text: O friend, with face always reddened, swallowing what seems like a mass of poison — clusters of words —
despising medicines and spells, O she-serpent, you discolor the blood. [GAss 606]
With the naive body of a land-lotus, standing on one foot in her anxious lap,
the kingfisher at the bank of the lotus-pond reassures the fish. [GAss 607]
Having made the area around the navel excessively fair with nail-marks, baring the garment —

children.text: anayā sevita pavana tvaṃ kiṃ kṛta-malaya-bhṛgupātaḥ ||GAss_608||
children.translated_text: O wind, served by her — have you made a precipitous descent from <s>Malaya</s>? [GAss 608]

children.text: sarvāṅgam arpayantī lolā suptaṃ śrameṇa śayyāyām |
children.translated_text: Offering her entire body, restless, upon the bed where he sleeps exhausted —

children.text: alasam api bhāgyavantaṃ bhajate puruṣayiteva śrīḥ ||GAss_609||
children.translated_text: like <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) in the <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top), she attends even the lazy but fortunate man. [GAss 609]

children.text: suditaṃ tad eva yatra smāraṃ smāraṃ viyoga-duḥkhāni |
children.translated_text: That very well-spoken word, there, remembering again and again the sorrows of separation —

children.text: āliṅgati sā gāḍhaṃ punaḥ punar yāminī-prathame ||GAss_610||
children.translated_text: she embraces tightly, again and again, at the beginning of the night. [GAss 610]

children.text: sāntar-bhayaṃ bhujiṣyā yathā yathācarati samadhikāṃ sevām |
children.translated_text: As the slave-woman, with inner fear, renders ever-increasing service —
so proportionally does the housewife become suspicious, jealous, and fearful toward him. [GAss 611]

children.text: sundari darśayati yathā bhavad-vipakṣasya tat-sakhī kāntim |
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, when your rival's friend displays his beauty —

children.text: patati tathā mama dṛṣṭis tvad-eka-dāsasya sāsūyā ||GAss_612||
children.translated_text: so falls my jealous gaze, I who am your sole servant. [GAss 612]
By her lip-wounds, nail-marks, leaf-patterns, and daytime sleep — all self-evident —

children.text: subhagā subhagety anayā sakhi nikhilā mukharitā pallī ||GAss_613||
children.translated_text: the entire village, O friend, has been made to proclaim 'What a fortunate woman!' [GAss 613]

children.text: sarita iva yasya gehe śuṣyanti viśāla-gotrajā nāryaḥ |
children.translated_text: In whose house noble women of extensive lineage dry up like rivers —

children.text: kṣārāsv eva sa tṛpyati jala-nidhi-laharīṣu jalada iva ||GAss_614||
children.translated_text: he is satisfied only in the salty waves of the ocean, like a rain-cloud. [GAss 614]
O fierce one, ornament of the entire army, with heart hardened, with tusks at the peak —

children.text: giribhuva iva tava manye manaḥ śilā samabhavac caṇḍi ||GAss_615||
children.translated_text: I think your mind, O angry one, has become stone, like one born in the mountains. [GAss 615]
O friend, hard to fathom and dense, causing displeasure even to loved ones —

children.text: khala iva durlakṣyas tava vinata-mukhasyopari sthitaḥ kopaḥ ||GAss_616||
children.translated_text: like a villain, your anger, hard to detect, stands above your downcast face. [GAss 616]
Bathed in the perspiration of her garments, taking the seven steps, circling the seven rounds,
with the transformations of the fire of <s>Madana</s> (love's fire) — the beautiful bride, bashful, bows. [GAss 617]
This assembly of those of similar conduct, proceeding with flavor —
is disrupted upon the arrival of those of different conduct, like a canto of poetry. [GAss 618]

children.text: sarvāsām eva sakhe paya iva surataṃ manohāri |
children.translated_text: O friend, with all women, lovemaking is delightful, like milk;

children.text: tasyā eva punaḥ punar āvṛttau dugdham iva madhuram ||GAss_619||
children.translated_text: but with her alone, the repeated return is sweet, like churned butter. [GAss 619]

children.text: svapne'pi yāṃ na muñcasi yā te'nugrāhiṇī hṛdi-sthāpi |
children.translated_text: She whom you do not release even in dreams, who is your benefactress, who dwells in your heart —

children.text: duṣṭāṃ na buddhim iva tāṃ gūḍha-vyabhicāriṇīṃ vetsi ||GAss_620||
children.translated_text: you do not recognize her as wicked, like an evil thought, a secret adulteress. [GAss 620]

children.text: saparāvṛti carantī vāty eva tṛṇaṃ mano 'navadyāṅgi |
children.translated_text: Turning and moving about like the wind with a blade of grass, O woman of faultless limbs —

children.text: harasi kṣipasi taralayasi bhramayasi tolayasi pātayasi ||GAss_621||
children.translated_text: you carry, you toss, you agitate, you whirl, you weigh, and you topple my mind. [GAss 621]

children.text: sā bahu-lakṣaṇa-bhāvā strī-mātraṃ veti kitava tava tulyam |
children.translated_text: Whether she is rich in many qualities or merely a woman — to you, O gambler, it is the same;

children.text: koṭir varāṭikā vā dyūta-vidheḥ sarva eva paṇaḥ ||GAss_622||
children.translated_text: a million or a cowrie — in the rules of gambling, everything is a wager. [GAss 622]

children.text: sā viraha-dahana-dūnā mṛtvā mṛtvāpi jīvati varākī |
children.translated_text: She, the wretched one, tormented by the fire of separation, dies and dies yet lives again —
like a gaming piece, O gambler, favored by you, toppled by the throw of dice. [GAss 623]

children.text: sparśād eva svedaṃ janayati na ca me dadāti nidrātum |
children.translated_text: Mere touch produces sweat, and it does not let me sleep —

children.text: pirya iva jaghanāṃśukam api na nidāghaḥ kṣaṇam api kṣamate ||GAss_624||
children.translated_text: like a beloved, the summer heat cannot endure even the hip-garment for even a moment. [GAss 624]

children.text: sā bhavato bhāvanayā samaya-viruddhaṃ manobhavaṃ bālā |
children.translated_text: That young girl, through dwelling on you, harbors desire contrary to propriety —
like a new vine, O handsome one, she bears fruit by the power of her longing. [GAss 625]

children.text: spṛśati nakhair na ca vilikhati sicayaṃ gṛhṇāti na ca vimocayati |
children.translated_text: She touches with her nails but does not scratch, grasps the hair but does not release it,

children.text: na ca muñcati na ca madayati nayati niśāṃ sā na nidrāti ||GAss_626||
children.translated_text: neither lets go nor intoxicates; she passes the night but does not sleep. [GAss 626]

children.text: stana-jaghana-dvayam asyā laṅghita-madhyaḥ sakhe mama kaṭākṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: O friend, my sidelong glance at her pair of breasts and hips, crossing over the waist between—
does not leave the two banks of the swelling river, like a pilgrim-crow. [GAss 627]
With a bashful smile and faint breathing, telling me 'Don't touch me!'—

children.text: ākopam etya vātāyanaṃ pidhāya sthitaṃ priyayā ||GAss_628||
children.translated_text: the beloved, reaching [the point of] anger, stood having shut the window. [GAss 628]
With hand-seizing, with weeping, with reproaches, with nail-and-fist [blows], with competitiveness—
her lovemaking is [true] lovemaking; anything else is the <s>Prājāpatya</s> sacrifice (i.e., mere ritual). [GAss 629]

children.text: sakhi na khalu nimalānāṃ vidadhaty abhidhānam api mukhe malināḥ |
children.translated_text: O friend, the impure certainly cannot even take the name of the pure on their lips;
who has heard any other sound from cuckoos except '<s>kuhū</s>'? [GAss 630]

children.text: svalpā iti rāma-balair ye nyastā nāśaye payo-rāśeḥ |
children.translated_text: Those [stones] that were cast [into the ocean] by <s>Rāma's</s> army as insignificant for the destruction of the ocean—

children.text: te śailāḥ sthitimanto hanta laghimnaiva bahu-mānaḥ ||GAss_631||
children.translated_text: those very mountains stand firm! Alas, great honor comes precisely from lightness! [GAss 631]
That dark, slender-bodied woman has been brought to pallor by separation—
which burns with cold remedies all the more fiercely—like <s>dūrvā</s> grass by frost. [GAss 632]
O friend, well-observed, with steady hand, sprinkled by the stream-water of the beloved—she did not become so intoxicated

children.text: sotkampena mayā sakhi dṛṣṭā sā mādyati sma yathā ||GAss_633||
children.translated_text: as when seen by me with a trembling [gaze]. [GAss 633]

children.text: sakhi moghīkṛta-madane pativrate kas tavādaraṃ kurute |
children.translated_text: O friend, O faithful wife who has rendered <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god) futile—who pays you respect?

children.text: nāśrauṣīr bhagavān api sa kāma-viddho haraḥ pūjyaḥ ||GAss_634||
children.translated_text: Have you not heard? Even the holy <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), wounded by <s>Kāma</s>, is worshipped! [GAss 634]

children.text: sā mayi na dāsa-buddhir na ratir nāpi trapā na viśvāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'She has no servile attitude toward me, no passion, no bashfulness, no trust—'

children.text: hanta nirīkṣya navoḍhāṃ manye vayam apiryā jātāḥ ||GAss_635||
children.translated_text: 'Alas, seeing the new bride, I think we were born prematurely!' [GAss 635]

children.text: sucirāyāte gṛhiṇī niśi bhuktā dina-mukhe vidagdheyam |
children.translated_text: The clever wife, consumed at night when her husband returns late, at daybreak
does not display her own body—[still bearing] white nail-marks, not yet moist with saffron. [GAss 636]
O beloved, one who cherishes her breasts, hips, and thighs, who clings tightly, who has been invested with love—

children.text: priya kāla-pariṇatir iyaṃ virajyase yan nakhāṅka iva ||GAss_637||
children.translated_text: this is the work of time that you become dispassionate, like a nail-mark [fading]. [GAss 637]

children.text: sā vicchāyā niśi niśi sutanur bahu-tuhina-śītale talpe |
children.translated_text: That slender woman, shadowless, on a bed very cold with much frost, night after night—

children.text: jvalati tvadīya-virahād oṣadhir iva himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe ||GAss_638||
children.translated_text: burns with separation from you, like an herb on the back of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayan mountain). [GAss 638]

children.text: sā nīrase tava hṛdi praviśati niryāti na labhate sthairyam |
children.translated_text: She enters your flavorless heart and exits, finding no steadiness—
O handsome one, O friend, like a crescent-moon streak on the orb of the sun. [GAss 639]

children.text: sukumāratvaṃ kāntir nitānta-saraatvam āntarāś ca guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Delicacy, beauty, extreme fluidity, and inner virtues—

children.text: kiṃ nāma nendulekhe śaśa-graheṇaiva tava kathitam ||GAss_640||
children.translated_text: O crescent moon, what indeed has not been told about you by the very seizure of the hare (the moon-mark)? [GAss 640]
For those whose minds are set only on fragrance, let the sandal tree have no distinction;

children.text: dharmārthināṃ tathāpi sa mṛgyaḥ pūjārtham aśvatthaḥ ||GAss_641||
children.translated_text: even so, for those seeking <s>dharma</s>, it is the <s>aśvattha</s> (fig tree) that is to be sought for worship. [GAss 641]
As the wife massages her reclining husband and fans him—
so too the young man's reassurance [comes] from her glances placed through the lattice-openings of the house. [GAss 642]

children.text: satyaṃ svalpa-guṇeṣu stabdhā sadṛśe punar bhujaṅge sā |
children.translated_text: Truly, she is stiff before those of small virtue, but before an equal serpent,
she bows with her crest offered—O handsome one, like the bow-staff of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). [GAss 643]

children.text: sarvaṃsahāṃ mahīm iva vidhāya tāṃ bāṣpa-vāribhiḥ pūrṇām |
children.translated_text: Having made her, like the all-bearing earth, filled with tear-water,

children.text: bhavanāntara-mayam adhunā saṅkrāntas te guruḥ premā ||GAss_644||
children.translated_text: your great love has now migrated to the inner chambers. [GAss 644]

children.text: sambhavati na khalu rakṣā sarasānāṃ prakṛti-capala-caritānām |
children.translated_text: Indeed, there can be no guarding of those who are passionate and whose conduct is fickle by nature;
even upon <s>Hara's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) head, the <s>Gaṅgā</s> experiences familiarity with the serpent. [GAss 645]
Though the lotus-filaments, <s>ketaka</s>, mango, and <s>kunda</s> flowers are easily available,
the bee, blinded by desire, longs to become the bowstring on <s>Smara's</s> (Love-god's) bow. [GAss 646]

children.text: sā lajjitā sapatnī kupitā bhītaḥ priyaḥ sakhī sukhitā |
children.translated_text: The co-wife was embarrassed, the co-wife angry; the husband frightened, the friend delighted—
when the doctors diagnosed the girl's ailment as sleeplessness [i.e., love-sickness]. [GAss 647]
Under the pretext of massaging the long-absent husband, embracing limb by limb,

children.text: puṣyati ca māna-carcāṃ gṛhiṇī saphalayait cotkalikām ||GAss_648||
children.translated_text: the wife cultivates the topic of her pride while fulfilling her longing. [GAss 648]

children.text: sā sarvathaiva raktā rāgaṃ guñjeva na tu mukhe vahati |
children.translated_text: She is wholly dyed in passion, yet like a <s>guñjā</s> berry, does not carry it on her face;

children.text: vacana-paṭos tava rāgaḥ kevalam āsye śukasyeva ||GAss_649||
children.translated_text: your passion for words—its redness is merely on the mouth, like a parrot's. [GAss 649]
Fallen into her beloved's arms at evening, having spent the entire night in lovemaking,

children.text: uṣasi dadatī pradīpaṃ sakhībhir upahasyate bālā ||GAss_650||
children.translated_text: the girl, offering the lamp at dawn, is laughed at by her friends. [GAss 650]

children.text: sā tīkṣṇa-māna-dahanā mahataḥ snehasya durlabhaḥ pākaḥ |
children.translated_text: Her pride burns fiercely; the fruit of great love is hard to obtain;

children.text: tvāṃ darvīm iva dūti prayāsayann asmi viśvastaḥ ||GAss_651||
children.translated_text: I trust you, O messenger, [but I am] wearying you like a ladle [in this fire of love]. [GAss 651]
Loss of affection, desire to conquer, battle unto the expenditure of life—of elephants;

children.text: na vitanute kam anarthaṃ dantini tava yauvanodbhaṭaḥ ||GAss_652||
children.translated_text: O elephant-woman, what disaster does your rampant youth not create? [GAss 652]

children.text: sadanād apaiti dayito hasati sakhī viśati gharaṇim iva bālā |
children.translated_text: The beloved leaves the house, the friend laughs; the girl enters the wife as if [becoming her];

children.text: jvalati sapatnī kīre jalpati mugdhe prasīdati ||GAss_653||
children.translated_text: the co-wife blazes; when the parrot chatters, the naive one is pacified. [GAss 653]
Her body contracted, wrapped in double cloth, her passion flickering only in the mind—

children.text: dayitāṃ bhajāmi mugdhām iva tuhina tava prasādena ||GAss_654||
children.translated_text: I enjoy my naive beloved, O frost, by your grace. [GAss 654]

children.text: sakhi lagnaiva vasantī sadāśaye mahati rasa-maye tasya |
children.translated_text: O friend, though dwelling, ever clinging, in the great, flavored, well-disposed [ocean] of his,

children.text: bāḍava-śikheva sindhor na manāg apy ārdratāṃ bhajasi ||GAss_655||
children.translated_text: like the submarine fire in the ocean, you do not adopt even the slightest moisture. [GAss 655]
O friend, this frost-day, having concealed the joy of sunrise and other [pleasures], at its end—
torments like a barren deadline-day. [GAss 656]
In the divine temple, by two young people whose eyes and hearts are mutually attracted,
the flower raised for the worship of the god has been offered to each other. [GAss 657]
At evening, the sound of bees emerging from within the lotuses—
by the lotuses, grieving at their friend's (the sun's) departure, a cry of lament seems released. [GAss 658]
Though the occasion for great anger was created by me myself, with trembling thighs,

children.text: na sakhīnām api rudatī mamaiva vakṣaḥ-sthale patitā ||GAss_659||
children.translated_text: not [falling] to her friends though weeping, she fell on my chest alone. [GAss 659]
'O fortunate one, even this friend of yours has gone slack-armed from waving the fan;'

children.text: udvartanaṃ na sakhyāḥ samāpyate kiñcid apagaccha ||GAss_660||
children.translated_text: 'the rubbing of your friend is not yet finished—go away for a while!' [GAss 660]
Bashful at the offering of nails and teeth, angry at deep [embraces], she the recent bride—
to be won only by much entreating and seizing of feet—has been born out of anger. [GAss 661]
Well-gripped, of dark faction (feathering), light, piercing others, and exceedingly sharp—

children.text: puruṣā api viśikhā api guṇa-cyutāḥ kasya na bhayāya ||GAss_662||
children.translated_text: men and arrows alike, when fallen from virtue (or fallen from the bowstring), are a source of fear to whom not? [GAss 662]
Something that reveals the cause of intoxication through its own cheek—

children.text: dviradasya durjanasya ca madaṃ cakāraiva dānam api ||GAss_663||
children.translated_text: both the elephant's and the wicked man's <s>mada</s> (rut/pride) has indeed become <s>dāna</s> (ichor/generosity) as well. [GAss 663]

children.text: satyaṃ patir avidagdhaḥ sā tu sva-dhiyaiva nidhuvane nipuṇā |
children.translated_text: Truly the husband is not clever, but she is skilled in lovemaking by her own wit alone—

children.text: mārttikam ādhāya guruṃ dhanur adhigatam ekalavyena ||GAss_664||
children.translated_text: like <s>Ekalavya</s>, who, having placed a clay [image of the] <s>guru</s>, mastered the bow. [GAss 664]
He, proud of his good fortune, was humiliated by you and brought to disgrace;
he extends his own pallor of separation—resembling a bath in ashes. [GAss 665]

children.text: sakhi mama karañja-tailaṃ bahu-sandeśaṃ praheṣyasīty uditā |
children.translated_text: 'O friend, I shall send you much <s>karañja</s> oil and many messages'—having spoken thus,
the unfaithful woman conceals her tears occasioned by the journey to her father-in-law's house. [GAss 666]

children.text: sandarśayanti sundari kulaṭānāṃ tamasi vitatam avikalpe |
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, in the darkness spread undiscriminating, the serpents show wanton women the path—
with the wick-like bud of the crest-jewel lamp. [GAss 667]

children.text: sarvaṃ vanaṃ tṛṇālyā pihitaṃ pītāḥ sitāṃśu-ravi-tārāḥ |
children.translated_text: The entire forest is concealed by a mist of grass; the white moon, sun, and stars are swallowed;
the paths are destroyed—by the impure cloud having risen. [GAss 668]

children.text: samyag aniṣpannaḥ san yo 'rthas tvarayā svayaṃ sphuṭīkriyate |
children.translated_text: A matter that, though not properly accomplished, is hastily made manifest by oneself—

children.text: sa vyaṅga eva bhavati prathamo vinatā-tanūja iva ||GAss_669||
children.translated_text: that becomes defective indeed, like the first son of <s>Vinatā</s> (<s>Aruṇa</s>, the dawn, born premature). [GAss 669]

children.text: sajjana eva hi vidyā śobhanāyai bhavati durjane moghā |
children.translated_text: Learning serves for the adornment only of the virtuous; in the wicked, it is wasted;
no one adopts a vulture for its far-sightedness. [GAss 670]

children.text: subhagaṃ vadati janas taṃ nija-patir iti naiṣa rocate mahyam |
children.translated_text: People call him 'fortunate' as 'her own husband'—but this does not please me;
even in nectar, when offered in the guise of medicine, there arises distaste. [GAss 671]

children.text: saudha-gavākṣa-gatāpi hi dṛṣṭis taṃ sthiti-kṛta-prayatnam api |
children.translated_text: Even though she has gone to the palace window, her glance—even at him who has carefully positioned himself—
like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> slipping from the peak of the <s>Hima</s> mountain, carries away <s>Airāvata</s>. [GAss 672]

children.text: saha-gharma-cāriṇī mama paricchadaḥ sutanu neha sandehaḥ |
children.translated_text: O slender one, your accompanying me in the heat is fitting here, no doubt;
but like the shade of an umbrella on a frosty day, it does not bring comfort when clinging. [GAss 673]
O king of trees, abode of all virtues, through the dwelling of a demon [in you],
you have become [one] on earth whose fruits and flowers are not accepted by the virtuous. [GAss 674]

children.text: sundari tāṭaṅkamayaṃ cakram ivodvahati tāvake karṇe |
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, in your ear, the earring-wheel, as it were, bears—
the arrow of the sidelong glance falls, exceedingly sharp, devoted to <s>Arjuna</s> (i.e., straight/white). [GAss 675]
The abundance of fruit is self-dependent, being the sustenance of people, the shade of the tall [tree]—
for a good man, like a tree in the desert, only bare life is to be wished for. [GAss 676]
To produce burning, delusion, and trembling, and even to slay creatures—

children.text: sakhi durjanasya bhūtiḥ prasarati dūraṃ jvarasyeva ||GAss_677||
children.translated_text: O friend, the prosperity of the wicked spreads far, like that of a fever. [GAss 677]

children.text: sukhayitatarāṃ na rakṣati paricaya-leśaṃ gaṇāṅganeva śrīḥ |
children.translated_text: Wealth, like a public woman, does not remain loyal to one who has given [her] greater pleasure, not preserving even a trace of familiarity;
but <s>Sarasvatī</s> (learning), like a loyal wife, does not abandon [one] even through many births. [GAss 678]
Simply upon seeing a lotus-pond near his own house with newly-sprouted leaves,

children.text: hā gṛhiṇīti pralapaṃś cirāgataḥ sakhi patiḥ patitaḥ ||GAss_679||
children.translated_text: crying 'Alas, my wife!'—O friend, the long-absent husband has collapsed. [GAss 679]

children.text: saci caturānana-bhāvād vaimukhyaṃ kvāpi naiva darśayati |
children.translated_text: <s>Śacī</s>, because of [<s>Indra's</s>] four-faced nature, never shows aversion anywhere;

children.text: ayam eka-hṛdaya eva druhiṇa iva priyatamas tad api ||GAss_680||
children.translated_text: this one is single-hearted, like <s>Druhiṇa</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), and even so is the dearest. [GAss 680]

children.text: satyaṃ madhuro niyataṃ vakro nūnaṃ kalādharo dayitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Truly the beloved is sweet, certainly crooked, assuredly skilled in arts (<s>kalā</s>)—

children.text: sa tu veda na dvitīyām akalaṅkaḥ pratipad-indur iva ||GAss_681||
children.translated_text: but he knows no second [woman]—spotless, like the first-day moon. [GAss 681]

children.text: sva-sthānād api vicalati majjati jaladhau ca nīcam api bhajate |
children.translated_text: Even from his own place he is displaced, sinks in the ocean, and also resorts to the lowly—
the virtuous man, intent on protecting his own side, like Mount <s>Maināka</s>. [GAss 682]

children.text: saṃvṛṇu bāṣpa-jalaṃ sakhi dṛśam uparajyāñjanena valayainām |
children.translated_text: O friend, conceal the tear-water! Adorn your eyes with collyrium, encircle them with bangles—

children.text: dayitaḥ paśyatu pallava-paṅkajayor yugapad eva rucam ||GAss_683||
children.translated_text: let the beloved see the beauty of tender shoots and lotuses simultaneously. [GAss 683]

children.text: sā pāṇḍu-durbalāṅgī nayasi tvaṃ yatra yāti tatraiva |
children.translated_text: She is pale, weak-bodied—you lead her wherever she goes,
like a die under a gambler's control, to be won merely by the grasp of the hand. [GAss 684]

children.text: sakhi viśva-gañjanīyā lakṣmīr iva kamala-mukhi kadaryasya |
children.translated_text: O lotus-faced one, like <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) to be spurned by the whole world when [belonging to] a miser,
you are fit only for the guarding-glance of this aged man. [GAss 685]
Thus ends the section beginning with the letter 'sa,' accompanied by the <s>vibhāva</s> commentary.
The section beginning with the letter 'ha.'

children.text: hṛdayajñayā gavākṣe visadṛkṣaṃ kim api kūjitaṃ sakhyā |
children.translated_text: By the friend who knows her heart, some indistinct cooing [was made] at the window—

children.text: yat kalaha-bhinna-talpā bhaya-kapaṭād eti māṃ sutanu ||GAss_686||
children.translated_text: because of which the slender woman, whose bed was separated by a quarrel, comes to me through the pretense of fear. [GAss 686]

children.text: harati hṛdayaṃ śalākā-nihito 'ñjana-tantur eṣa sakhi mugdhe |
children.translated_text: O naive friend, this thread of collyrium applied by a stylus steals the heart;
it is as if scratched by a callus on the bow-brow of the one who shoots eye-arrows. [GAss 687]

children.text: hasasi caraṇa-prahāre talpād apasārito bhuvi svapiṣi |
children.translated_text: You laugh when struck by my foot, sleep on the ground when removed from the bed—

children.text: nāsadṛśe'pi kṛte priya mama hṛdayāt tvaṃ viniḥsarasi ||GAss_688||
children.translated_text: O beloved, even when treated so cruelly, you do not depart from my heart. [GAss 688]

children.text: hasati sapatnī śvaśrū roditi vadanaṃ ca pidadhate sakhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The co-wife laughs, the mother-in-law weeps, and the friends cover their faces—
when she, as if in a dream, on that [bed], O fortunate one, babbles your name. [GAss 689]
O friend, my heart, cultivated at every moment, [and] my beloved <s>aśoka</s> tree—
the mighty one will split [the heart] like a water-pot, like a line of water [splits the pot]. [GAss 690]
Alas, separation on all sides ignites [me] with irresistible fierce intensity,

children.text: aruṇas tapana-śilām iva punar na māṃ bhasmatāṃ nayati ||GAss_691||
children.translated_text: like the dawn [igniting] a sun-stone—yet it does not reduce me to ashes again. [GAss 691]

children.text: hṛtvā taṭini taraṅgair bhramitaś cakreṣu nāśaye nihitaḥ |
children.translated_text: O river, having swept [it] away with your waves, spun [it] in whirlpools, placed [it] for destruction —
stripped of fruits, leaves, and bark, the tree has been abandoned by you in mid-air.
From the hip now freed of the binding of the girdle-vine, of a woman who has been enjoyed in the other kind of pleasure —
the line of body-hair gleams forth like the streak of poison on the breast of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva).
Thus the section of verses beginning with 'ha,' together with the <s>Vibhāva</s> commentary, is concluded.
Section of verses beginning with 'kṣa.'

children.text: kṣīrasya tu dayitatvaṃ yato 'pi śāntopacāram āsādya |
children.translated_text: As for the dearness of milk [the milk-ocean] — even upon obtaining the remedy of peace [after the churning],
the mountain [<s>Mandara</s>] bends its limbs. The remnant of love is like [the remnant] of a fever.

children.text: kṣāntam apasārito yac caraṇāv upadhāya supta evāsi |
children.translated_text: 'It is forgiven; [I have been] pushed away' — yet, placing your feet [near hers], you appear to be asleep.

children.text: udghāṭayasi kim ūru niḥśvāsaiḥ pulakayann uṣṇaiḥ ||GAss_695||
children.translated_text: Why then do you cause her thighs to open with hot sighs that make [her] horripilate?

children.text: kṣudrodbhavasya kaṭutāṃ prakaṭayato yac chataś ca madam uccaiḥ |
children.translated_text: That which is born from the lowly manifests bitterness, while that [born] from a hundred [flowers manifests] intoxication loudly.

children.text: madhuno laghu-puruṣasya ca garimā laghimā ca bhedāya ||GAss_696||
children.translated_text: The weightiness and lightness of honey and of a base man serve to distinguish [them].
Let the virtuous observe — what fault is there in my worshipping <s>Vāgdevī</s> (the goddess of speech),

children.text: vāg-devīṃ bhajato mama santaḥ paśyantu ko doṣaḥ ||GAss_697||
children.translated_text: who was courted in different meters by earlier [poets]: <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>, <s>Bhavabhūti</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, and the author of the <s>Raghu</s> [<s>Kālidāsa</s>]?
A good poem — a thing novel in [presenting] a worthy reflection, fit for offering to a worthy recipient —

children.text: kasya na janayati harṣaṃ sat-kāvyaṃ madhura-vacanaṃ ca ||GAss_698||
children.translated_text: and sweet speech: in whom do they not generate delight?
One, with resonance as its companion, the essence of the three worlds, clever in clear expression,
[delighting] the five-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>], beneficial to the bee — an ornament of the ear: [such is] the Seven Hundred.
a source of delight for the learned — this composition has been created by me.
A lion's roar in the battle of poets, a resonance of melody, a conversation solely of nectar,
This Seven Hundred was illuminated, having been purified, by my pupil-brothers <s>Udayana</s> and <s>Balabhadra</s> —
like the sky by the sun and moon.
<s>Govardhanācārya</s>, the wise one, ever offering obeisance at <s>Hari</s>'s feet, for the delight of the best of poets,
has composed this <s>Āryāsaptaśatī</s>.
Thus the <s>Āryāsaptaśatī</s> composed by <s>Govardhanācārya</s> is completed.
